title: Has the Regent Regretted It Today?
author: Canned Osmanthus Sugar
synopsis: 【Proud and Seductive Broken-Winged Crane x Cold-Faced Jealous Living Yama】 Shen Lingjiang is a well-known laughingstock in the State of Chu. Despite her icy beauty and exquisite appearance, the noble youths despise her. They loathe her for her mother’s humble origins and look down upon her as a pretty vase, believing she isn't even worth a strand of hair from the Third Imperial Princess of Great Chu. During the war between the states of Liang and Chu, the Third Imperial Princess, Shangguan Ying, hid within the army to devise strategies, engaging in a back-and-forth struggle with the Regent of Liang, Xie Yunzhou. Xie Yunzhou lost a few times, held a grudge, and secretly developed feelings for her. As for the Seventh Imperial Princess, Shen Lingjiang, she was merely a useless fool. When Great Chu was defeated, Shen Lingjiang was sent to the capital of Liang as a hostage. Xie Yunzhou scoffed, believing she was relying on...

chapters.title: Entering Yan Capital
chapters.content:
Heavy snow fell in thick flakes as a carriage, surrounded by a crowd, slowly entered Yan Capital.

"Could that be the Seventh Imperial Princess of Great Chu entering the city?"

"What kind of Imperial Princess is she? She’s just a hostage sent by a defeated nation! Think of what Great Chu did to our Great Liang back then. Not killing her already shows our dynasty’s benevolence!"

"I heard this hostage looks exactly like the Third Imperial Princess of Great Chu! I wonder what she looks like?"

"Are you talking about that Third Imperial Princess who is skilled in both literature and martial arts? I heard she was the one behind the scenes planning the battles these past few years? She actually went back and forth with our Regent!"

"You can't say it like that... didn't she lose in the end? She’s not that divine! Our Regent is the truly formidable one! He is the God of War of our Great Liang!"

As the hostage entered the city, the carriage procession was jostled and surrounded by curious onlookers. The intersection was packed so tightly that not even a drop of water could pass through, and the crowd chattered incessantly.

Inside the carriage, the attendant Ruyi rolled up the bamboo blind on one side to glance outside. After a moment, she withdrew her hand, turned to look at her mistress who was sitting and reading a book, and nodded slightly: "Your Highness, we have entered Yan Capital."

Shen Lingjiang nodded, turned a page, and said simply: "Understood. Put the blind down; the wind is biting cold."

Seeing her mistress’s calm and composed demeanor, one would think she was out for a leisurely trip, not entering an enemy state as a hostage.

Ruyi was somewhat anxious and asked hurriedly: "Your Highness, now that we are in Yan Capital, what should we do next?"

Shen Lingjiang smiled and tilted her head to look at her. She was wearing a plain robe, with a thick cloak draped over her shoulders.

Her naturally pale complexion was made even more bloodless by the white fur at her collar. Only the red mole just below her eyelid looked as if it had been branded with blood, vivid and bright.

"What use is your anxiety? Now that we are on someone else’s turf, we must act according to their rules."

Ruyi pouted upon hearing this, muttering in frustration: "...But it’s too unfair. Your Highness is also of noble blood."

Shen Lingjiang glanced at her with a smile and said vaguely: "Just an illegitimate daughter born of a humble background, what kind of noble blood is that?"

Ruyi’s expression changed. She immediately knelt down, kowtowing in terror: "Your Highness!"

Shen Lingjiang did not continue. She waved her hand casually, signaling her to rise, and said no more.

The royal surname of Great Chu is Shangguan, but Shen Lingjiang does not carry the royal surname; she is surnamed Shen.

Her mother was a Hu woman. Emperor Zhao met her while traveling, and after a moment of indulgence, Shen Lingjiang was conceived.

Later, Emperor Zhao left the Hu woman and returned to the palace. It was only after a long time that he remembered he had a child wandering outside and acknowledged her. However, her status was too lowly to be considered royal progeny. At that time, Shen Lingjiang wasn't even entered into the royal genealogy; she was raised in the palace without name or status.

Until now, with the two nations at war and the defeat of Great Chu, the state had no choice but to offer a hostage to the enemy. Only then was this nameless, statusless illegitimate daughter pushed forward and hastily given the title of Seventh Imperial Princess.

The carriage rattled through the bustling streets and stopped in front of a somewhat secluded residence.

"Your Highness, the Seventh Princess, we have arrived at the Hostage Residence."

Outside the carriage, a young soldier in armor approached and said softly against the window.

Immediately after, the carriage door was opened.

Ruyi jumped out first, then turned and reached out to help Shen Lingjiang down.

The Hostage Residence was located on a quiet street, looking cold and desolate.

"Thank you, General." Shen Lingjiang nodded in gratitude, holding Ruyi’s arm as she stepped down.

Shen Lingjiang’s health was poor, an old illness contracted in her home country. After stepping out and catching the wind, she couldn't help but cough several times. Ruyi quickly stepped forward to wrap the cloak tighter around her shoulders.

Shen Lingjiang patted her hand and whispered: "Go and knock on the door."

The little attendant nodded, lifted her skirts, and ran up the stone steps to knock on the circular bronze knocker on the gate.

It was truly freezing; it felt even colder than the imperial capital of Great Chu.

Shen Lingjiang couldn't help but bundle herself in her cloak and retreat under the porch. The snow seemed to be getting heavier, like goose feathers weaving through the air, filling the sky until the scenery was no longer visible.

Ruyi first knocked on the door knocker gently and politely, but there was no movement inside. After waiting for a moment, she simply raised her hand and pounded heavily on the gate.

"Is anyone there? Her Highness the Seventh Princess has arrived!"

No one answered, and no one opened the door. The little attendant continued to pound, her right palm turning red.

Two squads of soldiers stood outside the gate. Seeing this, they couldn't help but show mocking expressions, and a few even laughed out loud.

The young officer leading the soldiers heard the sneers from the ranks and glared at them, forcing the soldiers to straighten their backs and stand at attention, not daring to laugh again.

However, although the officer glared at them, he clearly cast a contemptuous glance at Shen Lingjiang’s back himself. He had no intention of helping; instead, he was happy to watch the hostage from afar make a fool of herself.

It was not surprising; she was an Imperial Princess of an enemy state and a defeated nation, so how much courtesy could one expect to be shown to her?

Facing the gazes that were either provocative or mocking, Shen Lingjiang remained calm, her eyes slightly lowered as she waited quietly.

"Open the door! The Seventh Princess is here! Is there anyone?"

Shen Lingjiang stood unhurriedly in the wind, but Ruyi was young and had a somewhat impatient temperament. Her knocking became heavier, and her tone grew impatient.

After a long time, the gate was finally opened, and a face poked out. The man had sallow, yellowish skin, a gaunt face with no flesh, and high cheekbones, which made him look somewhat mean-spirited at first glance.

He glared coldly at Ruyi and said with intentional sarcasm: "What Seventh Princess? We have no Seventh Princess in Great Liang."

Ruyi was furious: "You!"

"Oh! So the Princess of Great Chu has arrived!" The man acted as if he had just realized, slapped his forehead, and walked out slowly. His demeanor was not very respectful, but he still performed a formal bow to Shen Lingjiang, his actions leaving no room for complaint: "Your Highness, please forgive me. This residence is large and empty, and I didn't hear the noise, so I am late. Please, come in!"

What could Shen Lingjiang say? She shook her head with a faint smile, appearing good-tempered: "No need for apologies. Being new here, I must ask for your care."

The man walked in front with a slightly hunched back, leading Shen Lingjiang into the Hostage Residence, talking as they walked: "My name is Gao, Gao Ruoguan. I have been assigned from above to serve you. If you need anything or lack anything in the future, just command me."

"Oh, this is the Hostage Residence. Shall I show you around? The house is a bit cold and quiet, but I assume Your Highness is not picky and will get used to it."

Wasn't this just saying she was of low status and deserved to live in such a place?

Shen Lingjiang didn't answer immediately but looked up at the furnishings in the garden.

It was called a residence, but it wasn't very large; they had already walked halfway through it in the time it took to speak.

There were covered walkways, newly dug water channels and stone ponds, and cypress trees planted beside the rock formations, remaining lush and green even in winter.

However, the garden had indeed been abandoned for a long time; it was overgrown with weeds and devoid of people, yet it looked vibrant.

Shen Lingjiang looked around for a few moments and said with a smile: "It is all good, all good. It has a certain elegant charm."

Hearing this, Gao Ruoguan smiled even more deeply, his tone becoming even more perfunctory.

He led Shen Lingjiang around the garden once and finally said: "There is a palace banquet tonight, specifically inviting Your Highness. Please tidy up, as you will need to enter the palace later."

Ruyi was truly young and spoke without thinking. Her eyes widened, and she asked curiously: "Is it a banquet specifically to welcome my mistress?"

chapters.title: Standoff at the Palace Gate
chapters.content:
"Pfft!"

As if he had heard a great joke, Gao Ruoguan couldn't help but burst into laughter.

He looked at Shen Lingjiang and Ruyi with a strange expression for a long while before saying slowly: "It is the Golden Banquet, a victory celebration held for the Regent."

The Golden Banquet; Shen Lingjiang had heard of it.

This banquet, named after the sentiment of "offering gold to honor the king's intent," was held specifically to celebrate military achievements. It was clearly meant to celebrate the victory in the war between the two nations.

Inviting a hostage from an enemy state to such a victory banquet, the underlying meaning was self-evident.

This Gao Ruoguan was ostensibly a servant sent to serve Shen Lingjiang, but anyone with eyes could see he was an eye placed by the Emperor of Great Liang to monitor her.

And so, after leading Shen Lingjiang inside and spouting a basketful of nonsense, he didn't even offer a cup of hot tea before leaving her behind.

Shen Lingjiang said to her little attendant: "Ruyi, let’s tidy up."

Ruyi pouted, cleaned the main room, and dusted with a feather duster.

She muttered as she worked, "This is too bullying."

Shen Lingjiang asked her in return: "There will be more bullying in the future; can you not handle this much?"

Ruyi immediately replied: "This servant feels aggrieved for you!"

Shen Lingjiang shook her head and didn't answer.

The little attendant, however, kept chattering: "Your Highness, is that Regent the one the Emperor mentioned? The Emperor said... the Emperor said you are to marry him as his wife. I wonder if that Prince is willing."

The Regent...

Shen Lingjiang’s eyes went slightly vacant, as if she had fallen into a memory, though no one knew what she was thinking.

"Your Highness?"

Shen Lingjiang regained her focus and said with a hint of mockery: "You said it yourself, he is the Regent. What kind of celestial beauty could he not marry? Would he be willing to marry a lowly hostage from a defeated nation?"

The Regent, Xie Yunzhou, was approaching thirty and had no wives or concubines.

Emperor Zhao’s intention was that perhaps the Regent was too immersed in state affairs to care for women, so he was willing to offer the most beautiful Imperial Princess to relieve the emptiness of the Regent’s bed.

In fact, his intention didn't even require her to be a wife or concubine; he simply said he was willing to offer the Imperial Princess without asking for status.

Thinking of this, a mocking smile appeared at the corner of Shen Lingjiang’s mouth.

Her muddled and incompetent father only felt that because she was born of a Hu woman, she was as lowly as dust, and even if she were to become a nameless concubine, it was what she deserved, after all, her birth mother was the same, locked in the deep palace and dying without a name. He never considered that she, now the Seventh Imperial Princess of Great Chu, would be insulting the Great Chu royal family if she truly gave herself to Xie Yunzhou.

However... she didn't care. It would be better if it were an insult.

Shen Lingjiang smiled contemptuously, suddenly noticing a few sparrows flying outside.

She immediately walked over, leaned out to look, and called: "Ruyi, get some bird feed."

Ruyi, who was cleaning, immediately took a small bamboo tube from their luggage and handed it to Shen Lingjiang with both hands. Seeing her open the lid and take the feed, she sprinkled it outside the window, attracting a few sparrows to peck at it.

"I didn't expect there to be birds in Yan Capital in winter." Ruyi also took a look and said casually, "Since Your Highness likes birds so much, why not keep one yourself? I think those bulbuls and parrots are quite beautiful."

Shen Lingjiang liked feeding birds; she had even carried bird feed with her all the way from Great Chu to Great Liang.

Hearing Ruyi’s words, she was silent for a moment before speaking.

"It’s only interesting if they fly in the sky. If they are locked in a cage all day, it’s meaningless; it’s just disappointing to look at."

"Your Highness, the time is almost up. Shall we prepare to enter the palace?"

Gao Ruoguan appeared from nowhere, standing beside Shen Lingjiang with little respect, his head slightly lowered.

Shen Lingjiang changed into a slightly more formal outfit, but because of her awkward status, it was still a plain color with a simple style.

She nodded at Gao Ruoguan, followed him out, boarded the same carriage, and headed toward the palace.

Shen Lingjiang turned her body, tucked her sleeves, rolled up the bamboo blind of the carriage window, and leaned out to look.

The carriage had already entered the palace gates. Everywhere she looked were red walls and green tiles, the paths solemn and majestic.

She looked up at the sky, which was a square patch trapped within the golden palace. White clouds were layered and intertwined on the horizon, looking soft and white but piled very high, so high that even the palace at the very top couldn't touch them.

Outside the Qingyi Hall, her carriage was blocked at the gate.

Gao Ruoguan said pretentiously outside: "This is the carriage of the Seventh Princess of Great Chu."

Immediately, a guard holding a long spear scoffed and said disdainfully: "Pfft, just a hostage, how can she enter through the main gate of Qingyi Hall! Tell the Princess to get off and walk to the side gate to enter the hall!"

Ruyi was still by Shen Lingjiang’s side. She endured and endured, but finally couldn't hold back.

The little attendant snapped open the curtain, glared angrily at the guard, and shouted: "Is this the hospitality of your Great Liang?!"

The guard acted as if he had heard a joke, exchanged glances with his colleagues, and they all laughed heartily. Then, he mocked her unceremoniously: "Guest? Princess, do you really consider yourself a guest?"

Ruyi was furious, and before long, her eyes were red with anger.

At this moment, Gao Ruoguan acted considerate, extended his hand to help, hunched his back, and said: "Your Highness, you should get off. It’s only a few steps, and blocking the way here will only invite more ridicule."

As he said this, several people stood near the palace gate, all dressed in expensive clothing, both men and women, all curiously tilting their heads and stretching their necks to look outside.

How could Shen Lingjiang not understand?

This Gao Ruoguan was doing it on purpose. He knew she couldn't enter through the main gate, but he deliberately led her here to make her a laughingstock and invite mockery.

Shen Lingjiang tilted her head and looked at Gao Ruoguan with a half-smile but didn't point it out. She just said calmly: "I am new here and don't know the rules of Great Liang. But you, do you not know the rules either? Leading me to charge in blindly, aren't you afraid of offending the nobles in the palace?"

Gao Ruoguan: "..."

Gao Ruoguan froze, still maintaining his bowing posture, and said nothing.

Shen Lingjiang continued: "Although my words carry little weight, the Emperor of Great Liang is a benevolent and virtuous monarch. I believe he would grant my request to replace an ignorant servant."

Gao Ruoguan immediately broke into a cold sweat, pulled his hand back, knelt down, and threw himself onto the ground.

"Your Highness, please be magnanimous! Please forgive this servant’s stupidity!"

This was his own doing; he had thought this hostage was easy to bully and manipulate. Who knew that in just a few sentences, she would threaten to report him to the Emperor?

He was an eye placed by his superiors to monitor the hostage; how could he be sent back for being "ignorant"? If he really went back, would he even keep his life?

Gao Ruoguan was also extremely angry and hated the people of Great Chu.

He had two older brothers who had both gone to the battlefield, and neither had returned.

Therefore, Gao Ruoguan hated the people of Great Chu and naturally had no good expression for the hostage of Great Chu.

Overcome by hatred, he had privately led Shen Lingjiang to the main hall, thinking to dampen her spirit.

Shen Lingjiang let him kneel at the base of the wall for a long time before saying: "The carriage is not equipped with a step stool. Being at the palace gate, it would be unseemly for me to jump down."

Gao Ruoguan’s figure, huddled at the wall, paused slightly. The next moment, he immediately crawled on his knees to the front of the carriage and knelt down properly on the ground.

Ruyi blinked, immediately jumped off the other side of the carriage, ran over, and reached out to help Shen Lingjiang.

Shen Lingjiang reached out, stepped on his back, and stepped down from the carriage steadily.

She stood still for a moment before saying: "Aren't you going to lead the way? Do you really want me to charge blindly through the palace?"

Gao Ruoguan immediately scrambled up, hurried to the front, and led the way.

chapters.title: The Cruelty of Human Sentiment
chapters.content:
Entering the Qingyi Hall through a side door, Shen Lingjiang followed the palace attendants to her seat.

As she was merely a hostage princess, her seat was placed quite far back.

Once seated, although no one spoke to her, she could feel several gazes prickling her skin, like needles against her back.

There seemed to be whispers as well.

"Is that the Seventh Imperial Princess of Great Chu?"

"Shh... she really does look like a siren. I heard her mother was a Hu woman. Hu women are known for their beauty, so she must have inherited her mother's looks."

"Tsk, tsk, the Regent is truly a lucky man! But I heard the Emperor of Great Chu intends to use the princess for a political marriage!"

"A mere hostage... it’s impossible for the Regent to actually take a hostage as his wife! A defeated nation; they truly dare to dream!"

These voices were not loud, yet they burrowed into her ears like gnats, impossible to brush away, impossible to swat.

Shen Lingjiang sat upright, a faint, elusive smile always playing on her lips. Her posture and movements were perfectly proper, as if she were completely deaf to the disparaging and contemptuous remarks.

Though the gossip continued, no one dared to confront her directly, maintaining a strange, fragile peace for the moment.

Until...

"So, you’re the hostage princess sent by Great Chu?"

The speaker was a young man with a greasy, powdered face, dressed in luxurious silks. He wore a gem-encrusted silk headband, a high-quality jade pendant hung from his belt, and a dark thumb ring adorned his hand. He was decked out in ostentatious finery.

Several seats around Shen Lingjiang were empty; the man sat four places away, looking at her from afar with a provocative gaze.

Since someone had broken the ice, Shen Lingjiang could not play the mute. She nodded at him, raised her hand in a gesture of greeting, and replied, "I am indeed Shen Lingjiang."

"Shen, Ling, Jiang." The man chuckled, repeating her name. Then, with a frivolous expression, he leaned in and asked with a grin, "Why is your surname Shen? Isn't the imperial surname of Great Chu 'Shangguan'? I heard the famous Third Imperial Princess is called Shangguan Ying."

"You are truly beautiful. Even the concubines in my manor aren't as pretty as you." The man stared at her, speaking slowly. Despite the lewd and offensive nature of his words, he spoke with an air of brazen ease, as if there were nothing wrong with saying this to her. "Hey, is your third sister as beautiful as you?"

Shen Lingjiang had been sipping tea, but because of his words, she had to set down her cup.

Even as she heard him, she kept her eyes lowered in a humble, submissive manner, appearing to have a temperament that would endure anything.

She pinched the teacup in her hand, waited a moment, and then said to him, "I thank you for the compliment, Young Marquis. My appearance is plain; I dare not compare myself to the bright moon."

The man was taken aback for a moment before asking, "You know who I am? How did you know I am a Young Marquis?"

Shen Lingjiang released the teacup, pressed her reddened palm, and said unhurriedly, "The seat you occupy is the second position for a Marquis. Yet you are young; I assume there are no Marquises in Great Liang who inherited their titles at such a young age?"

"I had heard long ago that the Marquis of Jing'an dotes on his only son, raising him to be... well, exceptionally 'bold.' Indeed, among the princes and nobles present, everyone views me as a thorn in their side, yet no one dared to be the first to strike. Only the Young Marquis is so straightforward and frank. It seems you truly despise me."

In truth, Shen Lingjiang had prepared thoroughly before entering Yandu. She had obtained portraits of these people long ago and had memorized the faces of all the officials, from the two kings and six dukes to the eighteen marquises.

Seeing the Young Marquis’s expression shift, Shen Lingjiang continued, neither fast nor slow.

"Alas, there is nothing to be done. Though I know you despise me, I must ask you to bear with it for a while. You wouldn't have me thrown out of this Qingyi Hall, would you?"

This son of the Marquis of Jing'an was named He Weishi. As the only son in his family and with an aunt who was the current Empress Dowager, his status was noble. He had indeed been spoiled into having no sense of propriety; when angered, he had to vent his frustration immediately, regardless of the fact that he was in the imperial palace.

He stood up in a rage, grabbed his cup, and hurled it straight at Shen Lingjiang. The teacup grazed her temple and shattered on the floor, shards of cold porcelain scattering everywhere.

The cup hadn't hit her directly, but it had grazed her temple, breaking the skin and drawing a bead of blood.

"Insolent! You have some nerve!" He Weishi pointed at her and scolded, "Sharp-tongued! Truly, it is as they say: only villains and women are difficult to deal with!"

Did she think he couldn't tell? When she said he was "exceptionally bold," she was mocking his recklessness.

The teacup had been thrown at her head; although it missed, Shen Lingjiang had instinctively closed her eyes.

He Weishi, the only heir to the Marquis of Jing'an, backed by the Empress Dowager and cousin to the young Emperor, with such status, a tantrum at a palace banquet would at most earn him a mild, painless reprimand. Who could do anything to him?

Sure enough, those around him, seeing the farce, began to comfort him.

"Young Marquis, why bother with her? She’s just a lowly illegitimate daughter."

"Please, calm your anger, Young Marquis! Someone, bring the Young Marquis another cup!"

Shen Lingjiang let out a breath, released her left wrist with her right hand, and pulled her sleeve down to cover the purple bruises on her wrist.

She smiled again, bowed to He Weishi, and apologized, "It was my slip of the tongue... My status is lowly, I have not read many books, and I do not know how to speak well. Please, do not take offense, Young Marquis."

She was certainly capable of bending and stretching. Seeing her concede, He Weishi immediately smiled maliciously, his face changing as quickly as turning a page.

"Well, never mind. I have always been lenient toward beauties."

His smile deepened as he sat back down, propping his chin on his hand to look at Shen Lingjiang. "I heard the Emperor wants you to marry the Regent? Tsk, I don't mean to discourage you, but the Prince does not care for women. I fear that plan will come to nothing. However... I find you interesting. Why not come with me?"

"Oh! Right! I heard your mother was a Hu woman from the Yuezhi? Though Hu women are lowly, I hear they are all peerless beauties, skilled in song and dance. Since your mother was a Hu woman, did she teach you any dances? A banquet without music or dance is incomplete. Why not dance for us, Princess? Consider it a contribution to the festivities!"

He Weishi’s laughter grew more arrogant, and his gaze fixed on Shen Lingjiang became increasingly lewd and brazen.

Those around them roared with laughter, and some even joined in.

"Young Marquis! You are truly a joker! A hostage is just a hostage! What does it matter if she is beautiful? How could she have the figure of a dancer?"

"Exactly! You really know how to joke! A hostage... dancing? Hahahahaha!"

As the laughter filled the hall, Shen Lingjiang remained silent, only offering a smile toward He Weishi, though her eyes were cold enough to freeze.

"The Regent arrives!"

At that very moment, the call of the eunuchs echoed from outside the hall, layer by layer. The Regent, Xie Yunzhou, had arrived.

chapters.title: Bitter Harassment
chapters.content:
The hall fell silent. Even the boisterous and arrogant He Weishi shut his mouth, seemingly afraid of the Regent.

Shen Lingjiang took a plain handkerchief from her bodice, pressed it against the broken skin on her temple, and sat with lowered eyes.

Xie Yunzhou strode into the hall with crisp, decisive steps. He wore a black, tight-sleeved martial outfit with gold-threaded patterns on the cuffs and collar. He had heroic features, a tall and sturdy frame, and his gait was swift and steady.

"Greetings, Your Highness!"

"May the Regent be well!"

Everyone present bowed to Xie Yunzhou, except for Shen Lingjiang, who remained seated. She glanced at him once, then turned her head away, pressing the handkerchief to her temple and remaining still.

Upon entering, Xie Yunzhou had already heard of the hostage princess from Great Chu and knew of the Emperor's clever scheme.

He stood in the hall, scanning the room with eagle-like eyes that locked onto Shen Lingjiang in the corner. She appeared submissive and quiet, sitting in the shadows with her head bowed. Her jawline was elegant, her profile stunning; she was indeed as the rumors described.

Rumor had it that this hostage princess was of low birth, born to a Hu woman, and resembled her mother. She possessed a beauty as cold as ice and snow, a truly breathtaking appearance, but she was merely an empty vessel, a pretty fool, far inferior to her elder sister, Shangguan Ying.

Shangguan Ying’s brilliance was renowned, and even in the Liang Kingdom, her name was known. Though she was an imperial princess, she had insisted on going to the battlefield despite her noble status. Xie Yunzhou had faced her several times and had lost three times.

The undefeated God of War had lost for the first time in his life, and he had held a grudge, remembering her well.

In Xie Yunzhou’s eyes, the only person in all of Great Chu worth noting was Shangguan Ying; all others were merely common dross.

And now, Great Chu had sent him this "dross," claiming she would be his wife.

Xie Yunzhou sneered inwardly, flicked his sleeves, and walked forward, asking as he went, "I heard the noise from outside. What were you all laughing about? What was so amusing?"

Hearing the Regent’s inquiry, He Weishi hesitated for a moment before standing up. "In reply to Your Highness, we were just asking the Seventh Princess to dance for our amusement."

"Dance?"

Xie Yunzhou paused, instinctively looking toward Shen Lingjiang again, his gaze filled with astonishment.

Her? She looked as if a gust of wind could blow her away. Could she even dance? Could she even lift a sword?

He Weishi, unaware of the Regent’s misunderstanding, smiled maliciously and continued, "Just a dance to liven things up. I heard the Seventh Princess’s mother was a Hu woman, and they are all skilled in song and dance. I assume the Seventh Princess has inherited those talents!"

Xie Yunzhou raised an eyebrow, clearly interested.

He did not like Shen Lingjiang.

Strictly speaking, he loathed everyone from Great Chu.

Great Chu loved war, and the conflicts had always been instigated by them.

Fifteen years ago, Great Chu started the first war. The fighting was fierce, and the Liang Kingdom suffered repeated defeats with countless casualties. The yellow earth of the battlefield was stained red with blood, and bones piled up to the sky.

His eldest brother had died in that great battle, the Crown Prince, known for his virtue. There was no one in Liang who did not hate them.

Liang had lost once and retreated to recuperate, waiting to avenge the national grudge. But before they could act, Great Chu had impatiently launched a second war.

Alas, this time, Great Chu was defeated.

Xie Yunzhou hated them; the two nations were mortal enemies. Although he respected Shangguan Ying as an opponent, if she were to fall into his hands, it would be hard to say what would happen.

Therefore, Xie Yunzhou did not like Shen Lingjiang, and he was more than happy to watch her make a fool of herself.

"Is that so? I am somewhat curious about the dances of the Yuezhi. I wonder if I might have the chance to see one."

Hearing this, He Weishi became even more smug, feeling that even the Regent was on his side!

He immediately called over a palace servant who was waiting respectfully nearby and said with a wicked grin, "Go, fetch a dance costume that fits the Seventh Princess!"

Shen Lingjiang was frail, a sickly creature; where would one find a dress that fit her?

The servant was young and had been standing quietly aside. Suddenly being singled out by He Weishi, and knowing the Young Marquis's reputation, she couldn't help but tremble. She glanced at Shen Lingjiang several times before kneeling on the ground, her voice shaking as she said, "Young Marquis, I fear there are no clothes suitable for the Seventh Princess."

Being rebuffed by a mere maid, He Weishi’s face darkened. He kicked the maid in the chest, knocking her over, and scolded, "Insolent slave! You didn't even try, yet you make excuses. What, are you feeling pity for an outsider? Are you a spy lurking in the palace, perhaps a citizen of Great Chu?"

The maid had been kicked, but she dared not cry out. She crawled back in pain, her face pale with terror as she kowtowed. "Forgive me, Young Marquis! Forgive me! This servant is no spy!"

Shen Lingjiang’s brows furrowed slightly, but she quickly smoothed them, her face showing no sign of anger.

She bowed her head slightly and said to Xie Yunzhou, "Your Highness is renowned for your might. It is only unexpected that a man of such stature would have such unique tastes. It is not that Shen Lingjiang wishes to refuse, but I fear that if I were to dance, all the lords present would be so nauseated they would be unable to eat, which would be a waste of this fine feast."

Xie Yunzhou fixed his gaze on her, tilting his head slightly to look down at her.

He Weishi sneered, about to speak again.

Suddenly, the shrill voice of a eunuch rang through the hall.

"His Majesty arrives!"

The arguments and whispers died down instantly. Everyone except Xie Yunzhou rose and knelt on the ground, chanting "Long live the Emperor" three times.

The young Emperor walked out, a faint smile on his face. He first walked to Xie Yunzhou, supported the Regent as he began to bow, and said with a gentle smile, "Uncle, no need for such formalities. Please, sit!"

With that, he personally helped Xie Yunzhou to the first seat on the lower level before turning and waving his hand, saying calmly, "Everyone, rise."

Shen Lingjiang, who had been kneeling on the floor, slowly looked up before rising to take her seat.

Xie Chongguang, the young Emperor, scanned the room and suddenly asked, "Is the Sixth Uncle not here?"

A pale-faced eunuch behind him leaned in, bowing his back, and replied in a soft voice, "Your Majesty, Prince Xin is unwell and asked for leave early this morning."

Prince Xin, Xie Yunqi, was the sixth son of the late Emperor and one of the three princes of Great Liang. He was older than Xie Yunzhou.

But Xie Yunzhou and his sixth brother had never been on good terms. Who knew if he was truly ill or just making an excuse to avoid attending the victory banquet.

These were side matters. The young Emperor sat on the dragon throne, his gentle, smiling gaze peering out from behind the swaying strings of pearls on his crown.

He suddenly asked, "I heard the Seventh Princess of Great Chu has arrived. Where is she?"

It had come. Indeed, there was no escaping it.

Shen Lingjiang blinked, sighing silently in her heart.

Finally, she lifted her hem, stood up, walked forward, and bowed to the dragon throne. "Shen Lingjiang of Great Chu greets the Emperor of Liang."

Xie Chongguang looked at her with a smile, nodded slightly, and asked, "Your surname is Shen?"

chapters.title: Seeking a Path to Survival
chapters.content:
"Yes. Shen Lingjiang is of lowly status and does not share the national surname. Fortunately, the name Shen Lingjiang has been used for twenty years; if I were to change it suddenly, I would only find it uncomfortable."

"Oh... then you took your mother's surname?" Xie Chongguang asked thoughtfully. Though he asked, he didn't take it to heart, and changing the subject, he asked, "Do you have a courtesy name?"

Shen Lingjiang did not answer the previous question, only lowering her head as she said, "Shen Lingjiang, courtesy name Lanshu."

Xie Chongguang nodded, speaking as if to himself, "Lanshu... 'The orchid grows in the deep valley, not failing to be fragrant because no one admires it.' A fine name! Since you have come from afar, you are a guest. Someone, move the Seventh Princess's seat to the front. Lanshu, sit quickly!"

As he spoke, he gestured toward the seat beside Xie Yunzhou.

Several young eunuchs immediately bowed their heads, took quick, small steps over, and moved Shen Lingjiang’s dining table and stool forward.

Shen Lingjiang: "Many thanks, Your Majesty."

She had just sat down and had not yet managed to relax when she heard the Emperor say with a faint smile, "I already know the intent of the Emperor of Zhao. It is kind of him to remember my imperial uncle. I am also inclined to help fulfill his wish, but I wonder how my imperial uncle feels about this?"

The Emperor had not yet announced the start of the banquet, but Xie Yunzhou was already leaning against his table, having downed several cups of wine. Only upon hearing the voice did he look up, glance at Shen Lingjiang, and say indifferently, "Empty beauty; I have no interest."

Shen Lingjiang’s fingers, hidden in her sleeves, curled, but a smile remained on her face. She even lowered her head to speak to Xie Yunzhou, "The Prince has a discerning eye; my brothers and sisters have all said the same."

The Emperor laughed twice more, his smiling eyes sweeping over Xie Yunzhou. He stared for a moment, but ultimately did not continue the topic.

"Let the banquet begin! Drink freely, my subjects!"

Once the Emperor gave the word, the atmosphere in the hall eased slightly, and the sounds of clinking cups gradually arose.

It was a victory banquet, so naturally, there was no shortage of congratulations.

"A great victory for the Prince! You have raised the prestige of our Liang Kingdom! I toast you!"

"A total victory in this battle! I expect Great Chu will not dare to raise arms again! I toast the Prince; you must drink!"

"I also congratulate the Prince on your triumphant return! You are truly worthy of the title 'God of War'!"

Cup after cup was offered. It was unclear what Xie Yunzhou’s tolerance was; he hadn't eaten a single bite of food, drinking only wine, yet his expression remained unchanged.

Shen Lingjiang did not care for wine; she silently picked up two pieces of greens with her chopsticks, but had no time to eat them.

Suddenly, she heard someone call her name; it was the provocative voice of He Weishi.

"Seventh Princess! Everyone here has toasted the Prince! Since you are in our Great Liang for such a joyous occasion, won't you offer a toast?"

Very good, that was well said.

As a princess of the Great Chu Kingdom, Shen Lingjiang had to toast Xie Yunzhou at this banquet. But what was she to toast him for? For having just beaten her motherland into a state of disarray?

Sure enough, as soon as He Weishi’s words fell, laughter erupted in the hall.

Someone else chimed in, appearing to offer a way out but actually dripping with sarcasm, "Young Master, you are making things difficult for her! The Princess's motherland just suffered a defeat! She might be hiding under her covers crying at night! Asking her to toast is just rubbing salt in the wound, isn't it?"

"Exactly, exactly."

Shen Lingjiang acted as if she hadn't heard. She raised her wrist, filled a cup to the brim, and held it up respectfully toward Xie Yunzhou, who sat beside her.

"The Prince is undefeated in a hundred battles, and Yandu sings songs of triumph. Shen Lingjiang toasts you, wishing only for peace between our two nations so that the people may live in tranquility."

Xie Yunzhou looked at her expressionlessly, remaining silent for a long time.

Shen Lingjiang held the wine cup with a smile, her hands suspended in the air for so long that they began to ache. Only then did Xie Yunzhou pick up his own cup, clink it against hers in the air, and say emotionlessly, "I accept your well-wishes, Princess. As long as Great Chu behaves, the people will naturally be at peace."

Shen Lingjiang said nothing, only smiling as she drank the wine.

Afterward, songs and dances were performed at the palace banquet, and the atmosphere was filled with joy.

After the banquet ended, Shen Lingjiang and Ruyi walked out of the Qingyi Hall. She didn't know where Gao Ruguan had gone to slack off again; she couldn't see him anywhere.

Ruyi looked up, the hair buns on her head wobbling, "Princess, what shall we do now? Return to the Residence of the Hostage Princess?"

Shen Lingjiang sighed heavily, walking slowly along the palace path. She glanced at the young-faced Ruyi and answered patiently, "If we enter the Residence of the Hostage Princess, we fear we will be confined. Today was a victory banquet; Great Liang wanted to use this opportunity to suppress and humiliate me, a princess of a defeated nation. If we had gone back there today, we would never have been able to leave."

Ruyi’s eyes widened, and she asked hurriedly, "Then what should we do?!"

Shen Lingjiang looked around. The palace paths stretched in all directions, all clean and brand new.

She whispered, "All roads lead somewhere; there are always paths that do not lead to the Residence of the Hostage Princess."

That night, the stars and moon were hidden behind thick clouds, and not a glimmer of light could be seen. Fortunately, the palace was brightly lit, and the paths were illuminated, the lamps reflecting on the bluestone floor as if a plain yellow carpet had been laid out.

Shen Lingjiang and Ruyi walked out of the palace gate one after the other and happened to see a black wood carriage parked not far away.

This carriage was much grander than the green-cloth one Shen Lingjiang had arrived in. Though grand, it was not extravagant or ostentatious; the style was simple, with no gold or silver decorations.

Pinned to the front of the carriage was a black and red flag a foot long, fluttering in the cold wind. Embroidered on it in gold thread were two bold, sweeping characters: "Xuan Tie" (Black Iron).

"Xuan" and "Tie" represented the "Xuange Battalion" and the "Tieyi Battalion," the two divine armies under the command of the Regent, Xie Yunzhou.

In the vast capital, only Xie Yunzhou could, and dared to, use the characters "Xuan Tie."

Shen Lingjiang slowed her pace, speaking as if to herself or to Ruyi, "Look, the path has found us on its own."

Ruyi tilted her head, confused, and uttered a single word: "Huh?"

She opened her mouth blankly, her expression dazed as she looked at her mistress, like a simpleton whose head was filled with water.

But Shen Lingjiang did not explain further; she lifted her feet and walked toward the carriage.

Outside the carriage, two men were bickering.

One was a burly man with dark skin, a square face, and broad lips; he was dressed simply and carried a thick-backed black saber on his back. The other was a tall, thin man with fair skin, phoenix eyes, and his hair tied high; he held a sword and wore a stern expression at all times.

The former was "Li Wanli," the Left General under Xie Yunzhou; the latter was "Luo Yangming," the Right General under Xie Yunzhou.

The two were effectively Xie Yunzhou’s right and left arms.

Neither paid any attention to Shen Lingjiang and her maid as they approached, continuing to bicker back and forth.

Though they were arguing, Li Wanli spoke with such animation he was practically dancing.

Li Wanli shouted excitedly, "My sister got into the Imperial Academy! My sister got into the Imperial Academy! She’s a student there now! This is such a face-saver for our Li family! If she can pass the imperial examinations and become a Jinshi, the ancestral graves of my entire family will be smoking with good fortune!"

Luo Yangming, leaning against the carriage shaft with his sword, said expressionlessly, "Oh."

Li Wanli: "That’s the Imperial Academy! Sigh, I’m a brute; I can’t read! My other cousins only know how to wield swords and spears; she’s the only scholar our family has produced!"

Luo Yangming: "You’ve said that five times already. Aren't you annoyed?"

chapters.title: Casting Pearls Before Swine
chapters.content:
It wasn't until Shen Lingjiang drew near that the two stopped, both frowning and glaring vigilantly at the mistress and maid.

"Two Generals, is the Regent inside? I have some words I wish to speak with him. I wonder if it is convenient now?"

Li Wanli only frowned and said nothing, but Luo Yangming was much less polite. He drew his sword directly toward Shen Lingjiang and said mercilessly, "Enemy, you are not worthy to speak with our Prince."

Neither subordinate was welcoming, but a sound came from inside the carriage. The next moment, the door opened, and Shen Lingjiang saw Xie Yunzhou sitting inside.

He sat in the carriage, elbows on his knees, his body leaning slightly forward, and hooked a finger at Shen Lingjiang. "Get in."

Luo Yangming blinked, then coldly sheathed his sword and stepped aside without a word.

Shen Lingjiang nodded slightly, said "Many thanks," and reached for the carriage shaft to climb up.

She was truly climbing; to be honest, it was not a graceful sight.

No one offered her a footstool, and since the carriage was high and Shen Lingjiang was neither a martial artist nor in good health, it took quite an effort to pull herself up.

Xie Yunzhou leaned on his hand, looking down at her with a mocking smile in his eyes.

Shen Lingjiang acted as if she didn't see it. She even had the audacity to extend her right hand, smiling as she said, "Prince, could you lend a hand?"

Seeing this, Luo Yangming curled his lip, his eyes full of mockery.

But then, Xie Yunzhou actually reached out, grabbed Shen Lingjiang’s thin wrist, and dragged her inside.

Shen Lingjiang let out a startled cry, and before she could recover, she had been pulled in, and the carriage door slammed shut behind her.

Ruyi stood outside, hesitating, nervous and frightened, calling out timidly, "...Princess?"

Luo Yangming curled his lip and said nothing, propping one hand on the carriage board and vaulting up.

Li Wanli looked at her, and seeing she was even younger than his own sister, he softened his voice to comfort her: "Hey, little girl, don't worry. Our Prince doesn't eat people! Go back and wait; your mistress will return when the time is right."

With that, he mounted his horse, and with one driving the horse and the other the carriage, they headed toward the Regent’s mansion.

Ruyi didn't dare leave; she started running to keep up.

Inside the carriage.

Shen Lingjiang had been pulled in and was kneeling on the floor, rubbing her wrist, which had been gripped red.

Xie Yunzhou leaned back, looking at Shen Lingjiang with a mocking smile, and asked deliberately, "What? Can't forget the dance you didn't get to perform? Did you come specifically to offer a dance?"

Shen Lingjiang rubbed her wrist, looking up at him while kneeling. Under the candlelight, her exquisite face was visible; the red mole beneath her eye looked even more vivid in the flickering light, and the wound on her temple from the wine cup was even redder.

She smiled slightly, asking in a playful tone, "Does the Prince still wish to see it? It's a pity there isn't enough room to perform in this carriage."

Xie Yunzhou asked her, "Can you really dance?"

Shen Lingjiang continued to smile, answering slowly, "I would risk my life to entertain a gentleman."

As soon as she finished speaking, the carriage jolted suddenly.

Shen Lingjiang’s brows twitched, and she immediately took the opportunity to fall toward Xie Yunzhou’s feet, reaching out to grab his knees, and even turning her face to reveal her most exquisite and beautiful profile.

Unfortunately, Xie Yunzhou was as unyielding as wood.

He dodged quickly, and Shen Lingjiang’s forehead hit the thick wooden board of the carriage seat with a thud.

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Shen Lingjiang lowered her head in silence, while two bursts of hearty, mocking laughter sounded above her.

Well, it was as expected; how could a man like Xie Yunzhou be moved by beauty?

Shen Lingjiang thought to herself, rubbed her bruised forehead, and straightened up.

Xie Yunzhou looked at her for a moment, then suddenly leaned forward, reached out to pinch Shen Lingjiang’s chin, and tilted her face up. He examined her left and right, up and down, as if admiring a piece of porcelain or a toy, before saying, "Looking like you do, it’s no surprise you can dance. If I changed your clothes, no one would be able to tell your status."

The words were not polite; the tone was full of mockery and insult.

But Shen Lingjiang acted as if she didn't understand. She still smiled and said bluntly, "It is precisely because I look like this that I had the fortune to be sent to Yandu."

After a pause, she knelt forward two steps, her slightly hunched back appearing submissive and harmless, and said humbly, "My Emperor has sent me to you, Prince. Please, accept the gift."

"Heh." Xie Yunzhou watched her for a long time, then suddenly sneered, leaned back, and scolded, "Utterly vulgar."

Afterward, he leaned against the soft cushions, closed his eyes, and stopped looking at Shen Lingjiang, who was kneeling at his feet.

Shen Lingjiang did not stand up. She remained kneeling on the floor with a smile, continuing to lower her eyes and rub her wrist.

With her eyelashes lowered, no one could see the emotions hidden deep in her eyes.

In the dark night, the carriage traveled through the streets at a steady pace, turned several corners, and finally stopped outside the Regent’s mansion.

"Prince, we have arrived!"

Xie Yunzhou opened his eyes and, ignoring Shen Lingjiang kneeling at his feet, stepped out of the carriage.

Shen Lingjiang sighed, gently massaged her numb calves, and then pulled herself up by the carriage wall to step down.

Her legs were numb and trembling, almost devoid of sensation. As soon as she jumped down, her legs gave way, and she fell forward.

Xie Yunzhou was standing by the carriage, hands behind his back, giving instructions to Li Wanli. No sooner had he finished speaking than Shen Lingjiang fell into his arms, her hand grabbing his lapel so hard she nearly ripped his clothes off.

He pinned her down and lifted her up like a chick, frowning as he asked, "What new trick is this? Did the Emperor of Zhao teach you this too?"

Shen Lingjiang: "...Prince, this was truly an accident."

Xie Yunzhou: "Then the previous one was indeed intentional?"

Shen Lingjiang: "The Prince is sharp."

The two spoke back and forth as if in a riddle; Li Wanli and Luo Yangming stood by, completely bewildered.

Just then, a plump old steward came out from the mansion, smiling as he asked, "The Prince has returned! Hot water is already prepared; would you like to bathe first?"

Xie Yunzhou nodded, then grabbed Shen Lingjiang’s wrist and dragged her into the mansion.

Ruyi finally caught up, shouting "Princess!" at the top of her lungs, but before she could say more, she watched as her mistress was dragged through the tall, imposing gate of the Regent’s mansion.

"...Princess! What, what am I supposed to do now!"

Ruyi was so anxious that tears welled up in her eyes, and she rushed toward the gate.

Li Wanli stopped her, saying, "Hey, little girl, stop right there. The Prince’s mansion isn't a place just anyone can enter!"

Ruyi: "I... but my Princess..."

She spun around in circles, pointing with red eyes in the direction where Shen Lingjiang had disappeared.

Seeing how young she was and how pale with fright she had become, Li Wanli couldn't bear it and was about to offer a few words of comfort.

Luo Yangming walked over, holding his sword, and said irritably, "This is Yandu, not a battlefield. Do you really think they’re going to kill your Princess and use her for a flag sacrifice?"

chapters.title: Bathing Together
chapters.content:
Ruyi was terrified, her lips pouting as she began to shed tears.

Li Wanli couldn't bear it. He tugged at Luo Yangming’s sleeve and muttered in a low voice, "She’s just a little girl; why are you trying to scare her?"

The icicles shooting from Luo Yangming’s eyes didn't distinguish between friend and foe. He immediately glared back, "Don’t your cousins all dance with swords and spears? Many of them have died on the battlefield, haven't they? Isn't the youngest one about the same age as this person? Since when is it your turn to sympathize with the people of Great Chu?"

Li Wanli choked, his expression darkening. He stopped speaking, flicked his sleeves, and walked into the manor.

Luo Yangming gave a cold snort and followed closely behind.

The chubby old steward stepped forward, patted Ruyi on the shoulder, and said with a smile, "Little one, just wait here at the gate for a while."

Leaving that behind, the old steward also turned and entered the manor.

Ruyi sobbed as she wiped her tears, then hugged her shoulders and crouched by the gate, muttering softly, "That’s just too much of a bully."

The Prince’s servants had already prepared hot water for bathing. Xie Yunzhou dragged Shen Lingjiang by the wrist all the way into the bathroom.

"Doesn't Your Highness wish to serve this Prince? Then why not try it tonight? Serve this Prince while I bathe?"

As he spoke, he released Shen Lingjiang’s wrist and opened his arms toward her.

Shen Lingjiang smiled, not moving for a moment.

Xie Yunzhou asked again, "What? Did Emperor Zhao only teach you how to sleep with men? He didn't teach you how to serve them?"

Shen Lingjiang finally moved. She stepped toward Xie Yunzhou and reached out to cover his waist and back from the front.

Xie Yunzhou was a martial general and disliked wearing dangling jade pendants; his waist was only cinched by a wide black-and-gold sash.

Shen Lingjiang kept her head down as she reached out. With a few deft movements, she untied the sash and draped it over a nearby rack, then proceeded to remove Xie Yunzhou’s outer robe.

She was a head shorter than Xie Yunzhou, and due to her frail health, she had a thin, slight frame. Pressed against his chest, she looked like a newly grown, tender bamboo shoot, while Xie Yunzhou was like a sturdy, towering pine, his branches spreading out to completely shield the little bamboo.

Xie Yunzhou was making things difficult for her on purpose.

He always felt that this hostage princess wore a mask, and on that mask was a face that maintained a gentle smile at all times, a smile so fake that it made him want to take a knife and pierce it, to shred it.

He always wanted to see her mask crack, to see her unable to smile.

But Shen Lingjiang was like a piece of soft dough; no matter how he toyed with or kneaded her, she would never get angry or lose her temper. Just like now, she still wore that smile, dutifully undressing him, doing whatever she was told without a single complaint.

Xie Yunzhou glanced down and happened to see the bleeding scar on her temple and the redness on her forehead, the former caused by He Weishi’s wine cup, the latter from when she had bumped her head on the carriage seat.

How delicate; it swelled up from just one bump.

Xie Yunzhou’s thoughts wandered until he felt a chill on his skin. The noble Prince Regent finally snapped back to reality, only to realize he had been stripped bare by this thief-woman from the enemy state.

Shen Lingjiang blinked, staring straight at his exposed, naked upper body without blushing or skipping a beat. Her eyes scanned him from top to bottom, first the broad, thick shoulders and back, then the lean, sturdy waist. The muscle lines were fluid, and there were many healed knife scars and arrow wounds on his back, shoulders, and abdomen, crawling across his skin quite prominently.

She looked for a long moment, then curved her lips into a smile at Xie Yunzhou and asked, "Your Highness, please condescend to lift your leg."

Xie Yunzhou glared at her, then looked down to see that Shen Lingjiang was still holding the drawstring of his underpants.

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

"Shameless!" Xie Yunzhou snapped at her, snatched his waistband back from her hand, and stepped directly into the wooden tub.

Shen Lingjiang acted as if she hadn't heard him. She smiled and moved closer, using a wooden ladle to scoop water to rinse Xie Yunzhou’s hair, even asking, "It is Shen Lingjiang who is ignorant. In Great Liang, do people bathe while wearing their trousers?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou was struck dumb, but Shen Lingjiang continued, "Your Highness? Would you like me to add some flower petals for you?"

Xie Yunzhou: "?"

He thought he had misheard. He frowned, turned his head to glare at Shen Lingjiang, and exclaimed in disbelief, "What?"

Shen Lingjiang tilted her head toward him, her tone laced with a hint of amusement, "You require service even for bathing, just like a pampered, precious young nobleman. They all seem to love petal baths, wanting their skin to be fragrant. I thought you might like it too."

Xie Yunzhou narrowed his eyes, watching her gloomily without a word.

Shen Lingjiang didn't think much of it and turned to grab the incense pellets from the rack. But just as she turned, a powerful hand clamped onto her arm, and the next moment, she was dragged into the tub.

"Ah!"

She gasped, the wooden ladle slipping from her hand. Xie Yunzhou pressed her under the water, and she struggled, unable to escape.

Xie Yunzhou’s expression darkened. His hand, with its bulging veins, pressed down on the top of Shen Lingjiang’s head, holding her underwater for a breath before letting her go.

"Sharp-tongued. If you cannot learn how to speak, then this Prince will wash your mouth out for you."

Shen Lingjiang grabbed Xie Yunzhou’s arm to pull herself out of the water, one hand pressed to her chest. She coughed violently from inhaling water, her face turning even paler, her hair and clothes completely soaked.

She was already extremely thin; with her clothes soaked, the flimsy fabric clung to her skin, making her shoulders look even narrower and her waist even thinner. At a glance, she looked like a frame of gaunt bones.

Such a thin waist; he could snap it with one hand.

She was weak, indeed, but her mouth was quite formidable.

Shen Lingjiang retreated slightly, leaning against the edge of the tub, coughing as she said, "Cough, cough... You flatter me, you flatter me. My imperial sister is far more eloquent than I am."

Xie Yunzhou glared at her and said bluntly, "You? You think you are worthy of being compared to Shangguan Ying?"

Not knowing what she thought of, Shen Lingjiang actually laughed out loud, finally nodding as she added, "Your Highness is quite right. Shen Lingjiang is foolish; how could I compare to the Third Imperial Princess?"

Having said that, she paused for a moment, then suddenly looked up, smiling even more brightly at Xie Yunzhou.

A transparent drop of water rolled down her sharply defined brow, dripped slowly onto her slightly curved lips, and then fell further, instantly sliding down her chin into the water.

Soaked to the bone, her features stained with dampness, she remained there, smiling motionlessly, like a scroll of ink painting touched by moisture. Her affectionate eyes were enough to stir anyone’s heart.

Xie Yunzhou’s heart stirred for only a moment before the feeling was shattered by Shen Lingjiang’s next words, his expression suddenly turning dark and cold.

Shen Lingjiang asked, "My Third Imperial Sister is famous far and wide, but I wonder, how does she compare to the late Crown Prince of your noble country?"

The late Crown Prince. The late Crown Prince.

He was the legitimate son of the late Emperor, a renowned and virtuous prince of Great Liang, beloved by the entire nation. Yet, such a Crown Prince died under the brutal iron cavalry and blades of Great Chu.

It was said that Xie Yunzhou had been raised by his elder brother and was very close to the late Crown Prince. After the Prince died, he supported his brother’s only son to ascend the throne as Emperor.

chapters.title: Seeking a Way to Survive
chapters.content:
Hearing Shen Lingjiang mention his long-dead brother, Xie Yunzhou was so angry he wanted to strangle her on the spot. He endured and endured, finally just scooping up a handful of water and splashing it at Shen Lingjiang, then roaring, "Get out!"

Shen Lingjiang remained silent for a moment, then quietly climbed out of the tub and walked out of the bathroom in her wet clothes.

As soon as she opened the door, the cold night wind made her instinctively wrap her arms around herself. The bone-chilling cold bit into her, not to mention she was still wearing wet clothes.

Luo Yangming was guarding the door. Seeing her in such a wretched state, he revealed a mocking smile and sneered, "Did you really think the Prince kept you in the manor because he was infatuated with your beauty?"

Shen Lingjiang said nothing and no longer smiled, just looked at him calmly while hugging her shoulders.

Luo Yangming continued, "The Prince brought you back just so you could go to the ancestral hall and copy the reports of victory. They are all to be burned for the brothers underground. You must copy twenty of them; there are many brothers below, and I fear it won't be enough if there are too few!"

At this point, a trace of mockery leaked from the corners of Luo Yangming’s lips as he gloated, "The reports of victory copied by the princess of an enemy state and burned for them; they will surely find it satisfying."

Having said that, he pointed to a servant standing by a pillar and shouted, "A-Wu, take her to the ancestral hall. Don't let her out until she has finished twenty copies... Hmm, take her to change into some clean clothes first. A princess is delicate; don't let her freeze to death in the ancestral hall before the reports are finished, that would be bad luck!"

Halfway through, he seemed to realize Shen Lingjiang’s pale complexion with a delay, and after a moment of hesitation, he still told the servant to take her to change.

It was meant to be a kindness, but the words he spoke were sharp and mean.

Shen Lingjiang coughed, lowered her eyes toward Luo Yangming, and said in a low voice, "Thank you, General."

Luo Yangming paused, then gave her one last cold glare before flicking his sleeves and leaving.

Shen Lingjiang followed the servant to change her clothes and was then led to the ancestral hall.

Ancestral halls were for worshipping ancestors. Xie Yunzhou was of royal blood, and there shouldn't have been an ancestral hall in the Prince’s manor, yet he had built one, and it was quite large.

Shen Lingjiang was led through the door. Upon entering, she saw bronze lamp stands as tall as a person standing every five steps along the walls, with thousands of bright candles reflecting a warm glow on the floor.

Looking into the spacious hall, the left, right, top, and bottom were filled with black wooden spirit tablets. Shen Lingjiang stepped closer to look.

Spirit tablet of Jiang Huizhi, Eastern Route Assistant General.Spirit tablet of Lu Tongguang, Yan Territory Garrison.Spirit tablet of Li Zhiyao, Cavalry Captain....

Further down, the tablets were no longer large enough to hold just one person's name, gradually becoming things like "Spirit tablet of the eighteen sons of Yunjia Village, Liangshui Town, Baiyong City" and "Spirit tablet of the three hundred and twenty-six men of the Ninth Division who raided West Pavilion Mountain."

Shen Lingjiang held a candle stand and looked at them one by one. Finally, she took the victory reports and walked slowly to a small desk at the back, sat down, spread the paper, ground the ink, and began to copy.

The ancestral hall was empty and silent, accompanied only by thousands of flickering candle flames and countless pitch-black spirit tablets.

It was only twenty reports. Shen Lingjiang wasn't good at much, but she was quite skilled at copying books and writing. However, staying up all night with the lamps burning, how could her frail body withstand it? By the second half of the night, she began to feel lightheaded, her handwriting became sloppy, and golden spots danced before her eyes.

...Cannot sleep. Cannot faint.

If she passed out now, Xie Yunzhou would surely have her thrown back to the Hostage Princess’s residence, and she would never be able to come out again.

How could she let herself be trapped to death in that remote mansion!

Shen Lingjiang took a deep breath, set down her brush, and stared fixedly at the bronze lamp stand on the desk, where the candle wick was popping and curling. The flame burned and danced before her eyes.

She watched for a few moments, then suddenly stretched out her left hand, her fingers reaching toward the flame.

"Hiss... Mmm."

With a muffled groan, Shen Lingjiang pulled her hand back in pain. She frowned, pressed her palm, and stared fixedly at the fingers that had been singed by the candle flame, suddenly letting out two laughs.

She was laughing with her mouth, but her eyes were filled with coldness.

Having endured the pain, she suddenly became clear-headed.

After calming down for a moment, she picked up the brush and continued copying.

She didn't know how much longer she had been copying when she saw the sky turning a pale fish-belly white, with daylight gradually appearing.

Shen Lingjiang took a breath, used the candlelight to warm her frozen hands, and after warming them for a while, she stood up, rubbing her sore, numb legs. She rolled up the stack of rice paper on the desk and walked toward the exit.

The servant who had led her in was still guarding outside the ancestral hall. He didn't speak when she came out, only nodding slightly toward her.

"Where is the Prince Regent?"

The servant did not answer, only bowed to her and held out both hands, "Your Highness, just give them to me once you have finished copying."

Seeing he wouldn't answer, Shen Lingjiang naturally didn't want to let go, so she tucked the stack of rice paper under her arm and walked out.

Just as she walked out of the long corridor, she saw Li Wanli and Luo Yangming rushing past from the front.

Li Wanli was saying as he walked, "There still aren't enough laborers for the canal! And not enough money! The Ministry of Revenue cries poverty every day. If it drags on like this, I’m afraid it won't be finished in ten or eight years! Our Prince really picked a fine task! This is much harder than fighting a war!"

Luo Yangming also said, "Most of the court doesn't support building the canal, with the Marquis of Jing'an at the head of them. If it drags on because of manpower and money, I fear the opposition will only grow louder!"

...The canal?

The Yuan River Canal!

Shen Lingjiang’s eyes lit up. She hurried over with the papers, blocked their path, and asked, "Generals, please stay! Are you two speaking of the Yuan River Canal?"

The Yuan River Canal was a project championed by Xie Yunzhou. It started from Tao County in Baiyong and led all the way to Yunqin in the far east. Yunqin was a strong and wealthy commercial nation that had friendly relations with Great Liang. The two countries had just established trade last year, and the Yuan River Canal was being built to facilitate that trade.

Great Liang was divided into five provinces: Shangbei, Baiyong, Longxi, Dongpu, and Yan. The capital, Yandu, was in Shangbei, making it the first province, while the second province, Baiyong, was the most prosperous, with its capital in Tao County.

When Luo Yangming heard Shen Lingjiang’s question, he was still wary of her status as an enemy princess and stared at her vigilantly without answering.

But Li Wanli looked like a big, simple-minded man. Without thinking, he blurted out, "It is the Yuan River Canal! Why? Have you heard of our Prince building the canal even in Great Chu?"

Luo Yangming rolled his eyes and then glared fiercely at Li Wanli.

The big fool realized he had said the wrong thing. He scratched his head and didn't ask further, intending to step around Shen Lingjiang and continue walking.

The canal matter was urgent, and they were in a hurry to report to the Prince Regent.

Just as the two took a step, Shen Lingjiang immediately said, "Manpower, money... I have ways for both. I just don't know if I might have the opportunity to offer a strategy to the Prince?"

Offer a strategy?

Li Wanli scratched his head and pouted, "What strategy? What way could you possibly have?"

Shen Lingjiang smiled slowly and said calmly, "That must be told to the Prince."

Luo Yangming lowered his eyes, thinking silently for a moment, and finally slapped his palm to seal the deal, "Fine! We’ll take you to see him! If you dare to play me, I don't care if you are a princess or not!"

As he spoke, he patted the long sword he was carrying.

With the matter settled, Shen Lingjiang followed the two men toward the Prince’s study.

chapters.title: Offering a Sound Strategy
chapters.content:
Upon reaching the door, Li Wanli and Luo Yangming did not let Shen Lingjiang enter directly. They merely stated that they had to report to the Prince first, and she could only enter once he gave his consent.

Shen Lingjiang nodded in agreement and stood quietly at the doorway, gazing into the distance at birds flying over the treetops.

A short while later, Luo Yangming opened the door. Without a word, he gestured toward her with his chin, then stepped aside to clear the path, signaling for Shen Lingjiang to enter.

"Many thanks."

Shen Lingjiang whispered to him before stepping inside.

Xie Yunzhou was a military man; even in the dead of winter, he had no habit of lighting a charcoal brazier in his room. However, with the doors and windows tightly shut, it was still much warmer than outside. As soon as she entered, the sudden warmth made Shen Lingjiang cough twice, leaving her complexion even paler than before.

Xie Yunzhou sat in a chair, holding a dark yellow silk-bound booklet in his hands. It was a proposal submitted by the Ministry of Works regarding the construction of the canal. He was halfway through reading it when Luo Yangming and Li Wanli had come to report the matter.

"Seventh Princess, you are quite busy, aren't you? Even while finding time to transcribe military dispatches for this Prince, you still have the leisure to ponder the canal?"

Shen Lingjiang was still coughing. She covered her mouth and nose, bowing her head as she coughed heavily several times.

Xie Yunzhou frowned as he watched, his expression a mix of disdain and concern.

A moment later, he spoke to Li Wanli: "Have someone bring in a charcoal brazier, and get her a chair."

Li Wanli nodded obediently, brought a chair for Shen Lingjiang, and then hurried out to instruct the servants to prepare the brazier.

Shen Lingjiang sat down and said softly, "Thank you, Your Highness."

Xie Yunzhou asked again, "Are you finished copying?"

Shen Lingjiang nodded and handed over the stack of rice paper she had been holding. Luo Yangming stepped forward to take it and delivered it to Xie Yunzhou.

Xie Yunzhou flipped through a couple of pages, and his brow finally relaxed slightly.

If nothing else, Shen Lingjiang’s calligraphy was truly excellent.

Though she was sickly, thin, and frail, her brushwork was strong and elegant, full of character.

Xie Yunzhou sighed softly, handed the papers back to Luo Yangming, and said in a low voice, "Yangming, take these to the ancestral hall and burn them. They... have long been anxious to know this news."

Luo Yangming’s eyes reddened. He nodded heavily, gathered the papers, and strode out the door.

With both lieutenants gone, only Xie Yunzhou and Shen Lingjiang remained in the room.

Xie Yunzhou set aside the booklet, took a sip of tea, and asked, "Regarding the canal, what solution do you have?"

Shen Lingjiang looked into his eyes and uttered two words, one by one: "Conscript labor."

Xie Yunzhou’s movements froze. Then, with a slap, he slammed his teacup onto the table. He glared fiercely at Shen Lingjiang and demanded, "This is your 'good' solution?"

"Forcing labor and imposing heavy taxes has always been the act of a tyrant!"

Just as he finished speaking, two servants entered carrying a copper brazier filled with burning charcoal. They moved with light steps, placed the brazier down quietly, and bowed their way out.

Feeling the warmth, Shen Lingjiang let out a sigh of relief. She leaned forward and stretched her hands out toward the fire to warm them.

While warming her hands, she stared at the brazier and suddenly asked, "This is 'Rui' charcoal, isn't it?"

Xie Yunzhou’s brow remained furrowed. He looked at her in confusion, seemingly unable to understand why she would bring this up out of the blue.

Shen Lingjiang did not look at him, continuing, "I have heard that this 'Rui' charcoal is a tribute item, with only two hundred pieces offered each year. In all of Great Liang, aside from the palace, I fear only Your Highness has the means to use such fine charcoal. Each piece is over a foot long, hard as iron, and can burn for ten days. It is smokeless and odorless, emitting only heat. Such charcoal is worth its weight in gold."

Xie Yunzhou frowned. "What exactly are you trying to say?"

Shen Lingjiang sighed and finally looked up at Xie Yunzhou. "Your Highness, you were born into the royal family. Even if your household does not indulge in luxury, how could you know the value of money? Outside this city of Yandu, in small towns and villages, there are countless poor people who cannot afford food or clothing. Such people are in dire need of money."

Xie Yunzhou nodded, seemingly understanding, but his brow remained unrelaxed.

He glared at Shen Lingjiang again and continued, "Are you suggesting we pay the laborers? If they are paid to work, naturally there will be no complaints?"

"That is the logic. But besides the shortage of manpower, there is the shortage of funds. The Ministry of Revenue cries poverty, claiming they cannot even find the money to build the canal. Where would the money to pay the laborers come from?"

Shen Lingjiang coughed twice more, looked up at him with a pale face, and asked, "Your Highness, why are you building this canal?"

Xie Yunzhou looked down at her. Seeing her pale complexion, like snow in the dead of winter, and her hands held over the brazier, her sleeves falling back to reveal slender, porcelain-white wrists and the faint blue veins on the back of her hands, he watched her for a long time before blinking and answering, "To trade with Yunqin and open up foreign commerce."

Hearing his answer, Shen Lingjiang nodded and continued, "Despite the hardships, Great Liang is generally prosperous. Especially in Baiyong, where there are the most merchants, and the richest man in the land has his home in Tao County. The canal has just begun construction; others may not see the brilliance in it yet, but those who trade are the most astute when it comes to money. They will certainly understand immediately."

"The people are poor, but the merchants are wealthy. There are thousands of rich merchants across the country. One only needs to declare that those who donate money to build the canal will have merit to the state and be granted priority for foreign trade. Baiyong is wealthy, but it is far from Yunqin. They must be impatient to wait for this 'River of Wealth.' Those who trade with the outside world first will be the first to secure trade agreements with the people of Yunqin, naturally gaining a greater advantage than those who come later."

"Shen Lingjiang is short-sighted, but I know that Yunqin has many foreign vegetables, spices, gemstones, leathers, and fine horses that Great Liang lacks. To merchants, these are all business opportunities."

She had spoken a great deal, leaving her lips dry and her face deathly pale.

Xie Yunzhou watched her intently, his face devoid of much emotion, his lips slightly pursed.

After staring for a long while, he suddenly stood up, poured a cup of tea himself, walked over to Shen Lingjiang, and handed it to her. His tone was a mix of mockery and teasing: "You have a bit of cleverness, at least."

Shen Lingjiang stood up, about to take the tea.

However, she had stayed up all night, her spirit was exhausted, and she was already plagued by illness. Whether it was because she stood up too quickly or something else, the moment she rose, she felt the world spinning and pitched forward.

The hot tea in Xie Yunzhou’s hand spilled, and he instinctively caught Shen Lingjiang as she collapsed into his arms.

"...What are you doing? Shen Lingjiang, is your heart still set on schemes? You just said a few nice words, and now you’re throwing yourself at me?"

Xie Yunzhou had just finished grumbling when his hand inadvertently brushed the back of Shen Lingjiang’s hand. It was cold as ice.

She was sitting right by the fire, how could she be this cold?!

Xie Yunzhou’s expression turned sharp. He immediately reached for her face and lifted her drooping head.

"Shen Lingjiang? Shen Lingjiang? Wake up."

Of course, she did not wake up. She was completely unconscious, her brow still furrowed. The injuries on her forehead and temples from yesterday had not been treated; the swelling was worse, and while the small cuts on her hairline had stopped bleeding, the blood had dried on her skin.

Xie Yunzhou sighed, suddenly scooped her up, and walked out.

chapters.title: The Fever of Illness
chapters.content:
Luo Yangming and Li Wanli were dutifully guarding the door.

Li Wanli was a chatterbox; his mouth never rested for a moment. Luo Yangming, on the other hand, frowned with his eyes closed, turning his head away, looking thoroughly annoyed.

"Hey, do you think that hostage princess really has a way? Can she really solve the canal issue? Wow, that would be truly impressive!"

"Tsk... I really didn't expect it. Is the Ministry of Revenue really that poor? I went to see that old man this morning, and he said the wars have already emptied the national treasury!"

"Hey! I'm talking to you! Make a sound! What do you think our Prince and that person are talking about inside? Sigh, she is indeed beautiful. Do you think our Prince might actually..."

Before he could finish muttering, the study door was kicked open.

His Prince walked out in a rush, holding the sickly hostage princess in his arms. She was even covered in a black fox-fur cloak.

Li Wanli recognized that cloak; it was his Prince’s garment, extremely precious, but so thick and cumbersome that the Prince had never worn it once.

He gasped in shock.

Luo Yangming opened his eyes, staring wide-eyed at Xie Yunzhou and the Shen Lingjiang in his arms. After a long while, he said in disbelief, "So she actually succeeded?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou felt that with these two talented men following him, it was a miracle he had ever won a battle.

The Prince immediately pulled a long face. He glanced at Luo Yangming and said with forced patience, "She fainted. It’s an emergency... examine her."

Finally, he turned to Li Wanli and asked, "Where is that little servant of hers?"

Li Wanli paused for a moment, then immediately replied, "Still outside! That girl is quite loyal; she’s been guarding the door the whole time, not daring to leave."

Xie Yunzhou nodded and said, "Call her in. Tell her her mistress is ill and have her come in to serve."

With that, he carried her away.

Li Wanli slapped his forehead and turned to go find the girl.

Luo Yangming followed closely behind Xie Yunzhou, anxiously asking, "Where is Your Highness taking her? Wouldn't it be better if I instructed the servants to prepare a guest room?"

Xie Yunzhou kept walking without slowing his pace. "There’s no time. Treat her illness first, lest she actually die in my manor."

And so, Luo Yangming watched as his Prince carried her back to the main courtyard, entered the main bedroom, and carefully placed the unconscious woman on the bed.

He gritted his teeth and muttered, "She really did succeed!"

Xie Yunzhou shot him a sharp glare and scolded, "What are you muttering about! Get over here!"

Luo Yangming curled his lip, walked over, knelt on the footstool by the bed, and reached out to take Shen Lingjiang’s pulse.

It was worth noting that Luo Yangming, despite his cold and poisonous nature, was a rare, all-around talent. He was skilled in both literature and martial arts, knew medicine, and even understood a bit about disguise and ancient tactical formations.

As soon as his hand touched her pulse, he closed his eyes for a moment, then frowned.

Xie Yunzhou asked coolly, "Well?"
