Luo Yangming opened his eyes and withdrew his hand. He replied in a low voice, "She is riddled with illnesses. It’s hard to say which is the most severe, but there isn't a healthy part of her. She will never be able to live without medicine for the rest of her life. Oh, and even with medicine, she might not live for many more years."

Having said this, Luo Yangming’s expression softened, and his gaze toward Shen Lingjiang was less harsh than before.

A dying person, a discarded pawn thrown out by Great Chu; she was pitiful, after all.

Xie Yunzhou’s pupils contracted slightly, as if shocked.

But in the end, he said nothing and just quietly turned to look at Shen Lingjiang.

Luo Yangming continued to mutter with a sigh, "I heard she is of humble birth. She probably wasn't favored in the Chu royal family and hasn't had an easy life."

Xie Yunzhou remained silent, sitting by the bed and watching quietly.

"...Cold."

Shen Lingjiang, unconscious on the bed, murmured softly.

Xie Yunzhou looked at her, reached out, and pulled the black fox-fur cloak up to her chin.

The cloak was massive, wide, thick, and warm; one piece could cover a person entirely. Shen Lingjiang curled up under the cloak, her hands tightly gripping the fluffy black fur. Her face was turned slightly, and the ink-black fur made her skin look even whiter.

"Do what you must, force-feed her medicine or use needles. Just don't let her die."

Xie Yunzhou withdrew his gaze and stood up to leave.

Suddenly, he heard another faint murmur from the person on the bed.

She was wrapped up like a bear, and she was still cold?

Xie Yunzhou’s brow knotted in frustration. He turned his head impatiently, leaning in to hear what she was saying.

Curled under the black cloak, Shen Lingjiang muttered a few times before uttering a clearer word. It sounded like a name.

"...A-Man."

A-Man?

Calling someone else’s name while delirious?

Xie Yunzhou stood stunned for a moment, just as Ruyi came rushing in.

"This servant greets the Prince Regent!"

The little servant bowed to Xie Yunzhou, but her eyes were fixed on Shen Lingjiang on the bed, anxious as an ant on a hot pan.

Xie Yunzhou said nothing, waved his hand dismissively, and strode out of the room.

After he left, Ruyi finally let out a breath and rushed to the bedside, wanting to touch Shen Lingjiang’s forehead to check her temperature, but fearing that the cold air on her own body would make Shen Lingjiang’s illness worse.

Quite loyal, indeed.

Luo Yangming, who had been sour-faced the whole time, softened his tone and said to Ruyi, "She just caught a chill. After taking medicine and resting for two days, she will be fine."

My mistress was perfectly fine yesterday! How did she catch a chill after just one night in the Prince’s manor!

Easy for you to say, but my mistress is already frail. She’s fainted, who knows how much she’s suffered!

Ruyi pouted, cursing silently in her heart.

But she only dared to curse in her heart. This was Yandu, Great Liang, the Prince Regent’s manor; it was not her place to speak.

Ruyi pouted, her eyes red, and muttered reluctantly, "Thank you for treating my mistress."

Luo Yangming raised an eyebrow. He thought this girl was quite bold; while her words were thankful, her eyes looked like they wanted to carve him up.

Then again, Ruyi was young; it was impressive enough that she was holding back her tongue. Her eyes, however, could not hide her feelings.

Luo Yangming shrugged noncommittally and left the room.

Once everyone was gone, Ruyi dragged the charcoal brazier to the bedside and diligently changed the damp cloth on Shen Lingjiang’s forehead.

As she worked, she muttered to herself.

"Mistress, how are you feeling?"

"You must be hungry since you've been unconscious, please don't let your stomach trouble flare up again."

"Why are we so unlucky! Doesn't Great Liang call itself a land of etiquette? Why are they all so unreasonable, like savages!"

chapters.title: Inviting a Companion
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang slept for two days. During this time, the Prince’s attendants moved her to a prepared guest room, keeping Ruyi by her side to care for her, along with a young maid to brew her medicine.

Her bones felt as if they were turning to mush from lying down so long. Only then did she struggle to open her eyes, rubbing her sore, dry lids.

The moment she opened her eyes, she saw Ruyi dozing off by the bedside. Shen Lingjiang frowned, patted the back of her hand, and whispered, "Ruyi."

Having been ill for two days and consuming only liquid food, her throat felt parched and raw, as if stuffed with a handful of dry hay.

Ruyi jolted awake. Her eyes brightened when she saw Shen Lingjiang, and she cried out excitedly, "Your Highness! You’re awake! You scared me to death!"

Shen Lingjiang frowned, bracing herself on the bed with one hand. She scanned the room’s furnishings with a grave expression and gripped Ruyi’s wrist, asking, "Where is this?"

Her voice remained hoarse. Ruyi immediately turned and ran to the table, poured a cup of hot water from the kettle on the wind stove, and hurried back.

As she helped Shen Lingjiang drink half the cup, she explained, "We are at the Prince Regent’s mansion. Don’t worry, Your Highness, they haven’t locked us back in the Residence of Hostages!"

Shen Lingjiang finally let out a sigh of relief and finished the rest of the water.

Ruyi set the cup down, leaned over to touch Shen Lingjiang’s forehead, and exclaimed in surprise, "The fever is gone! It seems that 'Ice-Face's' medicine is quite effective!"

Shen Lingjiang: "…Ice-Face?"

Ruyi pouted and muttered, "You know, that general by the Prince Regent’s side who is always clutching his sword and wearing a cold, sour face!"

She was referring to Luo Yangming.

Shen Lingjiang chuckled softly, tapped Ruyi on the head, and scolded, "Say that in front of me if you must, but don't go saying it outside."

Ruyi hurriedly covered her forehead and shook her head repeatedly, muttering, "I wouldn't dare! He’s so fierce, always fiddling with that broken sword of his! I wouldn't dare!"

Just as she spoke, the chirping of birds sounded outside the window. Looking over, she saw a few grey-feathered sparrows.

Seeing them, Ruyi giggled, ran out to scatter some birdseed, and turned back to explain to Shen Lingjiang with a smile, "Your Highness! I fed them just like you did yesterday, I didn't expect them to come back today!"

As she spoke, Ruyi saw a man in black brocade robes walking along the path in the distance.

She shrank back in fear, immediately dropped the birdseed, and scrambled back to Shen Lingjiang’s side.

Shen Lingjiang tilted her head and asked softly, "What’s wrong?"

At the mere sight of the figure, Ruyi’s eyes turned red with fright, and she stammered, unable to speak.

Before she could say anything, the guest room door was pushed open, and Xie Yunzhou, dressed in black, stepped over the threshold.

He was carrying a bowl of medicine, steam rising from it.

Xie Yunzhou walked quickly to the bed and thrust the bowl toward Shen Lingjiang’s face.

"Your medicine for today."

Shen Lingjiang paused, then took the bowl with a smile.

It was a bowl of pitch-black, bitter broth. She drank it all in one breath without blinking, then handed the empty bowl to Ruyi.

After finishing the medicine, she looked up at Xie Yunzhou and smiled, saying as if casually, "The Prince and I truly share a heart; I’ve only just woken up, and you are already here?"

It was, of course, impossible to share a heart.

Xie Yunzhou understood the sarcasm; she was implying he had sent people to monitor her.

But Xie Yunzhou was uncharacteristically easygoing today. He pulled back his robes, sat on the low stool by the bed, and stared at Shen Lingjiang, asking, "How do you feel? Any better?"

This was strange; he was actually inquiring after her health.

Shen Lingjiang paused, then asked directly, "Does the Prince have something to ask of me?"

Caught in the act, Xie Yunzhou looked slightly awkward. He coughed, turned his head away, and said, "It’s about the canal. I heard that when the construction reached Jingtai, something went wrong, and work has been delayed for half a month."

Shen Lingjiang nodded. She gave Ruyi a look, signaling her to leave.

Once they were alone, she asked, "Does the Prince intend to go and see for yourself?"

Xie Yunzhou nodded, stating briefly, "Yes. I have already submitted a memorial to His Majesty and will be departing for Jingtai immediately."

Shen Lingjiang asked again, "And you must take me along?"

Xie Yunzhou paused, then turned his head away, looking slightly uncomfortable. "You seem to have a bit of cleverness; I thought it might come in handy."

Shen Lingjiang chuckled and couldn't help but ask, "A hostage from an enemy state, does the Prince dare to use her?"

Hearing this, Xie Yunzhou turned back to look at her. He leaned forward, stared into her eyes, and said word for word, "You are just a hostage. If you don't behave, I will kill you... what could the Great Chu possibly say?"

Xie Yunzhou was a general of war and slaughter; at this moment, a fierce, chilling light erupted in his eyes, like a wolf with green eyes.

Shen Lingjiang looked away, her smile fading. She only said, "My dirty blood would not dare to stain the Prince’s blade."

Xie Yunzhou stared at her for a long moment before rising to leave, leaving behind one sentence:

"Rest up. We leave for Jingtai in a few days."

A few days later, Shen Lingjiang’s health had improved significantly. She no longer felt constantly exhausted and even had the strength to walk around the courtyard.

The weather was beautiful that day, a warm winter sun casting a faint red glow over the trees and grass in the courtyard.

Xie Yunzhou dragged Shen Lingjiang out early. Tied outside the side gate were a chestnut horse and a pitch-black stallion.

"Longmei!" Xie Yunzhou whistled at the black horse. The next moment, the horse let out a long neigh and stomped its hooves at him.

Xie Yunzhou laughed heartily, walked over to stroke the horse’s mane, and fed it some fresh fodder.

Ruyi followed, taking small steps behind Shen Lingjiang. She tugged at her sleeve and whispered, "Your Highness, it seems the Prince Regent only knows how to fight and not how to read. Such a handsome horse, and he actually named it 'Longmei' [Dragon Sister]!"

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

She had spoken in a whisper, fearing Xie Yunzhou would hear. But Xie Yunzhou was a martial artist with exceptional hearing; he heard every word clearly without even trying.

Even Xie Yunzhou fell silent. He frowned, wanting to scold her, but she was just a young servant, and it wasn't worth getting angry over.

Shen Lingjiang couldn't help but burst into laughter. Seeing Xie Yunzhou’s expression darken further, she quickly praised, "A heavenly horse, a match for a dragon; this is truly a magnificent steed."

The horse was smart; it seemed to understand, snorted at Ruyi, and puckered its lips as if to nibble her arm.

Ruyi was terrified and scrambled to hide behind Shen Lingjiang.

Seeing this, Xie Yunzhou’s anger vanished, and he laughed heartily.

At this moment, Li Wanli and Luo Yangming rode up on their horses.

Li Wanli reined in his horse and asked bluntly, "Prince, haven't you mounted yet? Let’s go! Jingtai is far! Hey, little girl, can you ride? If not, get up here, I'll give you a lift!"

He teased Xie Yunzhou first, then waved at Ruyi.

Ruyi naturally couldn't ride. She clutched Shen Lingjiang’s sleeve in fear and looked at her. After receiving a nod, she let go and moved forward with small steps, trying to touch the tall horse to get familiar with it. Before she could reach out, Li Wanli bent down and scooped her onto the horse’s back.

"Prince! Yangming and I will go ahead to clear the path! Giddyap!"

With that, Li Wanli flicked his whip, squeezed the horse’s flanks, and galloped away.

Luo Yangming nodded at Xie Yunzhou and followed.

Xie Yunzhou muttered to himself, "Clear the path? They think they're still in the army."

He turned to look at Shen Lingjiang and asked, "Can you ride?"

Shen Lingjiang: "I suppose... I know a little."

chapters.title: Riding Together
chapters.content:
"I know a little"; Shen Lingjiang was being very modest.

Then, Xie Yunzhou watched as she fumbled and climbed onto the horse's back, held her breath in tension, gripped the reins, and flicked the whip.

In the end, the chestnut horse took two reluctant steps and then simply stopped in the middle of the road, twisting its mouth to chew on a branch extending from the eaves of the courtyard.

Shen Lingjiang, who always wore a smile, finally felt quite embarrassed. She patted the horse’s back and whispered, "Move... stop eating, there's nothing good about a dead branch."

It clearly didn't taste good; the horse sneezed and spat out the dead leaves.

The slight jolting nearly threw Shen Lingjiang off the horse.

Startled, she immediately leaned forward, hugging the horse's neck, gripping the reins and mane tightly.

Xie Yunzhou mounted his horse, rode over, scanned her up and down, and laughed deliberately: "You know a little?"

Shen Lingjiang answered honestly: "I really do know a little; I know how to get on the horse, at least."

Xie Yunzhou mocked: "That was crawling."

Shen Lingjiang: "...The Prince doesn't need to be so detailed."

After she spoke, she tugged at the reins again, but the horse wouldn't listen, stiffening its neck and refusing to move, stubborn as an ox.

Xie Yunzhou watched for a moment, finally losing patience.

He pulled his reins, rode close, and with one long arm, scooped Shen Lingjiang off the chestnut horse and onto his own.

Xie Yunzhou sneered, "If you ride like that, it’ll take half a year to reach Jingtai."

Shen Lingjiang: "...The Prince is exaggerating. Even walking wouldn't be that slow."

Shen Lingjiang was still wearing her thick, oversized ink-colored fox-fur cloak. Being scooped onto the horse to sit facing him, she bumped against Xie Yunzhou’s chest as the horse jolted.

Those who practiced martial arts were different; hitting his chest felt like hitting a rock, hard and painful.

Shen Lingjiang clutched her forehead, leaning back to put some distance between them.

She said, "Prince, how about a compromise? Let me turn around."

Xie Yunzhou didn't agree. Instead, he reached out with one hand, pulled the fur-lined hood over Shen Lingjiang’s head, and wrapped her up tightly.

"Facing the wind like that with your sickly constitution, you’d have your soul blown away before we reached Jingtai. You don't expect me to wait in Jingtai while you recover, do you? I don't have that kind of time."

Shen Lingjiang: "...The Prince is indeed very thorough."

Xie Yunzhou acted as if he hadn't heard the sarcasm in her voice. He flicked the reins, pressed his legs against the horse’s flanks, and gave a light lash of the whip.

The horse let out a long neigh and galloped away.

Shen Lingjiang, who had just tried to pull away, was jolted back against him, her cheek hitting his chest. She was so close she could hear the powerful heartbeat within his chest.

They galloped all the way, leaving Yandu and taking the main road, rushing toward Jingtai without stopping from dawn until dusk.

The stars and moon were beautiful that night. The bright moon hung in the sky, and the stars were brilliant, casting a silver-white light over the wide road.

Outside the Jingtai post station.

Two horses stopped by a tree, and a small, frail figure was leaning against the trunk, retching violently.

Luo Yangming stood to the side, arms crossed, clutching his sword, muttering with disdain, "She's too weak. We haven't been traveling that long, and she's already vomiting like this."

Li Wanli glared at him and reached out to pat Ruyi’s back. "Stop with the snide remarks. How old is this girl?"

Luo Yangming rolled his eyes at the sky and glared at Li Wanli. "Fifteen or sixteen. When I was that age, I was already leading a small team to raid Narrow Cloud Ridge. Li Wanli, get this straight; this isn't your sister! Your sister is still locked away in the Imperial Academy studying hard!"

Li Wanli was choked into silence. His sister was a student at the Imperial Academy, and he was a soldier, but his sister had been frail since birth, born with a frame so thin she could be blown away by the wind. She was timid, too, and would blush and tremble if she spoke too much to strangers.

Ruyi was even younger than his sister, and her personality was similar. Seeing her, Li Wanli couldn't help but think of his own sister.

Seeing Li Wanli fall silent, Luo Yangming felt he had won the argument. His mood improved, and he took a small white porcelain jar from his pocket and tossed it to Li Wanli, saying generously, "Anti-nausea medicine. Let her try it."

Just as he finished, a black-maned, black-tailed horse galloped onto the road, carrying two people.

Seeing the two pressed together, Li Wanli and Luo Yangming were stunned, their eyes nearly popping out. The porcelain jar almost fell to the ground.

Li Wanli: "I think I'm blind. Help me look, is that our Prince?"

Luo Yangming: "Who? I don't see anyone. I must be blind too."

Before they could say more, Xie Yunzhou had ridden close. He jumped off the horse and lifted Shen Lingjiang down as well.

Li Wanli’s face crumpled in confusion. "Prince, did all the horses in our mansion die?" Why did they have to ride one?

Luo Yangming was even more devastated, looking at Xie Yunzhou as if he were a master bewitched by beauty: "Prince! You are confused!"

Xie Yunzhou’s sword-like brows lifted. He flicked his whip and scolded them, "What kind of nonsense are you spouting!"

He looked at Shen Lingjiang.

She had just landed, stumbled a few steps, and suddenly covered her mouth and nose. Clutching her chest, she ran to a tree and began to retch.

Li Wanli: "..."

Luo Yangming: "..."

One master, one servant, one on the left, one on the right, vomiting in perfect unison.

Xie Yunzhou glanced at them, quickly looked away, and walked into the post station, leaving behind one sentence:

"Once she's done, bring her inside... Oh, and feed Longmei some fresh fodder."

Watching Xie Yunzhou enter the station, Li Wanli and Luo Yangming turned their attention back to Shen Lingjiang and her servant.

Li Wanli wondered, "Does the Great Chu royal family not teach archery and riding? How can they be this sick?"

Luo Yangming mocked, "They are truly master and servant; they even vomit in sync."

After muttering, Li Wanli hurriedly handed over the medicine jar Luo Yangming had given him.

"Seventh Princess, take two pills. It will stop the vomiting."

Shen Lingjiang had been retching for a long time, but because she hadn't eaten all day during the journey, nothing came up, leaving her throat dry and painful.

She was already in poor health. Although she hadn't been exposed to the wind, she hadn't eaten all day, and her face was pale as paper, her lips white and blue.

Covering her mouth with her sleeve, she turned slightly and whispered, "I have embarrassed myself... thank you."

Shen Lingjiang immediately took two pills and gave two to Ruyi.

After a moment, they entered the station.

Leading them to a room, Li Wanli cupped his hands and said, "I have already ordered dinner. Your Highness, please rest after you eat. We must leave for the Yuan River dam early tomorrow morning."

Shen Lingjiang: "Very well."

After he left, Shen Lingjiang led Ruyi into the room. The furnishings were simple but complete; it was plain, but not crude.

Just as they entered, a sudden gust of wind whistled outside, sounding like a wailing ghost.

Ruyi immediately walked to the window to close it. Just as she reached out, a flash of silver light struck, followed by a rumble of thunder.

Before long, the rain poured down like a broken dam. The wind and rain blew the branches outside into a frenzy, and the roof tiles rattled.

Ruyi was quick, closing the window, but her sleeves were already dampened by the slanting rain.

"Your Highness! We are so lucky; it started pouring the moment we arrived! But this weather is so strange, it's the dead of winter, and yet such a heavy rain."

chapters.title: A Good Person
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang entered the room and untied the ink-colored fox fur cloak draped over her shoulders, nodding as she replied, "Indeed, we are lucky."

Ruyi hurried over, reached out to take the fox-fur mantle from her, and after giving it a quick look, asked with curiosity, "Your Highness, where did this mantle come from? It wasn't in your trunks. I packed all your clothes, and I am certain this wasn't among them."

Shen Lingjiang paused for a moment, then smiled calmly, "With my status, how could I possess such a fine fox mantle? It was lent to me by someone else."

Ruyi nodded solemnly and affirmed, "Then he must truly be a good person!"

Shen Lingjiang tilted her head and nodded, saying, "A good person... let's count him as half a one."

Ruyi: "Huh?"

At that moment, the post-house attendant brought up their meal. Ruyi went out to receive it and carried it into the room.

As she walked, Ruyi said, "Your Highness, let's eat. It’s just some porridge and side dishes; although a bit plain, they look quite appetizing."

Shen Lingjiang straightened her clothes, tucked her sleeves, and sat at the table, replying, "When traveling, having some porridge and side dishes is already quite good."

Ruyi nodded and filled a bowl to the brim for Shen Lingjiang, "Eat up, Your Highness. You’ve been hungry all day, and your constitution is weak; be careful not to trigger your stomach ailment."

She chattered on endlessly, young as she was, acting like an old nanny who could never stop worrying.

"And you were riding a horse in the wind all day! You’ve only just recovered from your illness! Hmm... no, this won't do. I must go to the kitchen later and see if I can get them to boil a bowl of radish and ginger soup for you."

Shen Lingjiang’s hand, holding her chopsticks, faltered slightly. Not knowing what she had recalled, a faint blush stained her cheeks.

Ruyi caught sight of this and was alarmed, crying out, "Oh my! Why is your face red? Your Highness, are you running a fever again?"

Shen Lingjiang awkwardly avoided Ruyi’s reaching hand and, in turn, flicked her finger against Ruyi’s forehead, gently scolding her, "No, I am perfectly fine. I was dressed warmly today and didn't catch the wind... It’s you, go look in the mirror yourself. Your hair is blown askew, and your little braid is sticking straight up."

Ruyi was stunned. She immediately lowered her hand, stood up, and ran to the mirror. Sure enough, the bun she had pinned at the back of her head was loose and crooked, and a stray braid was pointing toward the ceiling.

She pressed it down with her hand, but as soon as she let go, it sprang back up. She pressed it again, let go, and it sprang up once more, stubborn as could be.

Ruyi: "Oh! Your Highness, why didn't you say so earlier? I looked so ridiculous just now!"

Shen Lingjiang smiled slightly and said, "I thought it looked quite fine."

Ruyi: "Why isn't your hair messy?"

Shen Lingjiang: "Uh... stop looking in the mirror and come eat."

Ruyi: "Oh."

While the mistress and servant chatted and laughed, the atmosphere on the other side was much more serious.

The food brought by the attendant had been sitting on the table for quite a while, but Xie Yunzhou hadn't touched it; he was sitting at the desk, flipping through a document.

Xie Yunzhou said while reading, "The current of the Xiao-Ju River in Jintai is rapid and prone to flooding. The sluice gates and embankments have been repaired many times, only to be washed away time and again. The terrain issue is truly difficult to resolve."

Luo Yangming stood before the desk and replied, "It is indeed a difficult problem. Jintai is also the territory of the Marquis of Jing'an. The Marquis has never supported the construction of the canal, and with him there, I fear there will be even more obstruction."

Xie Yunzhou frowned upon hearing this.

Li Wanli stood by the dining table, listening while staring intently at the food, his eyes glowing.

He endured and endured, but finally couldn't hold back anymore. With a bitter face, he said, "Your Highness, let's eat before we continue looking. We've been traveling all day without a single grain of rice; even a bear couldn't withstand such hunger. I'm truly about to starve to death."

Luo Yangming glared at him, "So you know you're a bear!"

Li Wanli scratched his head: "It was just a metaphor, why did you take it seriously?"

Xie Yunzhou was silent for a moment, then finally closed the document, stood up, walked to the table, and sat down to drink a bowl of porridge.

He ate extremely quickly, yet his movements did not appear unrefined.

Halfway through, he suddenly asked, "Did the person next door receive their food?"

Luo Yangming replied, "They did."

Li Wanli gave a simple-minded smile and asked without thinking, "Your Highness, I feel you are quite concerned about the Seventh Princess."

Luo Yangming: "..."

Xie Yunzhou: "Get over here and eat, aren't you about to starve to death!"

The next day, just as the sky began to brighten, the door was knocked upon. It was likely that Xie Yunzhou had sent someone to urge them.

Shen Lingjiang quickly tidied her clothes, tied on her fox-fur mantle, and went out.

At the door was indeed Li Wanli. He gave two simple-minded laughs and thrust a scallion-oil pancake wrapped in oil paper toward Shen Lingjiang’s face, grinning, "Seventh Princess, have some. The pockmarked woman at the end of the street makes these quite fragrant; I’ve already gobbled up three!"

Shen Lingjiang thanked him, tore half of the pancake in her hand, and handed it to Ruyi behind her, whispering, "You eat some too; we have a busy day ahead."

Ruyi’s eyes brightened. She quickly took the pancake, winked at Shen Lingjiang, and nodded: "Thank you, Your Highness!"

The big man scratched the back of his head. Seeing that although Shen Lingjiang was an imperial princess, she treated her servants with approachability and lacked the usual distinction between high and low, he couldn't help but look at her more favorably.

But Li Wanli did not know that when Shen Lingjiang was in the Great Chu, she was never a legitimate imperial princess to begin with. If it weren't for the need to send a hostage princess to Liang, her biological father would likely have acted as if she didn't exist at all.

Shen Lingjiang took a small bite and tilted her head to ask, "General Li, where is the Prince?"

"The Prince took Yangming to inspect the river before dawn! It was raining then, too. The Prince instructed me to wait until the rain stopped before coming to call you."

Shen Lingjiang nodded, finished the half-pancake in a few bites, wiped her mouth with a handkerchief, and said, "Then we must not delay; let us go quickly."

With that, the group set off toward the Xiao-Ju River.

The streets were decorated with lanterns and streamers, with red cloth draped everywhere and red 'Fu' characters pasted on doors.

Shen Lingjiang realized only then, "Is New Year's Eve in two days?"

Li Wanli replied while walking briskly, "That's right. The end of the year is always the busiest time. I fear I won't be able to spend the New Year with my younger sister this year."

This man was truly a sister-obsessed brother. Shen Lingjiang had heard him mention his younger sister at home several times. She couldn't help but smile and joked, "Those who are capable always have more work to do."

Li Wanli chuckled, then suddenly added, "It wasn't this lively in previous years. I heard the Marquis of Jing'an's household has added a new child, a double blessing, so they decorated the city."

Shen Lingjiang paused, thinking deeply.

...The Marquis of Jing'an.

Wasn't it the heir to the Marquis of Jing'an, He Weishi, who had insulted her on the Golden Platform that day?

Shen Lingjiang asked as if casually, "Doesn't the Marquis of Jing'an only have one son?"

Li Wanli was a scatterbrain with no guile, and she easily tricked the information out of him in a few sentences, "That's right! It’s just that he only had one seedling before, and now that a concubine in the house has finally given birth to another son, they are naturally excited and happy!"

Shen Lingjiang: "That is true."

As they spoke, they arrived at the Xiao-Ju River.

The Xiao-Ju River was the great river of Jintai, connecting to the capital of Yan in the north and Dongpu in the south. Opening a canal to intersect with natural rivers had always been a difficult task, not to mention that the Xiao-Ju River was already prone to rapid currents and heavy silt.

The river was wide, and as Shen Lingjiang reached the bank, she was hit by a fierce gust of wind.

"What is that?"

chapters.title: Thick Bitterness
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang tucked in her sleeves, which were flapping wildly in the wind, and pointed toward a string of magnificent, lantern-lit pleasure boats on the river.

It was indeed a string of them.

The most conspicuous was a massive two-story pleasure boat. Its hull was wide, looking like an exquisite, carved pavilion floating on the water. Several other lantern boats were arranged around it, connected by chains and wooden bridges, forming a large, opulent, and intricate fleet.

A flush rose on Li Wanli’s bronze-colored face, and he said embarrassedly, "I heard it's called something like... 'Orchid Boat on the Duckweed'? It's a famous pleasure spot here, with many beautiful boat-girls on board."

Shen Lingjiang was stunned for a moment, "Even though the water is rapid and dangerous, it cannot stop these high-ranking officials from seeking pleasure."

Li Wanli scratched the back of his head and muttered, "Dangerous is dangerous, but the scenery is truly beautiful. It's no wonder there are those who don't fear death."

As they were speaking, Xie Yunzhou and Luo Yangming walked over from the opposite side.

Xie Yunzhou held a dragon-scale bound scroll in his left hand and a purple-bristled brush with a black tip in his right.

Luo Yangming followed beside him, carrying a square inkstone with freshly ground ink.

Seeing Shen Lingjiang, Xie Yunzhou handed the brush to Luo Yangming, walked over with the scroll, and finally handed it to Shen Lingjiang, saying, "Take a look."

Shen Lingjiang tightened the mantle on her shoulders, took the scroll, and unfolded it to read page by page.

It detailed the recurring problems of the Xiao-Ju River and the difficulties of connecting the two rivers.

Severe siltation, rapid currents, frequent flooding...

Shen Lingjiang didn't look too closely, but instead tilted her head to point toward a cluster of exquisite buildings above the bank of the "Orchid Boat on the Duckweed," asking, "What place is that?"

Luo Yangming replied, "That is the Gold and Silver Terrace."

Shen Lingjiang asked again, "What is the Gold and Silver Terrace?"

Luo Yangming sneered with disdain, "A place for young masters and ladies to seek pleasure. I heard this was originally an orchard, but later the heir to the Marquis of Jing'an took a fancy to it, cut down the trees, destroyed the forest, and built this Gold and Silver Terrace. Even the 'Orchid Boat on the Duckweed' by the river is the property of the Marquis of Jing'an’s heir."

Shen Lingjiang’s eyes widened slightly, as if in disbelief, "Officials of Great Liang are forbidden from patronizing prostitutes. As a son of a marquis, he actually opens a brothel to amass wealth?"

Luo Yangming pursed his lips and said nothing.

Li Wanli spoke up first, "He only inherits his ancestor's shadow and has never entered officialdom. Since this is the Marquis of Jing'an's fief, buying land and building gardens is within the rules. Although there is gossip at court, nothing can be done to him."

Seeing her nodding thoughtfully, Xie Yunzhou frowned. He walked over quickly, held the scroll in front of Shen Lingjiang’s face, and said impatiently, "Why are you asking about these things? You, who are so weak that you vomit from riding a horse, are now concerned about pleasure houses? Hurry up and read!"

Shen Lingjiang: "...Your Highness, it's too close; the characters are blurring."

Xie Yunzhou loosened his grip, then crossed his arms and stared at her as she spread out the scroll to read carefully.

The river wind howled, blowing hair and robes into a frenzy.

Shen Lingjiang was dressed simply, with only the ink-colored fur mantle on her shoulders being the most luxurious item.

Her hair was held up by only a plain white ribbon, hanging loosely behind her head. Now, it was being blown wildly by the river wind. Two strands brushed across her lowered, slanted eyes, so she raised her hand to tuck them behind her ear before continuing to read.

Xie Yunzhou watched her intently. Her brows were like ink paintings, her figure as elegant as green bamboo; she possessed the bones of a celestial being.

Shen Lingjiang had been reading seriously at first, but as time went on, the gaze fixed upon her became increasingly unrestrained, making it difficult for her to concentrate.

"Your Highness, I am truly reading carefully now; you don't need to keep staring at me."

Xie Yunzhou was called back to his senses and shifted his gaze away, feeling quite awkward. A moment later, he suddenly asked, "How old are you? Have you not yet reached your capping ceremony?"

Shen Lingjiang’s hand, which was turning the page, paused slightly, then she replied calmly, "Nineteen."

Xie Yunzhou asked again, "Why are you not wearing a hairpin?"

Just a moment ago, he had told her to read the scroll seriously, but now that she was reading, he began to interrupt again.

Shen Lingjiang sighed, looked up at Xie Yunzhou, and said, "I am not wearing a hairpin naturally because there is no one to preside over my capping ceremony. Besides..."

At this point, she paused, her tone tinged with a hint of amusement. She pointed to the jade-encrusted gold crown on Xie Yunzhou’s head and teased, "Besides, hairpins look very expensive. How can they be cheaper than a strip of cloth? You can just cut a piece and tie it for a day; it's both convenient and practical."

No one to preside over her capping ceremony... Xie Yunzhou couldn't help but think of Shen Lingjiang’s awkward status in the Great Chu. It was likely that the Emperor had never held a ceremony for her at all.

But even without a father, there was a mother. Had her mother not held a capping ceremony for her either?

Xie Yunzhou suppressed the inexplicable bitterness that welled up in his heart and nodded, saying slowly, "That's true. You have already taken a courtesy name, so you must be over fifteen."

Shen Lingjiang nodded perfunctorily, lowered her head to look at the scroll again, and added, "Yes, yes, I am over fifteen, and Your Highness is over twenty; we are both adults. We should be more sensible and stop disturbing others for no reason."

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

The noble Prince was rendered speechless by a single sentence from the hostage princess. He glared at Shen Lingjiang and turned his gaze away.

After this, the group began to inspect the river in earnest, occasionally exchanging a few words.

Shen Lingjiang held the dragon-scale scroll, flipped to the end, and occasionally picked up a brush to write a few words.

They walked a long way along the Xiao-Ju River, gradually moving away from the bustling crowds. When they encountered craftsmen repairing the embankments, they would stop to ask a few questions.

"Young man, hasn't the embankment already been built? Why are you expanding it again?"

In the middle of winter, the young man was dressed thinly, his head covered in sweat. He pulled the handkerchief draped over his shoulder to wipe his brow, "Are you all from out of town? The Xiao-Ju River floods every year, and this embankment is repaired and reinforced every year. Oh, it's nothing unusual, nothing unusual."

Shen Lingjiang nodded and wrote a line on the paper:

"Severe siltation, rising riverbed; there is a fear of the danger of a 'hanging river' above ground."

After asking the man a few more questions, the group continued walking.

Just as Shen Lingjiang had said in the morning, they were indeed busy today, truly busy.

They didn't even have time to eat at noon. Li Wanli rode into town and bought a few thin spring pancakes. Each of them gnawed on two, without even a drop of water to drink, eating until they were choked and stuffed.

After a simple meal, they began to walk back. Shen Lingjiang had been blown by the wind along the river for too long; although she didn't have a fever or headache, she couldn't help but feel an itch in her throat and began to cough.

Around dusk, they suddenly saw a group of people walking hurriedly toward them on the road ahead. They were dressed neatly and opulently, unlike the workers repairing the embankments by the river.

One of them walked up to Xie Yunzhou, knelt on one knee, and bowed respectfully, "This humble one greets the Prince."

Xie Yunzhou: "And you are?"

The man stood up, bowed his back, and said, "This humble one is an official under the Marquis of Jing'an. The Marquis knows you have arrived and has already set up a banquet at the 'Orchid Boat on the Duckweed.' May I ask if the Prince would do us the honor of attending?"

Before Xie Yunzhou could speak, Li Wanli had already started shouting.

"What does your Marquis mean by this? Who invites guests to a brothel!"

chapters.title: The Pipa Player
chapters.content:
The man grew anxious, waving his hands and shaking his head repeatedly. "Not at all, not at all! The 'Ping Shang Lan Zhou' is a place of elegance, where the most renowned courtesans gather. It has always been favored by the scholars and literati of Jingtai; it is no ordinary brothel. Besides, the Marquis said that since it is his own property, he can rest assured of its quality, which is why he dared to invite the Prince here!"

He spoke with such logic and eloquence that Li Wanli, who was never good with words, was left speechless. In the end, he could only glare at the man, his face flushed with frustration.

Luo Yangming’s expression darkened. He adjusted his precious long sword and was about to say, "Not going, get lost."

Unfortunately, before he could speak, Xie Yunzhou, standing beside him, pondered for a moment and said, "Since Marquis He has extended such a gracious invitation, how can we refuse? Lead the way."

The man immediately bowed and gestured, saying respectfully, "Please, Your Highness. And you too, Seventh Prince."

Xie Yunzhou and Shen Lingjiang walked ahead, while Luo Yangming and Li Wanli followed two steps behind.

Li Wanli muttered discontentedly, "I can't believe the Prince actually agreed to go!"

Luo Yangming’s expression was equally grim. He merely said, "We must give the host some face. Besides, regarding the canal project, we will need the Marquis of Jing'an’s assistance here in Jingtai."

Ruyi trotted along behind them, grumbling, "Why does this have to involve my Prince too!"

Upon entering the pleasure boat, they saw red lanterns and colorful ribbons hanging from the rafters. The main hall was packed with guests, and the air was thick with a mixture of incense and the scent of rouge.

On the stage, a beautiful woman in silk dance robes swung her long, flowing sleeves like clouds as the music played. Her dance was as graceful as a swimming dragon, and the melody flowed like water, leaving the audience below completely mesmerized.

However, Xie Yunzhou kept his eyes straight ahead. He followed the guide through the bustling hall, passed through several doorways, and arrived at a small wooden bridge about three feet wide.

Chains were fastened beneath the bridge, connecting the main pleasure boat to several smaller lantern boats.

The man stopped, turned, and bowed. "The Marquis is on the lantern boat. Please, Your Highnesses, step inside."

Xie Yunzhou paused, exchanged a glance with Shen Lingjiang, and stepped onto the wooden bridge, with Shen Lingjiang following closely behind.

As the two crossed, Li Wanli and the others tried to follow, but the man raised a hand to block their path.

"Generals, please stay. A lantern boat has been prepared for you on the left. Please move there to enjoy the wine and music."

Li Wanli glared at him and shoved him, demanding, "You scoundrel! What is the meaning of this? The Prince is on that boat; why are you trying to separate us?"

The man stumbled back two steps from the push, then immediately hunched his back again, assuming a humble posture.

"General, you misunderstand! It’s just that the lantern boat is too small to hold so many people! The water in the Xiao-Ju River is swift; please, General, do not take the risk!"

With the man putting it that way, what more could Li Wanli and his companion say?

They couldn't very well force their way on. If something were to happen due to overcrowding, they would be blamed for not listening to reason.

Li Wanli curled his lip and shook his fist at the man, intentionally intimidating him. "Don't you try any tricks on me!"

The man offered a fawning smile, his face thick with feigned subservience. "How could I dare? Please, Generals, go ahead. The boat next door is fully stocked with fine wine and food. You haven't tried the local specialties of Jingtai yet, have you? The flavor is truly unique."

Li Wanli kept a wary eye on the lantern boat, while Luo Yangming, silent and stoic, simply turned away with his hand on his sword.

As they were led away, Li Wanli began to complain again after only a few steps.

"Are we there yet?"

"Isn't it right next door? How many boats have we passed already!"

"I can't even see the boat my Prince boarded! You did this on purpose!"

Shen Lingjiang and Xie Yunzhou were unaware of the commotion outside. They stepped onto the lantern boat to find a middle-aged man in luxurious silk robes sitting inside. Behind a small screen, a pipa player sat on a carved stool, playing slowly.

The man was He Yuming, the Marquis of Jing'an. Seeing the two enter, he immediately stood up to greet them.

He bowed to Xie Yunzhou first and said with a gentle smile, "The Prince Regent has come from afar; why didn't you send word in advance? I would have liked to prepare a proper welcome."

The Marquis of Jing'an was the biological brother of the Empress Dowager; even the Emperor privately called him "Uncle." Although Xie Yunzhou had achieved great military success, he still had to show some respect.

He returned the bow and said, "This visit is for the canal project. It is official business, and I did not wish to disturb the Marquis's peace."

He Yuming gestured for Xie Yunzhou to sit and exchanged a few more pleasantries.

"The Prince is too modest. We see each other every day at court; we are old acquaintances! It is only because the end of the year is approaching that I was able to return home to pay respects to my ancestors. Otherwise, I haven't been back to Jingtai in a long time... Tell me, is this the Prince's first time in Jingtai? Why not take a tour of the Xiao-Ju River? The scenery on this river is quite famous in our Jingtai."

With that, he walked to the side of the cabin, tapped on the wooden window, and ordered, "Row the boat for a tour."

As soon as he spoke, a respectful response came from outside.

Shen Lingjiang felt the lantern boat sway beneath her feet, as if rocked by the waves.

Having just boarded, she was not yet accustomed to the instability of the water, which made her feel dizzy. Reflexively, she grabbed onto the sleeve of Xie Yunzhou’s robe.

He Yuming seemed to notice her only then. He turned around, his face full of apology. "Oh my, I was so busy talking to the Prince that I neglected the Seventh Prince. My apologies, my apologies! Please, sit, Your Highness! Please sit!"

Xie Yunzhou condescended to help her, supporting her palm with the back of his hand, and added with a deliberate smirk, "Please, take the seat of honor, Your Highness."

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Shen Lingjiang hesitated for a moment, then smiled faintly and played along. "Then I thank the Prince."

Xie Yunzhou twitched his lips, revealing a strange, unnatural smile.

Both sat down, and He Yuming laughed as he took his seat.

No sooner had he sat down than he toasted Shen Lingjiang. "At the Golden Banquet, my son was unruly and offended you. As his father, I apologize on his behalf. He is just a child; I hope Your Highness will not hold it against him."

Since he had already said it all, what could Shen Lingjiang, a hostage in an awkward position, say?

She picked up the wine cup from the long table and smiled slightly. "I wouldn't dare. The young Marquis is simply straightforward."

He Yuming forced a smile and downed his drink in one gulp.

"Keep drinking, keep drinking. Prince, you should drink too... Hmm, pipa player, stop playing. Come over and pour wine for the Prince and the Prince."

From behind the small screen, the beautiful woman in a rouge-colored silk dress emerged. She bowed gracefully, moved with light steps, knelt on the floor, and lifted her fair wrists to pour wine for them.

"Prince, please have a drink."

"Seventh Prince, please have a drink."

The "Ping Shang Lan Zhou" truly gathered the most stunning beauties. This pipa player had skin like congealed fat and a face as vibrant as cinnabar. Her beauty was striking, and every slight movement of her brow or tilt of her head was filled with allure.

Unfortunately, Xie Yunzhou was not a man easily swayed by women; such charms were wasted on him.

The woman was dressed in thin, translucent gauze, revealing glimpses of her skin, and her chest was quite exposed. Shen Lingjiang felt something was off, but she was too embarrassed to stare, so she couldn't help but frown slightly.

Because of this, neither of them noticed the smile that didn't reach the woman's eyes.

chapters.title: The Red Thread
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang drank only half a cup and stopped. She glanced quietly at Xie Yunzhou, who seemed to have a high tolerance for alcohol, as he finished another full cup.

He Yuming asked, "Eh, why has Your Highness stopped drinking?"

Shen Lingjiang smiled slightly and replied, "I am physically weak and prone to illness, so I must decline the fine wine."

He Yuming countered, "This wine is the 'Crane Year Imperial Brew' bestowed by the Emperor. It is infused with medicinal herbs, so it won't harm your health. Drinking a few more cups might even strengthen your constitution!"

What did he mean by that?

Did he invite them here just to force them to drink?

Hearing this, not only Shen Lingjiang but even Xie Yunzhou set down his cup.

He enjoyed good wine, and this "Crane Year Imperial Brew" was rare even in the palace, so he had indulged in a few cups, relying on his high tolerance. But now, coming to his senses, he felt something was wrong.

He Yuming continued, "I wonder how the Prince is handling the Yuan River canal project?"

Xie Yunzhou, unsure of what the Marquis was plotting, replied vaguely, "It is progressing."

He Yuming nodded with a smile. "The Prince is formidable on the battlefield, but I didn't expect you to be so capable in these matters as well. With such bold actions, I imagine trade with Yunqin will be possible within two years. Once this is accomplished, the Prince will deserve the greatest credit!"

Xie Yunzhou looked at him and asked, "Did the Marquis not oppose my canal project?"

Hearing this, He Yuming sighed, putting on a look of concern for the nation. "This project is complex and massive; it is a drain on the people and the treasury. I only pity the common folk."

After saying this, he pointed at the pipa player, who was shrinking back, and shouted, "Get out! We are discussing important state affairs; what is a musician doing lingering here?"

Before he finished speaking, the pipa player seemed startled. The white glazed wine pot in her hand fell onto the table, and she began to tremble uncontrollably.

"You clumsy fool! Get out of here!"

The pipa player let out a low sob, wiped the spilled wine from the table with her skirt, and stumbled out of the cabin.

Shen Lingjiang frowned, watching the pipa player’s retreating back, feeling even more suspicious.

Why was she so terrified?

Was she just scared because she was seeing important figures for the first time?

That didn't seem right.

Since he was hosting the Prince Regent, the Marquis of Jing'an would certainly not hire a musician who couldn't handle the situation.

Even Shen Lingjiang couldn't figure it out for a moment. Instead, the alcohol began to go to her head, making her face feel hot.

She shook her head and looked at Xie Yunzhou.

He was frowning, shaking his sleeve, which had been dampened by the spilled wine.

The Marquis of Jing'an apologized repeatedly, "Poor hospitality, truly poor hospitality!"

Xie Yunzhou’s brow was tightly furrowed, but having been on the battlefield where blood was often on his clothes, he wasn't that particular.

He shook his hand and said, "Forget it." He didn't say anything more, just picked up his silver chopsticks to pick at the side dishes.

The Marquis of Jing'an glanced at them and suddenly turned to shout outside, "Why haven't the remaining dishes been served yet?"

Someone outside replied, "Coming, Marquis, they will be here immediately."

He Yuming looked at the two and repeated, "Poor hospitality, truly poor hospitality."

Xie Yunzhou and Shen Lingjiang remained silent, but He Yuming didn't seem embarrassed. He continued, "I am older, so please forgive me for speaking too much, but Prince, it is time for you to take a wife."

After all that talk, it had actually come to this.

Xie Yunzhou looked back at him with a smile on his lips. "Oh? Does the Marquis intend to act as a matchmaker for me?"

"I wouldn't dare act as a matchmaker." The Marquis of Jing'an laughed, then glanced at Shen Lingjiang, saying intentionally or unintentionally, "It’s just that seeing the Prince bring the Seventh Prince along, I thought... The Great Chu monarch has the same intention. If it could be accomplished, it would be a wonderful thing for both countries."

Shen Lingjiang: "?"

Shen Lingjiang was stunned. How did it end up involving her?

Xie Yunzhou was also stunned for a moment. He instinctively turned to look at Shen Lingjiang, seeing that her face was flushed with the effects of the wine, her eyes hazy and unfocused.

Tsk... With that tolerance, she was getting drunk after half a cup?

Xie Yunzhou laughed, then looked at He Yuming with a half-smile and asked, "The Marquis is not usually a talkative man; why are you meddling in my private affairs today?"

The Marquis of Jing'an stiffened, then hurriedly said, "I wouldn't dare! The Prince should just consider it drunken chatter. Hmm... why haven't the dishes come yet! Please sit for a moment, I will go urge them myself! These servants, how dare they be so lazy and slow!"

With that, he lifted his robes, held his head as if he were also drunk, and stumbled out of the cabin.

Xie Yunzhou and Shen Lingjiang exchanged a look, both feeling strange.

What exactly was the Marquis of Jing'an trying to do? Was it really just drinking and chatting? He couldn't be that idle.

Shen Lingjiang supported her forehead, shook her head, and looked at Xie Yunzhou with blurry eyes. "Prince, what do you make of this?"

Xie Yunzhou was taken aback by the question. He awkwardly looked away and asked, "Your Highness is so clever, can you not see through it?"

Shen Lingjiang didn't answer. She shook her head again and tapped it twice. "My head is spinning... why is it so hot in here?"

Suddenly, a sliver of unease rose in her heart. She grabbed the half-drunk wine cup and sniffed it lightly.

Xie Yunzhou teased her, "Surely not. He is a Marquis; would he really resort to drugging us?"

Shen Lingjiang shook her head, set the cup down, and replied, "It is definitely medicinal wine. Artemisia, citron, osmanthus... there are too many, I can't identify them all."

Whether it was the charcoal fire in the cabin or something else, seeing the flush on Shen Lingjiang’s face, Xie Yunzhou suddenly felt a surge of heat in his own chest.

"You know medicine?" he asked, standing up to push open the wooden windows to let in some cold air.

Shen Lingjiang laughed, sitting still. "I wouldn't say I know it. Long-term illness makes one a doctor; I just know a few medicinal herbs."

"Your nonsense cannot be fully trusted." Just as Xie Yunzhou finished his sentence, his eyes suddenly narrowed. He slammed the last window open with great force and leaned out to look.

The movement was loud, and the window rattled. Shen Lingjiang immediately turned to look, asking anxiously, "What is it?"

A cold light flashed in Xie Yunzhou’s eyes as he replied, "There is no one on the boat."

Shen Lingjiang: "?"

Shen Lingjiang frowned, forced herself to stand up, and walked unsteadily toward the outside.

The river wind hit her face, and indeed, there was no one outside the boat. The lantern boat had drifted quite far; the main pleasure boat was no longer in sight. Only the shimmering ripples on the water remained, with the silver moonlight shattered within them.

Shen Lingjiang looked around, took a deep breath, and turned back. "Wonderful. Not only are there no people, but they didn't even leave the oars."

"Prince, is this the Liang way of hospitality? It’s quite unique."

Her words left Xie Yunzhou speechless.

Shen Lingjiang looked at him, frowning more as she did so. After a long while, she added, "Are you drunk too? Why is your face so red?"

Xie Yunzhou glared at her, then immediately looked away, gritting his teeth as he muttered, "He Yuming, that old scoundrel, he really dared to drug us!"

Shen Lingjiang fell silent. After a long time, she slowly murmured, "This way of hospitality is truly unique."

chapters.title: Drunken Spring Night
chapters.content:
Xie Yunzhou’s constitution was far better than Shen Lingjiang’s, so the effects of the drug took hold more slowly.

However, having consumed more than half a pot of wine, his reaction was many times more intense than Shen Lingjiang’s. He felt dizzier, hotter, and his eyes were bloodshot from the strain.

For a moment, he felt lightheaded, as if every step he took was on clouds.

Wave after wave of heat washed over his face, and the blood beneath his chest felt like a pool of boiling, molten lava, threatening to burn through his very skin and flesh.

He looked at Shen Lingjiang with crimson eyes, the whites dense with blood vessels. His gaze seemed veiled, the emotions within unreadable.

Shen Lingjiang resembled her late mother. At this moment, with her face flushed and her hair disheveled, the blood-red mole beneath her left eyelid looked vivid and striking, making her appear all the more bewitching.

She was smiling, a soft, amorous smile.

But the moment Xie Yunzhou had first seen her, he knew she was a person covered in thorns, with a dagger hidden in her smile.

What kind of thorns were they?

He truly wanted to pull them out, one by one. Once the thorns were gone, he wondered if she would still be able to smile like that.

Xie Yunzhou’s mind was a tangled mess; he didn't even know what he was thinking, only staring fixedly at Shen Lingjiang.

Shen Lingjiang was even more lost. The drug had taken full effect, blurring her vision and making it hard to even stand.

Though she had only drunk half a cup, it was already unbearable. She leaned her weight against the dining table, her eyes fixed on the delicacies and fine wine laid out before her.

There were silver chopsticks with plum and bamboo patterns, jade chopstick rests, and gold-traced plates filled with food. At the corner of the table sat a small, exquisite white-glazed vase with a long neck and a bulbous belly, holding a few sparse, vibrant sprigs of red plum blossoms.

She stared for a long while, then suddenly swept her sleeve, knocking the bowls and plates to the floor, and backhanded the vase, toppling it onto the table.

With a few crisp sounds, the beautiful vase shattered into pieces, and the plum branches scattered.

Shen Lingjiang’s smile faded. She reached out her left hand and pressed it firmly onto the shards of porcelain. Blood gushed out, staining the white glaze red.

The blood was bright red, the plum blossoms were bright red, and together they were an even deeper crimson.

Shen Lingjiang’s eyelashes trembled; the palm of her left hand was a mangled mess of flesh and blood.

The pain was real, but as the blood flowed, the effects of the drug seemed to dissipate by more than half, and her mind cleared significantly.

"You’re even cruel to yourself?"

Xie Yunzhou had appeared behind her at some point. He grabbed her wrist and flipped over her blood-drenched palm, a thick, viscous red pooling in his hand.

The blood trickled down her skin, winding its way down, warm and sticky, flowing onto Xie Yunzhou’s fingers.

His hand, which had never trembled while wielding a sword or blade, suddenly shook violently. Xie Yunzhou’s entire body was burning, scorching hot, yet he felt the blood flowing onto his fingers was even hotter, like molten iron poured onto him, branding a scar into his flesh that could never be removed.

Seeing Xie Yunzhou’s eyes growing redder and his breathing more ragged, Shen Lingjiang frowned and tried to pull her hand away, but he clamped down so tightly she couldn't move.

"Xie Yunzhou!"

It was the first time she had addressed the Regent by his name, her tone laced with agitation.

Xie Yunzhou seemed not to hear her. He simply raised his head, staring straight at her, and leaned in closer and closer.

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Clang!

Suddenly, a loud crash echoed. Xie Yunzhou swayed from the impact, looked at Shen Lingjiang again in a daze, and after a long while, spat out, "...Why are your lips so red?"

As soon as the words fell, he closed his eyes and collapsed to the floor.

Even in his unconscious state, his hand, still gripping Shen Lingjiang’s left wrist, did not loosen; he pulled her down with him.

Shen Lingjiang fell onto him, her cheek hitting his chest. Through his thin clothing, she could feel the scorching skin beneath the fabric.

Shen Lingjiang scrambled up, tossed aside the gilded incense burner she had used to strike him, and pried open Xie Yunzhou’s hand.

Her left hand was still bleeding. She looked around, knelt on the floor, fumbled with Xie Yunzhou’s upper body for a moment, and finally tore a large piece of silk from the sleeve of his inner robe, wrapping it crudely around her wound.

After dressing the wound, she climbed up, shook her dizzy head, and looked down at the unconscious Xie Yunzhou with a blank expression. Suddenly, she raised her foot and kicked his leg hard twice.

Although the drug’s effects had mostly faded, she was still lightheaded. After the two kicks, Xie Yunzhou didn't react, but Shen Lingjiang nearly tripped herself.

She steadied herself against the table, looked around, and muttered belatedly, "Lips... red? Whose?"

After looking for a while, she finally spotted a small vanity behind a screen. She stumbled over, found a mirror, and rubbed her lips hard against it.

Well, she had rubbed them even redder.

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Shen Lingjiang tossed the bronze mirror down in defeat and turned to look at the chaos in the cabin.

It was unclear how much more time had passed when Xie Yunzhou groggily opened his eyes. He felt a splitting headache and, just as he reached out to rub his temples, realized his hands and feet were spread-eagled and tied to a cramped small couch. His wrists and ankles were bound with several layers of silk, tied very tightly.

His outer robe had been stripped away, his inner robe was torn to shreds, and he was lying on his back with his chest exposed.

That wasn't the worst of it. The most critical thing was that he was soaking wet, his hair, clothes, and trousers were drenched, and there were water stains on his face. He felt as if he had been submerged in water.

Xie Yunzhou opened his mouth to speak, but as soon as he did, he felt as if his mouth were filled with coarse, wet sand. Disgusted, he turned his head and coughed several times.

"Shen Lingjiang! Shen Lanshu! You have some nerve!"

Xie Yunzhou struggled against his wrist bindings, then glared at Shen Lingjiang, who was sitting opposite him, with red-rimmed, hateful eyes.

The flush had not yet faded from Shen Lingjiang’s face. Perhaps because it was too hot, she had also removed her outer robe and was sitting on a square stool in her inner garment.

Despite her disheveled appearance, her movements were slow and elegant. She said leisurely, "Your Highness, I did this for your own good. I couldn't let you lose your senses to the drug and ruin your chastity, could I?"

Heh, chastity.

Xie Yunzhou was so angry he laughed.

He took a few deep breaths and asked slowly, "Where did you get the cold water?"

Water?

Speak of the devil.

Shen Lingjiang picked up the lotus-edged celadon basin she had placed on the table and splashed all the water inside onto Xie Yunzhou’s clothes, saying with a smile, "Dipped from the river. The boat is drifting on the Xiaoqu River; why would I worry about finding water?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou felt a chill strike his heart from the basin of water.

Fine. No wonder he felt mud and sand in his mouth; it was water from the Xiaoqu River!

Xie Yunzhou was choked with rage and hissed, "Shen, Lan, Shu."

Lanshu was Shen Lingjiang’s courtesy name, though few people used it. Shen Lingjiang was stunned for a moment upon hearing it, then set down the basin and explained, "Your Highness, cold water calms the heart. I splashed myself with it too."

As she spoke, she walked toward the small couch, spread her arms, and turned slowly, as if wanting Xie Yunzhou to see clearly that she, too, was soaked.

Xie Yunzhou stared at her silently. He saw that Shen Lingjiang’s clothes were thin, her damp black hair hanging loose behind her, water droplets dripping down and soaking the back of her garment.

She sat back down on the square stool, turned her back to him, and raised her hands to comb through her hair, gathering the damp black locks in front of her. She lowered her head and gently wiped them with a handkerchief.

With her thin, soaked clothes, one could faintly see the slender, fair neck and the butterfly bones pressing against the wet fabric. She looked like a water spirit.

Xie Yunzhou immediately turned his head away. He suddenly felt that the heat wave, which had been extinguished with such difficulty by the cold river water, was threatening to return. A surge of heat rose to his face, and the volcano buried in his heart erupted once more.

Damn it, the drug’s effects must not have worn off yet!

chapters.title: Nightmare of Old Dreams
chapters.content:
He wondered when Xie Yunzhou’s two subordinates would find them.

Shen Lingjiang wrung out her hair with the handkerchief, still feeling dizzy.

This time, it wasn't the drug.

It was a headache and dizziness; she feared that after all the tossing and turning throughout the night, the drenching and the disrobing, her old illness had flared up again.

Shen Lingjiang leaned against the table, dazed, and drifted off to sleep.

Xie Yunzhou also closed his eyes, suppressing his turbulent thoughts, and channeled his internal energy to resist.

The dark night quietly faded, and the eastern horizon revealed a faint, pale white as daylight leaked in.

There was movement outside the boat, the sound of oars churning water, and soon, someone hurried onto the deck.

"Your Highness! Your Highness!"

"Are you inside?"

It was Li Wanli’s voice.

Xie Yunzhou, on the small couch, suddenly opened his eyes. He frowned, looked toward the cabin door, and barked, "Stop! Do not come in."

The two men outside stopped in their tracks, only Li Wanli’s frantic shouting drifting in.

"Your Highness, how are you?"

"Your Highness? Your Highness!"

Xie Yunzhou pretended not to hear. He looked down at himself; in this disheveled state, how could he let his subordinates see him?

He exerted force, and a burst of internal energy shredded the cloth bindings on his wrists and ankles.

Xie Yunzhou immediately sat up, grabbed another neatly folded outer robe, and scrambled to put it on.

Once dressed, he walked quickly to the table and patted Shen Lingjiang’s shoulder. "Shen Lingjiang? Shen Lanshu?"

She didn't wake up.

Damn it, he had forgotten she was a sickly thing!

Xie Yunzhou immediately reached out to touch Shen Lingjiang’s forehead. Sure enough, it was burning hot.

With one hand, he pulled the fox-fur cloak from the screen, and with the other, he scooped up the unconscious Shen Lingjiang from the table, wrapping her tightly in the cloak.

"Yangming! Come in!"

The next moment, the wooden door of the cabin was pushed open, and Li Wanli and Luo Yangming hurried in.

"Your Highness, it is our negligence and dereliction of duty!"

The two knelt halfway, but before they could finish their plea, Xie Yunzhou waved his hand impatiently.

Xie Yunzhou: "Yangming, come and take a look at her. She’s burning up again. Is it her old illness?"

He sat at the table, cradling Shen Lingjiang, who was wrapped tightly in the thick, wide black fox-fur cloak. Her face was obscured, but both men knew that the person inside was the Seventh Prince of Great Chu.

The Regent sat upright, his back straight, his head lowered as he adjusted his sleeves. Though he looked a bit disheveled, his outer robe was clean and tidy.

The two subordinates had no idea that beneath their master’s outer robe was an inner garment torn to shreds, as ragged as a broom.

Luo Yangming was slightly stunned by Xie Yunzhou’s uncharacteristic anxiety, but he quickly regained his composure and stepped forward to take her pulse.

"Hmm... is it Pu Ren Xiang?"

Pu Ren Xiang (The Seducer’s Fragrance) was the name of the drug, a common aphrodisiac in the pleasure quarters. The name implied "a fragrance of orchids and musk clinging to one's body," sounding subtle and ambiguous, but its potency was strong.

Luo Yangming frowned and continued, "The Seventh Prince did not ingest much, and by drawing blood to counteract the poison, the drug is neutralized. However, she is naturally of a frail constitution, and to have been drugged and then exposed to the cold all night..."

He rambled on, and Xie Yunzhou, frowning, interrupted him directly: "Just tell me, is it serious?"

Luo Yangming was a blockhead, a man of wood. He pondered for a moment and said immediately, "I can use golden needles to stimulate the acupoints, then dissolve a Zijin Pill in strong liquor for her to take. Three doses in a row will wake her. After she wakes, she must continue taking it three times a day, and she will be able to hold on for another half-month. With that time, it will certainly not delay the canal project."

Xie Yunzhou stared at him in silence.

He didn't speak, but Li Wanli gasped and clicked his tongue, "Brother, you are truly more ruthless than that Master Tian east of the city who keeps two hundred tenant farmers."

Luo Yangming: "..."

Seeming to belatedly understand the deep meaning in Xie Yunzhou’s eyes, Luo Yangming coughed in a rare moment of guilt, switched to the other wrist to take her pulse again, and finally added, "It is serious, yet not. She won't die this time, but if it happens a few more times, that might not be the case... There are also more gentle treatments."

Xie Yunzhou: "Then treat her."

Shen Lingjiang was trapped in a nightmare. In the dream, she was in Xuncheng, Great Chu.

Smoke filled the air, and the thick stone walls were plastered with blood. Fresh blood poured over old blood, dark red turning to bright red, layer upon layer, thick and foul-smelling.

On the platform, soldiers in armor lay in heaps, some riddled with arrows, their guts spilling out; others were pinned to the walls by spears, their armor shattered, their blood drained dry; some, dragging broken limbs, stubbornly held up a war banner burned half to ash, their eyes wide open, dying with grievances unavenged.

A million corpses lay in the fields, blood flowing for a thousand miles.

Shen Lingjiang stood beneath the city wall with crimson eyes, watching the corpses falling one after another, the stench of blood making her retch.

Suddenly, a piercing horn sounded in her ears, and soon after, she heard people shouting one after another.

"The Emperor has sent the letter of surrender!"

"We’ve lost, we’ve lost, Great Chu has lost!"

"Your Highness! Quickly, protect the Highness and return to the capital!"

Your Highness... Oh, that title certainly wasn't meant for her.

As Shen Lingjiang was thinking this, someone hurried toward her from behind.

The person was half a head taller than her, wearing silver armor and a red cloak over their shoulders, looking as majestic as a true general.

The person approached in a rush, raised a whip, and lashed it toward Shen Lingjiang.

The tip of the whip was sharp and flexible, yet it whistled as it swung, as if it could tear the very air apart.

With a flick of the long whip, Shen Lingjiang took the blow head-on. The pain made her gasp, but before she could cover the wound, the person stepped forward and kicked her hard in the chest.

"Shen Lingjiang, Great Chu has lost!"

"You useless piece of trash! Those plans and strategies of yours, not a single one worked! The Liang Dynasty was once our defeated foe, and who does this Xie Yunzhou think he is! You couldn't even defeat them! Tell me, what is the point of keeping your wretched life!"

Shen Lingjiang gasped for air, the pain in her chest making her cough repeatedly. She scrambled up and looked at Shangguan Ying before her. "Your Highness, I... I still have a brilliant plan, I can definitely drive back the enemy!"

Shangguan Ying sneered, flicked the whip to coil it around Shen Lingjiang’s neck, and said coldly, "A brilliant plan? You did indeed offer a few good strategies before, making Xie Yunzhou stumble badly. But what is the use now? The Emperor has already sent the letter of surrender; it cannot be changed."

Shen Lingjiang’s eyes went blank, her gaze dull for a moment. The next instant, she turned her head in a panic, looking around as if searching for someone.

Almost simultaneously, Shangguan Ying waved a hand at the lieutenant behind her, a sinister, cruel smile playing on her lips.

The next moment, Shen Lingjiang saw a thin, frail figure hanging from the tall, sturdy city wall. She was wearing tattered gray clothes, her head drooping, her hair disheveled, motionless, life or death unknown.

Shen Lingjiang’s pupils contracted. Almost subconsciously, she lunged toward the city wall, crying out in a heart-wrenching voice.

"...Aman!"

She had only lunged forward two steps when she was pinned to the ground by several soldiers.

"Aman! Let me go! Let me go!"

Her eyes were bloodshot as she struggled with all her might, but with Shen Lingjiang’s frail body, how could she break free from these strong, burly soldiers?

Shangguan Ying circled her and said mockingly, "The Emperor ordered her execution. Shen Lingjiang, you have some cleverness, but that bit of wit couldn't help Great Chu win. This is the Emperor’s punishment for you. Look... your lowly maid-servant mother is hanging there. You had better pray that the Liang general doesn't implicate civilians and drag her down to whip her corpse."

chapters.title: Initial Probing
chapters.content:
"Someone, drag her back. After all, she still carries royal blood; who knows, she might be of use later! Break camp and return to the capital!"

Shen Lingjiang was dragged away by several men who pinned her limbs. She struggled, stretching her neck to look toward the city wall, her eyes fixed on the corpse hanging at the highest point.

The person was far too thin and frail, hanging there with long limbs, head drooping, and disheveled hair obscuring her face.

In the end, Shen Lingjiang never got to see her face.

"Shangguan Ying! Shangguan Ying!"

"If you don't kill me today! One day, I will surely avenge the murder of my mother! I will!"

Inside the Jingtai Post House.

Xie Yunzhou sat in the room with his eyes closed. Not far from him, on the bed, lay Shen Lingjiang. Luo Yangming was sitting on a wooden footstool, taking her pulse.

"How is it?"

Xie Yunzhou opened his eyes at some point, walked over with light steps, and asked with a frown.

Luo Yangming stood up immediately and replied, "The fever hasn't broken. She is not conscious, and I can't get any medicine down."

Xie Yunzhou knitted his brows, tugged at his robe, sat on the edge of the bed, and reached out to touch Shen Lingjiang's forehead.

It was scorching hot, covered in a layer of damp sweat.

Xie Yunzhou’s frown deepened. "Why is there so much sweat?"

As he frowned, Luo Yangming immediately handed him a damp cloth that had been soaked in water.

Xie Yunzhou wiped his hands with the cloth while looking down at Shen Lingjiang on the bed.

She was seriously ill, her face devoid of any color; it was hard to tell whether her skin or her lips were whiter. Sweat beaded on her forehead, soaking her temples. She seemed to be murmuring something, her lips slightly parted.

"...A-Man."

"...A-Man."

Xie Yunzhou was curious. He leaned down to listen and heard the name again.

It sounded like a name; this sickly girl had called it out the last time she had a fever as well.

Luo Yangming explained from the side, "Perhaps she is trapped in a nightmare; it is normal to have some delirious speech."

Xie Yunzhou did not reply. He suddenly reached out, pulled Shen Lingjiang up from the bed, and held out his hand to Luo Yangming, saying coldly, "Medicine."

Luo Yangming was stunned for a moment but quickly reacted, handing over the medicine bowl from the side table.

"...Your Highness?"

It really couldn't be fed to her. He had tried many methods today, and all of it had been spat back out.

Luo Yangming wanted to say this, but he didn't dare.

Xie Yunzhou had called for the "medicine," but he didn't take the bowl immediately. Instead, he lowered his head and stared at Shen Lingjiang, whose eyes were tightly shut, for a long while.

Luo Yangming held the bowl, wondering if he should call out again, when he saw his wise and mighty Prince reach out and pinch the chin of the Princess. With a crisp "click," Shen Lingjiang's mouth opened.

Luo Yangming: "..."

Luo Yangming drew a sharp breath, feeling his own chin ache in sympathy.

Xie Yunzhou said nothing. He took the bowl and poured the bitter decoction into her mouth. Most of it went down, with only a little spilling from the corners of her lips.

Xie Yunzhou wiped her mouth with his own handkerchief, expressionless, and only then did he hand the empty bowl back to Luo Yangming with satisfaction.

He even said, "See, that works. Next time you can't get her to drink it, call me."

Listening closely, he even sounded a bit proud.

Luo Yangming: "...Yes."

Just then, hurried footsteps were heard outside, and Li Wanli rushed in.

The silly, hulking man sat down on a chair as soon as he entered, scowling and huffing, "Your Highness! Word came from the Marquis of Jing'an's mansion, saying the Marquis was drunk yesterday and only just woke up today!"

He seemed to have walked in a hurry, and as he spoke, he looked for water, eventually gulping down half a pot of tea in his haste.

"When I went to hold that old scoundrel accountable, he claimed it was the pipa player on the boat who was bold and malicious, wanting to marry into the Prince's mansion but knowing her status as a songstress was too low, so she resorted to a desperate measure. I heard that the pipa player has already committed suicide out of fear of punishment, and he even said if Your Highness is still angry, you can take the body and dispose of it however you like!"

"Bah! The old thing, truly an old fox! How dare he!"

Xie Yunzhou did not speak, but lowered his eyes in thought.

What did he not dare to do?

The Marquis of Jing'an was the Empress Dowager's own brother, the Emperor's uncle. Even without merit, he could clear his name based on this status alone.

Although Xie Yunzhou had glorious military achievements and was the Regent, one person below the Emperor and above ten thousand, he could not use this matter to manipulate him without solid evidence.

After all... this matter brought no benefit to the Marquis of Jing'an at all.

What was the point of tying himself to Shen Lingjiang?

Did he really want to force him to take a wife?

But that held no advantage for the Marquis.

Was this something he wanted to do, or was he instructed by someone else?

That Henian imperial wine; it seemed to have been bestowed by the Emperor himself.

Thinking of this, Xie Yunzhou gave a bitter smile.

The dignity of the Regent already pressured the imperial power; perhaps it was time to gradually let go.

The surface remained calm, and three days passed before Shen Lingjiang gradually regained consciousness.

Shen Lingjiang opened her eyes. She seemed still trapped in a nightmare, staring at the bed curtains for a long time without coming to her senses.

"Oh? You're awake? You truly are precious and pampered; you can really sleep."

Xie Yunzhou, for reasons unknown, was in the room again. Seeing her wake up, he paced to the bedside to throw a jab at her.

Ruyi was serving carefully by the bedside, tucking in the quilt and wiping sweat.

With such a "Great Buddha" in the room, Ruyi didn't even dare to breathe loudly, her movements light and cautious, fearing she might anger this Prince and be tied up and thrown out.

Xie Yunzhou walked to the bed and said coldly to Ruyi, "Go, bring Luo Yangming here to take your mistress's pulse."

Ruyi shrank her neck, wishing she could bristle all over to protect herself. She trembled, not daring to speak, only nodding with her head tucked in before scurrying out.

Shen Lingjiang propped herself up and sat up, shaking her head with a bitter smile. "Who can compare to Your Highness's precious status? You are a person of golden stature, why bother frightening a servant?"

Xie Yunzhou curled his lips and said nothing.

Shen Lingjiang also remained silent for a long time. Her eyes were unfocused, as if she had fallen into some memory, and a flush gradually rose in the depths of her pupils.

After a long while, she suddenly said in a hoarse voice, "The Great Chu was defeated, ceding Xun City and Ming City to Liang."

This topic had veered quite far. Xie Yunzhou pursed his lips in confusion. "Hmm?"

Shen Lingjiang coughed twice, a dry, rasping laugh leaking from her throat, and she continued to ask, "I heard that after the battle of Xun City, where bones piled up to the sky regardless of friend or foe, it was Your Highness who ordered them to be buried?"

Speaking of this, Xie Yunzhou gave a disdainful laugh and said with contempt, "The Great Chu has quite the skill. After the defeat, the commander abandoned the city and fled. When I entered Xun City, there wasn't a single general left, only commoners welcoming us with hoes and sickles. Looking at them, they seemed to have harder bones than the Great Chu's generals."

Speaking of this, Xie Yunzhou was also somewhat puzzled.

He admired Shangguan Ying as an opponent; the military tactics and strategies used in past battles hinted at this person's character, not at all like someone who would abandon a city and flee.

Shen Lingjiang continued to smile and asked back, "How does Your Highness know the commoners' bones are hard? Did you fight them too?"
