It was meant as a jest, but Xie Yunzhou’s face darkened, appearing somewhat displeased. He said, "In war between two nations, we do not harm the common people. Do you think I am like you people of Chu, bullying and torturing civilian captives?"

Shen Lingjiang’s expression stiffened, and she immediately changed her tone. "Yes, it was my slip of the tongue. Your Highness truly possesses the demeanor of a great general."

Xie Yunzhou did not reply, only huffing coldly with a stern face.

Before long, Ruyi led Luo Yangming in, who stepped forward to take her pulse.

"Nothing is wrong now. Continue taking the medicine, and you will recover your spirit after some rest. However, given the nature of your old illness, it will be difficult to fully recover."

She knew her own body well. Shen Lingjiang smiled, nodded gently, and thanked him. "Many thanks, General, for your trouble."

As the saying goes, one does not hit a smiling face. Luo Yangming kept his icy expression and said nothing, though his face looked strangely stiff.

Xie Yunzhou suddenly stood up, turned, and walked out, leaving behind the words, "If you're not dead, let's go."

Luo Yangming immediately bowed to Shen Lingjiang and turned to follow.

Shen Lingjiang let out a breath and sat for a long while before saying, "Ruyi, bring water for me to wash."

Ruyi nodded repeatedly and soon brought in a copper basin filled with water.

Shen Lingjiang put on a robe, got up, and walked over. As she scooped water to wash her face, she suddenly saw her own reflection in the water.

She cried out in surprise, "Ruyi, why is there a bruised finger mark on my chin?"

chapters.title: Clever Calculations
chapters.content:
A few days later, Shen Lingjiang’s health had improved significantly.

At night, draped in a black fox-fur cloak, she carried a candle holder to the desk, sat down, opened a memorial on the table, and began to write.

Just then, Ruyi entered with a bowl of pear soup and saw Shen Lingjiang sitting at the desk.

"Your Highness? Why have you gotten up?"

Ruyi walked over quickly, placed the pear soup on the table, and tilted her head to ask.

Shen Lingjiang covered her mouth and coughed twice before looking up at her. "I've been lying down for several days and am mostly recovered. The matter of the canal cannot be delayed any longer."

Although Xie Yunzhou was treating her a bit better than when they first met, she couldn't remain sickly forever. In this prosperous Yan Capital, useless people could not be kept.

Ruyi nodded, not quite understanding, and pushed the pear soup toward Shen Lingjiang’s hand, urging, "Your Highness, drink some pear soup to sweeten your mouth. Official business is important, but you must also cherish your health. You are naturally frail, so please don't force yourself."

Shen Lingjiang nodded, then looked up at Ruyi.

She had saved this child back in the Great Chu.

She was still young, simple-minded, and lacked strategy or talent. Truth be told, she was of little use for the things Shen Lingjiang was planning.

However, Shen Lingjiang had no one she could fully trust, and Ruyi’s simple nature and talkativeness made her a good companion to have around.

Shen Lingjiang let her thoughts wander for a moment before picking up the small bowl and taking a few sips.

"Cough... Tomorrow, let's go for a walk by the Xiao-Ju River. I heard the canal construction has reached the western section of the Xiao-Ju River; we might as well go and take a look."

Ruyi nodded and replied, "I heard they are dredging the upper western section recently."

Shen Lingjiang: "Dredging?"

Ruyi nodded, her hair bun bobbing along. "Yes, even the Regent took people there today. I heard that for the dredging, even the 'Ping-Shang Lan-Zhou' and the 'Golden Silver Terrace' in the middle section of the river have closed for business, but..."

Shen Lingjiang’s brows furrowed slightly, and she asked quickly, "But what?"

Ruyi curled her lips and muttered softly, "But the Heir of the Marquis of Jing'an refuses to leave, finding a few dancing girls and songstresses to make merry on the boat every day."

Shen Lingjiang lowered her head, masking her long, dark eyelashes. The candlelight flickered, casting spots of light on her face.

"...It's him."

Shen Lingjiang said softly, and listening closely, she seemed to have chuckled.

Ruyi was baffled by her tone, scratching the back of her head while frowning, then watching as Shen Lingjiang continued to write.

The next day, Shen Lingjiang indeed went out with Ruyi.

Xie Yunzhou seemed uneasy about her going out alone and sent Li Wanli to follow.

As she walked, Shen Lingjiang said, "The Great Chu also suffered a major flood a few years ago, with countless casualties. I gained some insights into flood control back then."

Li Wanli followed behind, frowning as he asked, "Your Highness is talking about the Hong River flood three years ago? That flood was very severe; even I heard of it in Great Liang. Hmm... wasn't it said that the Third Princess of Great Chu, Shangguan Ying, went to control the flood herself? I heard she gained a good reputation and won the hearts of the people?"

Shen Lingjiang remained silent, only taking a dragon-scale scroll from Ruyi, opening it, and writing on it.

Li Wanli touched his head blankly and stepped forward to take a look.

"Dredging... Heh, our Prince is taking people to dredge the western section of the river! Flood season sand discharge? Establishing river inspectors? Waterways Supervision Office? What is all this? So complicated?"

Shen Lingjiang laughed upon hearing this and teased, "It is enough for the General to know how to lead troops in battle; you don't need to understand these things. As long as your Prince can understand this scroll, it is enough."

With that, she closed the scroll and walked forward a few steps.

Li Wanli was still confused, scratching his forehead in a dazed manner, muttering, "...Did she just say I have a simple mind?"

They walked all the way to the Ping-Shang Lan-Zhou.

The previously lively painted boats and lantern boats were much quieter. Although one could still hear the pleasant sound of strings and bamboo, it was nothing like the bustle of that day.

Shen Lingjiang suddenly stopped and stared quietly at the massive, magnificent painted boat.

He Weishi’s voice suddenly echoed in her ears again.

"...I heard your mother was a Hu woman from the Yue tribe? Hu women are lowly, but I hear they are all peerlessly beautiful and skilled in singing and dancing."

Shen Lingjiang curled her lips slightly and walked quietly toward that side.

Reaching the riverbank, she reached out and touched the bluestone embankment.

The stone was wet from the river, washed clean and looking as if it had been built recently.

As the riverbed rose, creating a suspended river, the only way to resolve the danger was to add to the embankment day by day.

However, Shen Lingjiang discovered that this newly built embankment seemed to be made of the lowest-grade "tile-blue stone."

Back when the Hong River flooded in Chu, she had gone there herself.

She had heard from veteran flood-control workers that the most taboo material for building embankments was tile-blue stone; it was cheap, but became brittle when exposed to water.

Now, she found that the embankment stone was mixed with a lot of tile-blue stone, and some of it even showed signs of collapse; it probably wouldn't last long.

Shen Lingjiang took a deep breath, scanned the area, and after a moment of silence, asked, "Are there any households nearby?"

Li Wanli shook his head.

Shen Lingjiang asked again, "What about farmland?"

Li Wanli still shook his head, looking bitter as he said, "There used to be an orchard, but isn't it... isn't it that after they cut down the trees, they built this Golden Silver Terrace!"

"They say it's a place of pleasure, but it's actually more like a private villa for the Marquis of Jing'an, only receiving noble families. Commoners avoid this place like the plague!"

Shen Lingjiang nodded and continued, "I heard the Golden Silver Terrace is temporarily closed, which means only the people of the Heir of the Marquis of Jing'an are left here to make merry."

Li Wanli didn't understand why she was asking this, only nodding blankly as he followed her.

Shen Lingjiang said, "Since we are already at the Ping-Shang Lan-Zhou, why don't I go up and persuade the Heir? Lingering here all day is delaying the dredging of the river section."

Li Wanli’s eyes widened in shock.

He had heard about what happened at the Golden Banquet that day. Although the two nations were enemies, He Weishi had been the first to provoke and insult her with crude and vulgar language. Could the Princess really endure even this?

Li Wanli’s eyes were as wide as cow bells as he watched Shen Lingjiang board the Ping-Shang Lan-Zhou.

"Stop! Who goes there! How dare you barge in here!"

A small servant in gray blocked the entrance to the painted boat. He was young but just as arrogant and overbearing as his master, looking down his nose at people.

Shen Lingjiang was not annoyed. She stood where she was and said softly, "My name is Shen Lingjiang, and I am with the Regent. The river dredging is reaching the middle section, so I have come specifically to persuade the Heir to return to his mansion."

Hearing the words "Regent," the servant finally restrained himself slightly and said in a low voice, "It hasn't reached the middle section yet, has it? This Ping-Shang Lan-Zhou is my master's place; the Heir stays if he wants to, and leaves if he wants to!"

Shen Lingjiang continued unhurriedly, "Don't be anxious, little brother. Why don't you pass on a message for me? I will persuade the Heir myself. The Heir knows me; if you report my name to him, he might just be willing to see me."

The servant hesitated for a moment, but eventually turned and entered the boat.

Li Wanli frowned as he listened from behind.

He felt that this Seventh Princess didn't seem very smart, who would go out of their way to seek trouble!

But he couldn't stop her, and in the end, he watched helplessly as Shen Lingjiang was led into the boat by the servant.

"Your Highness! Seventh Princess! If the Heir of Jing'an tries to molest you, just shout! I'll come in and save you immediately!" The big oaf shouted several times toward the boat, finally pacing in circles in his anxiety, muttering to himself, "Don't let anything happen! This is a task assigned by the Prince; if I mess it up, I'll be punished with military rods!"

After muttering, he glanced at Ruyi and continued, "Hey, you girl, why aren't you worried at all? Ugh... no wonder you're so dim-witted; you're just like your mistress!"

Ruyi: "..."

chapters.title: The Exquisite Heart
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang was led by a servant into the pleasure boat, where she saw several dancers in revealing attire spinning and dancing on the stage, accompanied by musicians playing the pipa and konghou.

Upon seeing Shen Lingjiang, He Weishi, who had been embracing a beauty, pushed the woman aside and squinted at Shen Lingjiang for a long moment.

"Oh... if it isn't the Seventh Highness! What? Have you already climbed the high branch of the Regent? Why come here to find this Prince? Looking to stray from your marriage?"

Shen Lingjiang walked in unhurriedly, found an empty seat, and sat down. She looked at He Weishi and said, "Shen Lingjiang has come today to advise the Prince to return to the manor. The river dredging is underway, and with the recent heavy rains, the Ping Shang Lanzhou is too dangerous."

He Weishi burst into loud laughter, so much so that he couldn't hold his wine cup steady, spilling it as it wobbled.

Before he could speak, the beautiful concubine serving him giggled twice, then looked at Shen Lingjiang with a disdainful arch of her brow, saying in a coquettish voice, "This young lady is truly alarmist! We sisters have stayed on the Ping Shang Lanzhou for a long time, sleeping on the boat every night, and nothing has ever happened! Why must you try to scare people, miss?"

"Exactly! Exactly! Is this young lady here specifically to frighten us sisters?"

Another dancer in a red dress drifted over, swaying her waist to He Weishi’s side, and threw herself into his arms with a giggle. "Your Highness, let me toast you!"

As she spoke, she leaned down, her red lips parted slightly, gently catching the rim of the cup, and turned to offer it to He Weishi. He took the cup from her lips, called her "beauty" and "darling" a few times, and finally drank it down with a laugh.

Shen Lingjiang continued, "The stone materials used for the nearby embankments are mixed with 'waqing' stone. This stone becomes brittle when exposed to water and lacks wind resistance; it is not suitable for building embankments. Yet, a great deal of it has been mixed in. If the water levels rise, I fear it will not hold."

He Weishi did not believe her; instead, he looked at Shen Lingjiang with annoyance and cursed, "Who do you think you are! How dare you cast doubt on the river embankments my father is overseeing! Jingtai is my father's fief. By saying the Xiao-Ju River embankment is mixed with waqing stone, are you accusing my father of lining his own pockets, deliberately swapping in inferior materials to embezzle the construction funds?"

The girls beside him chimed in hurriedly, "Exactly! How dare you slander the Marquis!"

"We stay on this boat every day and have seen fierce winds and heavy rains, and nothing has ever happened!"

"What waqing stone? Never heard of it... Is this young lady here to stir up trouble?"

"Your Highness, let's ignore her. Sisters, let's sing and dance for you!"

Shen Lingjiang did not actually suspect the Marquis of Jingan. She assumed he was unaware of the waqing stone; such trivial matters were likely left to subordinates. If he had known, he would never have allowed his own son to build a pleasure pavilion by the river and operate the Ping Shang Lanzhou. However, since Jingtai was his territory, he would be the first to suffer if something went wrong.

Shen Lingjiang suddenly lowered her head and smiled, then said, "Hearing the Prince mention the Marquis, you must be a very filial son. But it is the New Year season, and there is a double celebration at the manor; the Prince should return to reunite with your family."

As she spoke, she looked up slightly to observe He Weishi's expression. It was the end of the year, yet He Weishi was not home for the holidays, spending his days on the boat instead, and no one from the manor had come to find him. Could it be... that a new child had been born, and the Marquis was too busy to manage his disobedient eldest son? Was He Weishi angry about the new addition to the family, and thus refusing to go home?

Indeed.

He Weishi, who had only been slightly annoyed, suddenly flew into a rage. He smashed his wine cup, pushed the beauty in his arms aside, and glared at Shen Lingjiang like a vicious wolf. "Do I need you to teach me how to act? A lowly hostage princess! A bitch born to a low-class slave! Get out!"

Shen Lingjiang didn't even blink, though a dark glint flashed in her eyes. She remained composed and continued, "Why is the Prince angry? A new addition to the family is a joyous occasion, is it not? Speaking of which, I haven't congratulated you on having a new younger brother."

"The young master has just been born; counting it up, this is the first New Year your family is spending together. On such a day of family reunion, why are you lingering on the Ping Shang Lanzhou for so many days? Did the Marquis not send anyone to invite you home?"

If she hadn't said anything, it would have been fine, but the more she spoke, the angrier He Weishi became. He stood up abruptly, kicked over the food table in front of him, and charged toward Shen Lingjiang in a fury, cursing, "You are all bitches born to bitches! What are you, to dare teach me how to act? I said I’m not leaving, and I’m not leaving! Even if the Regent himself came to persuade me, I wouldn't go back!"

As He Weishi ranted and raved, he lunged toward Shen Lingjiang, raising his foot to kick her.

Li Wanli, who had been outside the boat, heard the commotion and burst in just as he saw the young prince acting like a madman. He glared, scanned the room, and seeing a rosewood incense tube in the corner, he kicked it toward He Weishi’s feet.

He Weishi missed his kick, tripped over the tube, and fell flat on his back.

"Get out! Who allowed you to break into my Ping Shang Lanzhou! Get out! All of you, get out!"

He Weishi struggled on the floor like a turtle, unable to get up, roaring in a frenzy.

Li Wanli rolled his eyes and muttered, "As if anyone wants to manage you! You're not my father!"

With that, he supported Shen Lingjiang and said, "Seventh Highness, let's go. Once the dredging workers reach the middle section, the Prince will deal with him himself!"

Shen Lingjiang smiled slightly and said to the thrashing He Weishi and the trembling musicians, "Very well... the message has been delivered. If something happens, it is fate; you cannot blame me."

"Relying on the Empress Dowager's backing, he is truly lawless!"

Li Wanli led Shen Lingjiang out of the Ping Shang Lanzhou. Being a simple-minded man with a hot temper, he couldn't help but curse as soon as they were outside.

Shen Lingjiang didn't answer, but walked to the embankment and stared at it for a long time. Ruyi followed worriedly, casting angry glares toward the direction of the boat.

"General Li," Shen Lingjiang suddenly called out.

Li Wanli stopped and hurried over.

The wind by the river was strong, and perhaps having caught a chill, Shen Lingjiang began to cough.

She coughed as she said, "This is waqing stone; it is black-green in color with fish-scale-like white spots. It is sandy, brittle, and easily forms rock debris after weathering. I have checked; this section of the embankment is mixed with a lot of waqing stone. I must trouble you... cough, cough... to go and inspect the other river sections."

Li Wanli was a martial artist with sharp hearing; he had heard the conversation between Shen Lingjiang and He Weishi from outside, and hearing her mention it again, he was even more furious.

"For such a critical matter as the river embankment, they dare to use inferior stone to make up the numbers! If something goes wrong, ten heads wouldn't be enough to pay for it!"

Shen Lingjiang coughed twice more, covered her lips with a handkerchief, and lowered her eyes. "The situation is urgent, General. Please go and inspect it quickly. My body is truly useless, so I will return to the post house with Ruyi first."

Li Wanli was impatient; after bowing to Shen Lingjiang, he turned and hurried away.

Ruyi frowned, tidying Shen Lingjiang’s wind-blown hair, and muttered, "Should have worn that fox-fur cloak... sigh, the river wind is strong, Highness, let's go back. It's time for your medicine."

chapters.title: A Laughing Support
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang did not move. She stood before the embankment, head bowed, quietly watching the stone wall.

A significant amount of pulverized rock debris had accumulated in the corners. The waqing stone on the embankment had weathered to a pale color and felt very rough to the touch, with a heavy sandy texture; it seemed as if the interior was already hollow.

In fact, all along the way, Shen Lingjiang had been observing. The other sections of the embankment were also mixed with some waqing stone, but the brittleness and weathering were not as severe as in this section. Perhaps it was related to the river; this part of the channel narrowed, the current was faster, and there was no vegetation around, putting more pressure on the embankment.

Seeing her lost in thought, Ruyi tilted her head and called out again, "Highness?"

Shen Lingjiang regained her focus, looked up at the sky, and slowly uttered, "It looks like there will be a heavy rain soon."

Ruyi hurriedly said, "Then let's go back quickly! We didn't bring umbrellas!"

Shen Lingjiang nodded in agreement, tucked her hands into her sleeves, and started walking back, saying slowly, "When the rivers are full, the rain falls like a bursting dam."

Ruyi didn't understand and didn't reply, only urging her to return to the post house quickly.

The two returned to the post house, and Xie Yunzhou and the others didn't return until evening.

At that time, a torrential rain was falling. Thunder and lightning intertwined outside, and dark, gloomy clouds covered the sky. The horizon seemed to have been pierced, and the rain poured down like a basin being overturned. The wind drove the heavy rain, and the water from the eaves fell like ropes.

Xie Yunzhou and his men hadn't brought umbrellas, and they hurried under the eaves, their clothes and hair soaked through.

Shen Lingjiang was just walking slowly toward the corridor with a bowl of medicine. She watched Xie Yunzhou with a hint of schadenfreude, extended the bowl forward, and joked, "Ruyi just brewed this medicine; would the Prince like a bowl to ward off the cold?"

Xie Yunzhou stood under the eaves, wringing out his soaked hem. He glanced at Shen Lingjiang and said irritably, "With the Seventh Highness’s frail constitution, why don't you keep it for yourself?"

With that, he turned and headed into the hall. He was dripping wet, leaving a wet footprint with every step of his boots.

Shen Lingjiang tilted her head and followed, trailing at a distance, and asked again, "Prince, compared to the Xiao-Ju River water from earlier today, which one is cooler?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou paused, turned his head, and looked at Shen Lingjiang behind him.

Shen Lingjiang was wearing a snow-blue outfit, wrapped in that black fox-fur cloak. She was dressed neatly and covered tightly from head to toe, but the moment Xie Yunzhou looked at her, he inexplicably recalled the butterfly bones beneath her soaked inner garment and her thin, straight spine.

Xie Yunzhou stared at her for a long time, until Shen Lingjiang couldn't help but frown, starting to regret her teasing. This scoundrel was wearing his fox-fur cloak, yet dared to mock him.

Xie Yunzhou’s eyes darkened. He suddenly strode toward Shen Lingjiang, grabbed his soaked sleeve, and wiped it across her face, saying in a rough, cold voice, "Which one is cooler? Why don't you try it yourself and find out."

Shen Lingjiang: "Mm... Unh..."

Shen Lingjiang was pushed back by him, but unfortunately, there was a pillar behind her. She was blocked in place and had her face wiped by his soaked sleeve. His movements were fast and rough, and his strength was great, as if he were using her face as a washboard, wanting to rub a layer of skin off.

"Prince, wipe it..."

Just then, Luo Yangming hurried over, holding a dry towel. He saw this scene as soon as he arrived and was so shocked that he couldn't finish his sentence.

"Pfft... cough..."

He stood there, stunned, while Li Wanli, hiding at the door, covered his mouth to stifle a laugh. The man’s face turned red as he suppressed the laughter that threatened to spill out.

Luo Yangming took a deep breath and muttered irritably, "...What are you laughing at? Did water get into your brain too?"

Li Wanli coughed twice, suppressing his laughter, and whispered, "First time seeing the Prince like this..."

Luo Yangming took another deep breath, as if wanting to say something, but couldn't find the words, so he just glared at Li Wanli.

Li Wanli didn't know, and continued to mutter, "My sister and I used to play like this when we were kids... but the Prince and this Seventh Highness have unusual statuses. Do you think this is inappropriate?"

Luo Yangming: "Heh."

Li Wanli frowned and glared at him. "Sss... your brain must have water in it, laughing like that."

Luo Yangming: "..."

Xie Yunzhou naturally heard the conversation between his two subordinates. He slowed his movements and finally withdrew his hand in silence.

Shen Lingjiang: "Cough... cough, cough..."

Being covered and rubbed by him, she coughed several times. She turned slightly and raised her sleeve to wipe her face.

"Prince, how old are you this year? Are you still a child?"

She tilted her head and glanced at Xie Yunzhou, her tone slow and leisurely. Half of her face was turned toward him; her chin was rubbed bright red, her cheeks were flushed, and even her lips had gained a vivid color... as if they had been fiercely toyed with and rubbed.

Xie Yunzhou’s heart skipped a beat, and he hurriedly looked away.

"Wan... Wanli!"

He suddenly turned and shouted, startling Li Wanli at the door, whose lazy posture instantly straightened.

Xie Yunzhou: "Didn't you go to inspect the waqing stone just now? Take some men and reinforce all the marked areas!"

Li Wanli replied in a booming voice: "Yes!"

Li Wanli and Luo Yangming retreated. Xie Yunzhou didn't speak again; he didn't even look at Shen Lingjiang, but hurried back to his room to change his clothes.

Shen Lingjiang stared at his back for a moment, then withdrew her gaze and prepared to finish the remaining half-bowl of medicine. But as soon as she raised her hand, she saw that the black liquid in the bowl had spilled out, staining even her snow-blue sleeves.

Shen Lingjiang: "...I think he’s the one with water in his brain, acting like a madman."

Ruyi shook her head and sighed, stepping closer and whispering, "Highness only dares to mutter behind his back."

Shen Lingjiang glared at her. "Good Ruyi, didn't you just hide outside and watch the fun? Is it fun to watch your master being bullied?"

Ruyi giggled twice, trying to curry favor by leaning closer. "Highness! There is more medicine in the stove; I'll ladle some more for you!"

Hearing this, Shen Lingjiang stepped back half a pace, about to speak. Suddenly, a shout came from Xie Yunzhou’s room.

"Shen Lanshu!"

Shen Lingjiang stepped back another half pace and said, "The Prince is calling me; I'll go see."

With that, she turned and walked toward the back. Ruyi couldn't stop her, stomping her feet in frustration. "Highness! Highness! You haven't finished your medicine!"

Shen Lingjiang didn't stop, walking even faster. Ruyi stomped her feet again, muttering to herself, "Calling others a child, but I don't think the Highness is any better."

chapters.title: Pleasant Conversation
chapters.content:
Shen Lingjiang did not hear Ruyi’s muttering. She pushed open the door and entered Xie Yunzhou’s room, finding that he had already changed his clothes. He was sitting behind a long desk, holding a dragon-scale scroll, the one she had written that day, and was flipping through it, reading carefully.

Seeing her enter, Xie Yunzhou looked up, then immediately averted his gaze. He asked in a deep voice, "These... did you write them?"

Shen Lingjiang nodded and walked over slowly, saying as she moved, "The Hong River in Great Chu is very similar to the Little Ju River. I learned a few things about flood control back then."

Hearing this, Xie Yunzhou looked up again to size her up. "The Hong River floods... I recall that it was Shangguan Ying who went to manage the water that time?"

It was a treacherous, dangerous place, yet Shangguan Ying had gone in person as an imperial princess. After successfully managing the flood, she gained great renown and was highly revered by the common people.

Shen Lingjiang said nothing, merely lowering her eyes as if lost in thought.

Xie Yunzhou said with a half-smile, "So, you are just following the pattern, learning from your elder sister?"

Shen Lingjiang sighed slightly, the corners of her mouth curling up involuntarily. She said indifferently, "If the Prince says so, then so be it."

Seeing her put on that mask of a fake smile again, Xie Yunzhou couldn't help but frown, finding it extremely grating.

He suppressed his smile, tapped his fingers on the desk, and said, "Sit."

Shen Lingjiang walked over and sat opposite him. The two stopped making small talk and began to discuss the contents of the scroll in detail.

"The Little Ju River has a lot of silt and a swift current. If the canal is to be connected to it, that is the first major challenge," Shen Lingjiang said, taking a scroll of paper nearly four feet wide from her sleeve. She spread it out on the desk and held the ends down with paperweights. "We can start from here, building four sluice gates along the river to regulate the water and keep it flowing. When the water is full, we open the gates to release it immediately."

"I have seen the blueprints for the dredging; they were set here, but I’m afraid this location won't work. I noticed it during my boat trip last time. There are towering rocks on both banks here. Although the current isn't as turbulent as elsewhere, it is too close to the Jing River. If we encounter the spring and summer rainy seasons, I fear there will be a risk of the river water backflowing."

Xie Yunzhou listened to her and picked up the blueprint on the table to examine it closely.

He asked, "Is this a new drawing you made today?"

Shen Lingjiang replied, "I returned early, so I drew a bit."

Xie Yunzhou curled his lip and let out a scoff. "When you had me tied to the couch the other day, you certainly had the leisure to observe other things."

Shen Lingjiang was silent for a moment, then said leisurely, "Does the Prince perhaps wish that I had observed your weak state while lying on the couch instead?"

Weak?

Who was he calling weak?

Xie Yunzhou glared at her fiercely, gritting his teeth. "Your tongue is as sharp as a blade. Sooner or later, I will seal your mouth shut."

Shen Lingjiang: "The Prince had better not worry about my mouth for now; it would be better to look at the business at hand."

Xie Yunzhou fell silent and lowered his head to look at the blueprint again.

Shen Lingjiang pointed to several spots on the map and continued, "We can excavate a canal here specifically for water transport, and then connect the east and west sections through this river segment. We should set up more auxiliary channels, I have marked them on the map, to divert water through branch canals. Here and here, we can set up ports. Since the Little Ju River is turbulent, we could also establish a Water Conservancy Inspectorate to patrol the river regularly and dredge the channel in time."

The two talked for a long time.

The canal project was vast and complex; it couldn't be finished in a day. They talked for two days, then three. Today they discussed ship locks, tomorrow they discussed aqueducts, and they actually found themselves in a pleasant conversation.

After a few days, their relationship had eased considerably.

Xie Yunzhou was a man who cherished talent, which was precisely why he could never forget Shangguan Ying from the enemy state.

After talking for a few days, his attitude toward Shen Lingjiang had changed; even his eyes seemed to carry a hint of appreciation.

On the night of the third day, the two were locked in the room, discussing a critical point, when hurried footsteps sounded outside.

"Your Highness! Your Highness!"

"Something terrible has happened! The dam in the middle section of the river has collapsed! The Ping Shang Lanzhou and the Jin Yin Tai have been submerged, and the heir to the Marquis of Jing'an is missing!"

Xie Yunzhou was startled. He stood up abruptly and walked toward the door, asking as he went, "What? The levee collapsed?"

He strode to the door, pushed it open forcefully, and frowned at Li Wanli, who was standing outside.

Shen Lingjiang remained seated steadily at the desk. Upon hearing this, she only lowered her eyelashes slightly and, without haste, picked up the tea on the table and took a light sip.

As the lukewarm tea went down her throat, the corners of Shen Lingjiang's lips curled slightly as she listened intently to the conversation between Xie Yunzhou and Li Wanli.

Li Wanli looked anxious, his speech rapid. "It collapsed! But fortunately, it only collapsed in that one spot. Yang Ming has already taken men to handle the emergency. It’s just... the heir to the Marquis of Jing'an was still on the Ping Shang Lanzhou. I fear he is in grave danger... The Marquis of Jing'an has also received the news and is already on his way."

Xie Yunzhou’s brows were locked tight. He immediately asked, "He Weishi? Why was he still on the Ping Shang Lanzhou? Didn't I order the people to be cleared from the Ping Shang Lanzhou and the Jin Yin Tai long ago?"

Xie Yunzhou had been busy with the river dredging in recent days, and with the continuous heavy rain over the past two days, he hadn't gone out, staying in the room with Shen Lingjiang to discuss the details of the canal excavation, completely forgetting about the Marquis of Jing'an's heir.

Li Wanli sighed twice, so angry that he slammed his right fist into his left palm. He said irritably, "It’s his own fault! The Seventh Prince even went to persuade him personally, but he refused to leave! Yesterday, when we arranged for workers to reinforce the dam, he complained that it was noisy and disturbed his dancing and music, so he drove all the workers away! You tell me, with that kind of behavior, if he doesn't die, who will?"

That might be true. But He Weishi was, after all, He Yuming's eldest son. If he died on the Little Ju River, it was likely that He Yuming would obstruct the canal project even more.

Xie Yunzhou rubbed his temples, paused for a moment, and asked, "Apart from the Ping Shang Lanzhou, were there any other casualties? Were any forests or lands destroyed, or houses washed away?"

Hearing this, Shen Lingjiang put down her teacup and stood up to walk over.

This was the silver lining in a dark cloud. Li Wanli let out a sigh of relief and replied, "Fortunately, the Jin Yin Tai is in a remote location. There are no villages nearby, and the original fruit forests had already been cleared. Plus, because we were reinforcing the dam these past two days, we had surrounded the river and forbidden people from approaching, so the flood only destroyed the pleasure boats and the Jin Yin Tai."

Only then did Xie Yunzhou breathe a sigh of relief.

He Weishi had sought his own death; it wasn't a pity if he didn't survive, but...

Seeing him frown, Shen Lingjiang glanced at him and asked out of the blue, "Is the Prince worried that the Marquis of Jing'an will use this to cause trouble?"

Xie Yunzhou coughed lightly, straightened his back, and replied, "Would I be afraid of him? It was He Weishi who sought his own death; it’s not like I threw him into the river to drown."

Shen Lingjiang nodded, following his lead. "That is exactly the point."

"Actually, the Prince doesn't need to worry. That Marquis of Jing'an is probably more anxious than you are right now."

Xie Yunzhou turned to look at her upon hearing this, and after thinking it over, he immediately understood.

Only Li Wanli was a bit slow. He looked completely bewildered, asking foolishly, "What? Isn't the Marquis of Jing'an grieving? How could he have time to be anxious?"

chapters.title: Heaven's Assistance
chapters.content:
Xie Yunzhou glanced at Li Wanli and said, "The levee of the Little Ju River was built with inferior stone as a substitute for quality. Regardless of whether the Marquis of Jing'an knew about it, this Jing Terrace is his territory. Now that the stone levee has been washed away by the flood, if he isn't anxious, who would be?"

It was his own agitation from earlier that had prevented him from thinking of this layer immediately.

Li Wanli suddenly realized and said, "Then this time we must make the Marquis of Jing'an pay! He has to pay for the reconstruction of the dam! The funds allocated by the Ministry of Revenue are already insufficient; we have to scrape together whatever we can!"

Shen Lingjiang nodded slightly and added, "Since the Jin Yin Tai has been destroyed, we can take this opportunity to return the land to the people for forestry."

"As the ancients said, 'When the grass and trees are flourishing, the axe should not enter the mountains, so as not to stunt their growth or cut off their life.' Cutting down trees to build estates was foolish to begin with."

Li Wanli, a warrior, didn't understand. He nodded in confusion, finally spitting out two words: "Foolish!"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou rolled his eyes at him and said with a half-smile, "Go get a straw raincoat and hat. After all, he lost his own son; I should go and offer my condolences to the Marquis."

Li Wanli immediately replied, "Yes!"

Before long, the two of them put on their rain gear and went out.

Shen Lingjiang stood under the veranda, watching them walk away. After a long while, she said to herself in a leisurely tone, "It wasn't me who killed you; this is Heaven helping me."

Xie Yunzhou went to offer his hypocritical condolences and then, citing the issue of the inferior stone, demanded 30,000 taels of silver from the Marquis of Jing'an.

The body of his own son hadn't even been recovered yet, and the old man He Yuming was so angry that he fainted on the shore.

Come to think of it, Heaven was truly "considerate." After all that turmoil, the sky cleared up, and there were no more days of torrential rain.

On this day, the weather warmed up, and a warm, yellow sun actually appeared. Shen Lingjiang led Ruyi out, saying they were going out to soak up the sun.

Recently, there had been many matters regarding the canal, and Xie Yunzhou had no time to manage her, nor did he send anyone to follow her. She had finally gained some rare freedom.

Shen Lingjiang wore a robe of white with silver floral patterns, her waist cinched with a ringed belt, and her hair tied with a ribbon of the same color, giving her an air of refined nobility.

Ruyi nodded secretly and muttered in a low voice, "Your Highness, it’s actually quite good following the Regent. We have food, lodging... and even clothes."

Shen Lingjiang feigned a fierce look and tapped her on the head, saying irritably, "I spent three nights drawing over a dozen blueprints for him to get this outfit. You think it was so easy to come by?"

Ruyi rubbed her forehead and giggled for a long time, then reached out to touch the fabric, muttering to herself, "This material feels so good; it must be very expensive."

Shen Lingjiang raised her eyebrows slightly and subconsciously smoothed her collar.

It did feel comfortable, and the texture was excellent.

Shen Lingjiang held the title of Imperial Princess and had seen many fine things, but these fine things had never been for her to use. Just like this cloud-silk satin, she had never worn it before.

Shen Lingjiang collected her thoughts and looked up at the market.

It looked somewhat desolate; there were few people and few vendors.

Shen Lingjiang frowned, subconsciously counting on her fingers, and then her frown deepened.

She tilted her head to look at Ruyi and asked, "Isn't today the Lantern Festival? Why is the street empty?"

Ruyi curled her lips secretly and leaned in to whisper, "I heard the Marquis of Jing'an forbade the city's commoners from celebrating. They say the body of the Marquis's heir hasn't been found yet, and the Marquis is so angry and anxious that he ordered no red lanterns to be hung in the city for the Lantern Festival."

Shen Lingjiang raised her eyebrows and smiled. "How overbearing."

Ruyi imitated her expression and nodded repeatedly.

"It’s rare to have some free time; I was thinking of enjoying the lanterns tonight." Shen Lingjiang wore an expression of regret and let out a long sigh, but looking at her eyes, there seemed to be a hint of joy.

Ruyi couldn't see through it and just asked, "Does Your Highness also like lanterns?"

Shen Lingjiang didn't answer, just looked at her with a smile.

Ruyi nodded and continued, "When I was little, my family was poor, so we couldn't afford lanterns even on holidays. But my mother would buy me pine nut candy during the festivals! It was so delicious! Sweet and sugary!"

Her eyes were bright, as if she had fallen into some memory.

Seeing Ruyi like this, Shen Lingjiang couldn't help but recall some past events.

She walked with her head lowered for a long time before finally saying, "I lived with my mother when I was little. The Yue people don't have our festivals, and they don't celebrate the Lantern Festival. Their customs and habits are different from ours. I was very curious back then, so every year for the Lantern Festival, my mother would make lanterns herself. She learned specifically to coax me."

Ruyi’s eyes went wide, and she asked curiously, "That must have been beautiful!"

Shen Lingjiang seemed amused by her expression and laughed out loud. After a long while, she shook her head and said slowly, "To tell you the truth... they were quite ugly."

"My mother wasn't good at handicrafts; she wasn't good at cooking, and she wasn't good at making lanterns. Those lanterns were crooked, neither round nor square, and looked strange. They barely held together without falling apart. When I was young, I wasn't used to the food of the Yue people, so she would make things herself. Either she would get burned here, or cut there, and the things she made were barely edible..."

Ruyi watched Shen Lingjiang speak quietly. There was a smile on the Princess's face, but Ruyi always felt that her eyes seemed very sad.

After a long while, Ruyi said dryly, "Your Highness and your mother had a very close relationship."

Shen Lingjiang suddenly stopped walking and turned to look at Ruyi sharply, her smile mocking. "You call her 'Your Ladyship'?"

Ruyi: "...Ah?"

Shen Lingjiang said again, "You call me 'Your Highness', and you call her 'Your Ladyship'?"

Shen Lingjiang was still smiling, the corners of her mouth curling up, her eyes slightly curved, her tone flat and slow, but Ruyi was suddenly panicked, not knowing how to answer.

"Your... Your Highness?"

Shen Lingjiang didn't speak, nor did she get angry. She suppressed her smile, turned her head, and continued walking. She walked for a long time, and just when Ruyi thought she wouldn't speak again, she suddenly saw Shen Lingjiang take out money to buy two sticks of candied haws.

She handed one to her and said softly, "There are too few vendors on the street; I couldn't find pine nut candy. Just make do with this."

Ruyi: "Ah, oh... thank you, Your Highness."

Shen Lingjiang bit into a red hawthorn covered in sugar syrup and suddenly asked, "Ruyi, you mentioned pine nut candy so suddenly, were you missing your mother?"

Ruyi blinked, not answering immediately. Instead, she muttered to herself, thinking that this question should have been asked of the Princess, after all, she was the one who had said more.

But she felt that the Princess was a bit strange today, so she didn't dare ask more, answering in a low voice, "Well, I was sold when I was very young, so I don't remember my mother's face anymore."

...Face?

Shen Lingjiang’s heart trembled. She suddenly looked up and scanned her surroundings, then stared blankly at the distant city gate.

The city gate in front of her was very high; even from a distance, Shen Lingjiang could still see it.

But the city gate in her memory was even higher. She had been hung upon it, her hair disheveled, and she, too, could not see her own face.

"Your Highness?"

chapters.title: Feelings Hard to Suppress
chapters.content:
Seeing Shen Lingjiang lost in thought again, Ruyi called out to her in a low voice, her brows knitted with worry as she watched her.

Shen Lingjiang let out a sigh, regained her focus, and continued walking, saying, "I'll buy you some pine nut candies when we return to Yandu."

Ruyi did not respond with joy; instead, she bit her lip and looked at Shen Lingjiang with concern.

Shen Lingjiang said nothing more, walking along while biting into the candied hawthorn in her hand.

When she finished the last piece of candy, she stopped and stood before a mansion gate.

"Jing'an Marquis Mansion... Your Highness! It's the residence of the Marquis of Jing'an!"

Shen Lingjiang glanced at the white mourning banners and lanterns hanging on the gate. Although the gates were closed, one could faintly hear the sounds of heart-wrenching wailing from within.

While those inside wept in grief, Shen Lingjiang curled the corners of her lips, then slowly shifted her gaze and continued walking, remarking, "People stepping out into the spring sun, truly a fine season. How joyous and congratulatory."

Shen Lingjiang led Ruyi for a stroll through the market before returning to the post house. Judging by her expression, she seemed quite pleased.

The Marquis of Jing'an had lost his son, and the Xiaoju River levee had been breached, flooding the Golden Silver Terrace.

Xie Yunzhou had been busy with this matter for several days, returning late every night. After much labor, the newly reinforced levee was finally completed, and the new plan for the canal had been discussed with the veteran craftsmen and finalized, waiting only for the excavation to connect them.

As soon as Xie Yunzhou returned to the post house, he went to find Shen Lingjiang. The mistress and servant were sitting across from each other at a desk, with Ruyi seemingly busy transcribing something.

Hearing Xie Yunzhou enter, Shen Lingjiang looked up and glanced at him, asking coolly, "When will the Prince learn to knock before entering a room?"

Xie Yunzhou, who had pushed the door open and walked straight in, stopped at the threshold, raised an eyebrow, and tapped the half-open wooden door heavily twice.

Shen Lingjiang remained silent for a moment, then looked down and signaled Ruyi to withdraw.

Ruyi kept her head buried, quickly gathered the pages she had been transcribing, and hurried out the door.

As she passed Xie Yunzhou, she lowered her head even further, muttered a soft "Greetings, Your Highness," and then fled as if her tail were on fire.

As she passed, Xie Yunzhou saw clearly that the little attendant was holding a few sheets of very thin tracing paper, on which were written simple phrases from texts like Zengguang Xianwen and Liweng Duyun.

Seeing her look like a "mouse seeing a cat," Xie Yunzhou frowned and rubbed his chin, pondering whether he was truly that terrifying. This girl trembled every time she saw him, as if he were a man-eater.

"Indeed, the Prince carries an air of slaughter, so naturally, Ruyi is afraid."

Shen Lingjiang seemed to see through his thoughts and said indifferently.

Xie Yunzhou did not answer, withdrew his gaze, and walked toward the desk.

He saw Shen Lingjiang tidying the papers on the table, stacking them neatly one by one.

Xie Yunzhou picked one up to look at it. It was in Shen Lingjiang's handwriting, the last line reading, "Be cautious in all things, and above all, do not deceive your heart."

He had barely glanced at it when Shen Lingjiang snatched the paper from his hand.

She stacked it with the others, and while organizing them with lowered eyes, she said, "I was just teaching Ruyi to write a few characters in my spare time. Please don't look, Your Highness."

That was it. The handwriting on the papers the little attendant held had faint traces of Shen Lingjiang's style, though it was a mere imitation of the surface without the soul.

Xie Yunzhou withdrew his hand nonchalantly and asked, "Did you write these copybooks for her?"

Shen Lingjiang nodded.

Xie Yunzhou added, "You are quite good to your servants."

Shen Lingjiang nodded again, smiling faintly without speaking.

Xie Yunzhou watched her for a long time, then narrowed his eyes and continued, "You seem to be in a good mood as well."

Shen Lingjiang raised an eyebrow slightly and asked, "What makes you say that?"

Xie Yunzhou sat at the desk, propped his chin on one hand, and watched her for a long while before saying leisurely, "He Weishi is dead, hence your good mood."

Shen Lingjiang’s movements paused; she finally looked up at Xie Yunzhou, meeting his gaze.

"Your Highness says that as if... I have been holding a grudge against the Heir?"

Xie Yunzhou countered, "Is that not the case?"

Shen Lingjiang’s tone faltered. After a brief silence, she suddenly laughed. Unlike her usual fake smiles, this one was somewhat genuine and carefree.

She stopped what she was doing, rested both hands on the desk, leaned forward slightly, and whispered slowly, "Your Highness is quite right... Shen Lingjiang is a person with a heart like a scorpion, calculating every penny and seeking revenge for every slight."

"He offended me, so naturally I held a grudge. It is only a pity that He Weishi was unlucky and didn't give me the chance to take my revenge."

Xie Yunzhou narrowed his eyes.

Night had fallen, and the room was lit only by a bronze lamp on the desk.

The flickering flame cast a reddish glow upon Shen Lingjiang’s face.

She was as beautiful as when he first met her, delicate features, brows like distant mountains, and a perpetual pallor that made her lips appear exceptionally vivid.

Shen Lingjiang was born beautiful.

Xie Yunzhou had known this since they first met, but back then, he had only seen her as a useless, embroidered pillow, a delicate, fragile flower.

But now, the thorns on the flower’s stem were all standing upright, unobtrusive, yet sharp.

Only now did he feel that this flower had truly come alive.

Xie Yunzhou leaned forward, mimicking her posture, and lowered his voice: "Because he humiliated you with a dancing girl? That is why you hold a grudge?"

Shen Lingjiang did not answer immediately.

Xie Yunzhou tilted his head, frowning, as if muttering to himself or asking, "If so... then didn't I also mock you back then? By that logic, shouldn't you hold an even greater grudge against me? Isn't keeping you by my side like burying a firecracker for myself?"

Shen Lingjiang smiled slightly. "Then the Prince must be very careful."

Xie Yunzhou said no more, his head tilted as he stared into Shen Lingjiang’s eyes.

She loved to smile and was adept at masking her thoughts. Just looking at her, he could see through nothing... though the red mole beneath her eyelid was particularly striking, seeming to soften its sharp, dazzling edge under the candlelight, becoming tender and lovely.

After a long while, Xie Yunzhou suddenly stood up and tossed out, "The canal matters are mostly settled. Pack your things; we return to the capital tomorrow with me."

With that, he turned and quickly left the room.

Just outside the door, Xie Yunzhou found Ruyi huddled there. Seeing him emerge, she shrank her neck and trembled like a startled quail.

Xie Yunzhou’s gaze dropped to the stack of tracing papers she still held, and he noticed that one of Shen Lingjiang’s drafts had been mixed in.

Perhaps she had grabbed it by mistake in her haste.

It was a Rhapsody on Bamboo. Remembering that Shen Lingjiang hadn't let him see it earlier, Xie Yunzhou raised an eyebrow and suddenly called out to Ruyi, "Come here."

Ruyi shuddered, her mouth pouting as she replied, "Your... Your Highness! W-what are your orders!"

Xie Yunzhou reached out and snatched the Rhapsody on Bamboo from her arms, folded it twice, tucked it into his sleeve, and said briefly, "I’ll take this."

Ruyi: "..."

While Ruyi was stunned, she watched the dignified Regent, the renowned God of War of the Great Liang, snatch her things and stride away.

Ruyi’s mouth pouted even more. She watched him walk away with trembling legs before running into the room, wailing, "Your Highness! Your Highness! The Regent snatched the copybook you wrote for me!"

chapters.title: Difficult to Serve
chapters.content:
The next day, Shen Lingjiang dressed neatly, wrapped herself in her black fox fur cloak, and wandered into the backyard of the post house.

Xie Yunzhou’s mount, Longmei, seemed to recognize her; tethered in the stable, it stretched its neck to nuzzle Shen Lingjiang’s hand and tugged at her sleeve, pulling her toward the fodder.

Ruyi followed behind, whispering, "Is Longmei hungry?"

Shen Lingjiang: "...Didn't I tell you? This horse is called 'Longmei'."

Ruyi, perhaps still holding a grudge about the horse's owner snatching her paper yesterday, pouted and muttered even more quietly, "I'll just call it... I'll call it secretly! Longmei, Longmei, Longmei!"

Shen Lingjiang was speechless. After a moment, she grabbed some fodder and fed the black horse.

To her surprise, the horse kicked its hooves, curled its lip, and snorted, refusing to eat.

Seeing this, Ruyi couldn't help but chuckle: "Your Highness, you gave it dried hay. Maybe this horse likes fresh grass!"

Shen Lingjiang nodded in agreement and fed it a handful of fresh grass.

This time it was right; the black horse opened its mouth and rolled the grass inside.

Shen Lingjiang found it quite novel, fed it another handful, and muttered to herself, "Quite picky, just as difficult to serve as its master."

"I am not picky."

Xie Yunzhou appeared out of nowhere, interjecting coldly.

This gave Ruyi a real fright; she shrank behind Shen Lingjiang, trembling and daring not say a word.

Shen Lingjiang, however, smiled slightly and feigned ignorance: "Oh... who is picky? Did someone say the Prince is picky? That shouldn't be! Look at the Prince, so sturdy and robust, one look and you can tell he can eat three bowls of rice at a meal. He must be the easiest person in the world to feed!"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Based on his experience lately, Xie Yunzhou knew he couldn't win an argument with her. He simply glared at Shen Lingjiang, silently led Longmei out, and mounted the horse.

He trotted slowly around the courtyard before suddenly leaning down and sweeping Shen Lingjiang up in front of him. The person in front of him gasped in surprise, instinctively clutching Xie Yunzhou’s clothes.

Seeing Shen Lingjiang’s flustered appearance, Xie Yunzhou felt he had won a round and couldn't help but curl his lips. Finally, he slapped the horse’s back and shouted, "Let's go, back to the capital!"

The horse’s hooves thundered, and they were gone in a flash.

Ruyi blinked, standing rooted to the spot in a daze. It took a long time for her to recover, and she screamed, "Your Highness! Your Highness..."

Luo Yangming, clutching his sword, glanced at her, likely annoyed by the noise, and said irritably, "Stop shouting. The Prince isn't going to eat your mistress."

On the other side, Li Wanli was also dumbfounded, shaking his head and sighing, "What a blatant lie! The Prince’s waist is not round at all!"

As he spoke, he gestured with his hands, looking quite unconvinced. "The Prince has a 'dog’s waist', broad shoulders and a narrow waist. It’s a top-tier physique!"

Luo Yangming rolled his eyes again, glared at him, and cursed angrily, "Shut up too! What you said wasn't any better!"

With that, he led his own horse from the stable, mounted it, looked down at Ruyi, and said coldly, "Get on."

Ruyi: "..."

She felt that "get on" sounded more like "give me your life."

Ruyi was startled and instinctively looked at Li Wanli.

Li Wanli shrugged and spread his hands, saying, "I’m not going back to the capital with you. The canal work isn't finished; the Prince left me behind to supervise."

Ruyi’s mouth pouted, and she looked at Luo Yangming on his horse, her body trembling again.

Li Wanli, seeing her pitiful state, sighed and patted her shoulder, comforting her: "Don't be afraid. Yangming just has a cold temperament; he’s actually a good person. He usually doesn't kill people."

Ruyi was stunned: "...Ah?"

Luo Yangming stepped into the stirrups, rolled his eyes even more frequently, pulled the reins to move closer, and leaned down to hoist Ruyi onto the horse like a chick, muttering with disdain, "What a nuisance."

Ruyi lay horizontally across the horse’s back. At this moment, the urge to survive was stronger than her fear.

She raised her hand tremblingly and protested weakly, "G-General... can I sit up? This position makes me want to vomit."

Luo Yangming rolled his eyes again and adjusted her position. Ruyi let out a breath, looking as if she had finally come back to life.

Luo Yangming withdrew his focus, snapped the reins, and rode off.

Li Wanli watched them for a long time, chewing on a blade of grass, before muttering, "See? Even being that impatient, he didn't kill anyone. Yangming is really much better than before."

Two horses and four people headed toward Yandu, galloping all the way.

Inside the Chuigong Hall, the golden dragons coiled around the beams. Beneath the cinnabar steps and vermilion windows, the towering red-lacquered pillars supported eaves with intricate brackets, topped with dense, scale-like glazed green tiles that shimmered with brilliance.

"...If there are matters to report, speak; if not, the court is dismissed!"

The personal eunuch beside the Emperor drawled in a shrill voice.

Below, the numerous officials, dressed in scarlet or blue, stood in rows.

Upon hearing this, one civil official holding an ivory tablet stepped forward, bowed, and said, "Your Majesty, I have heard that the Regent recently visited Jingtai to inspect the canal. Due to consecutive heavy rains, the Xiaoju River in Jingtai surged, breaching the levee and destroying buildings along the banks."

After the New Year, the Marquis of Jing'an had also returned to Yandu from Jingtai.

Perhaps because he had just lost his son, his complexion was poor; he looked ten years older, and his hair had turned much whiter.

Hearing the other official bring it up, he immediately replied, "Reporting to Your Majesty! The supervision of the levee was indeed due to my lax discipline, which allowed subordinates to take advantage of the situation and substitute inferior materials. I discussed this in detail with the Prince that day and am willing to use my family’s wealth to rebuild the levee to make up for my failure."

The official who spoke first glanced at the Marquis. "It is truly a tragedy for the Marquis to bury his own son. However..."

He paused slightly, turned toward the dragon throne in the center, and continued, bowing his back: "However, this is a matter of great importance. Why did the Prince not report it to Your Majesty before making plans? To... to order the Marquis to use private funds to repair the levee... is this not overstepping his authority?"

Xie Yunzhou stood in the front row, his expression unchanged, quietly waiting for the official to finish.

Only when the official finished did he glance back. The man was a Censor.

If he remembered correctly, this man was one of Xie Yunqi’s people.

Xie Yunqi, the sixth son of the late Emperor and one of the two Princes, was, by calculation, Xie Yunzhou’s elder brother.

Since the Golden Banquet, Xie Yunqi had been claiming illness and staying in his residence; he hadn't even attended today’s court session. No one knew just how ill he really was.

chapters.title: Acknowledging the Marriage Alliance
chapters.content:
Xie Yunzhou paused slightly, pondered for a moment, and then stepped forward to reply: "Your Majesty, the situation was critical that day. The Xiao-Ju River was rising and would not recede, and the stone embankment was filled with inferior rubble. To prevent further damage to the dam, we had no choice but to prioritize reinforcement. Jingtai is densely populated; if a flood were to occur, the casualties would be countless. In that emergency, I had no choice but to order the construction of the dam. However, the project was massive, and the public treasury was insufficient. It was Lord He who, out of concern for the people, was willing to provide the funds to resolve the urgent crisis."

These words effectively pushed He Yuming into the spotlight, leaving him standing there, unable to either admit or deny it.

The Censor, holding his tablet, seemed to want to say more, but a senior official in the front row suddenly spoke up.

He was dressed in deep purple court robes embroidered with snow-white cranes. He stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty, although this matter was handled irregularly, there was a cause, and it is understandable. The dam had already been destroyed; we could not have waited for the Prince to submit a memorial, for us to debate it in court for two days, and only then decide on a strategy. If we had delayed like that, I fear the rain in Jingtai would have already stopped."

This man’s surname was Lou, given name "Lou Liangyu." He was the head of the civil officials and the Grand Tutor of the Great Liang.

With Grand Tutor Lou speaking, the Censor knew he could not continue. He lowered his head and signaled to someone else.

Before long, another man stepped out.

"Your Majesty! I impeach the Regent!"

The young Emperor on the dragon throne remained silent for a long time, his expression unreadable.

After a long while, having watched for quite some time, he finally spoke.

His voice was low, devoid of any discernible joy or anger: "Presumptuous."

The man’s legs trembled, and he immediately knelt on the ground, his hands shaking as he held his tablet and finished his statement: "I impeach the Regent for privately keeping a hostage princess from an enemy state and even taking her out of the capital!"

The Emperor remained silent for a moment before shifting his gaze to Xie Yunzhou, calling out neither lightly nor heavily: "Imperial Uncle?"

Xie Yunzhou sighed, lowered his eyes to glance at the kneeling official, and then looked back at the Emperor: "Your Majesty, wasn't that woman a gift from the Emperor of Zhao to me?"

A commotion broke out below.

The kneeling official was also stunned, not expecting Xie Yunzhou to answer this way.

The Emperor of Great Chu did indeed have the intention of sending an imperial daughter for a marriage alliance.

However, everyone in Great Liang treated this as a joke, believing it impossible that the Regent would truly take a fancy to a hostage. Thus, officials high and low still viewed the Seventh Princess of Chu as a hostage, not a bride.

Even the Emperor on the throne seemed to raise an eyebrow, surprised: "Imperial Uncle, are you truly moved by her beauty? I saw her that day as well; she is indeed quite striking."

"However... she is, after all, a hostage. Imperial Uncle, you must think this through."

The Emperor seemed to smile, the corners of his lips curling slightly as he looked at Xie Yunzhou.

Xie Yunzhou suddenly recalled the scent of the woman from that night. The drug had been placed in the imperial wine; without instructions from above, he reckoned that old fool He Yuming would never have dared to offend him directly.

Xie Yunzhou took a deep breath and lowered his gaze: "The Seventh Princess is staying at my residence. It will take some time to know if we are a suitable match."

The Emperor smiled and nodded: "Very well. In that case, let the Seventh Princess remain at the Imperial Uncle's residence."

After the court session, returning to the manor.

"Why did the Prince say that in court!"

Once inside the manor, Luo Yangming hurried to catch up with him, his icy face nearly melting with anxiety.

Xie Yunzhou stopped and glanced at him sideways before saying indifferently: "That is what His Majesty wanted me to say."

"His Majesty?" Luo Yangming was startled and immediately asked: "His Majesty and you are as close as uncle and nephew, why would he think that!"

Xie Yunzhou laughed upon hearing this: "Close as uncle and nephew? Yangming, your temperament is truly unsuited for the officialdom. You had better return to the camp to train the troops."

Luo Yangming stood there, frowning, stubbornly muttering: "This subordinate does not understand!"

Xie Yunzhou was silent for a while before finally opening his mouth, saying in a low voice: "His Majesty is wary of me."

Luo Yangming’s pupils shrank in shock, and he stood frozen. By the time he regained his senses, he realized Xie Yunzhou had already disappeared.

His Majesty... wary of the Prince?

It was not rare for a monarch to be wary of capable subjects, but for it to happen between the Emperor and the Prince was particularly shocking.

The current Emperor was the child of the Prince’s elder brother. The Prince had been raised by his elder brother since childhood and shared a deep bond with him, helping the young child ascend the throne after the death of the former Crown Prince.

The Emperor was only five when he lost his father. He was young and orphaned, unable to sleep at night from fear, and every night it was the Prince who coaxed him to sleep in his arms. They were closer than father and son.

At that time, the Prince was only eleven. The title of "God of War" he earned fifteen years later was forged through blade and spear.

Having helped the young child ascend the throne based on his military merits and having assisted him diligently for years, the Emperor had always shown great respect and love for this Imperial Uncle.

How could he be wary? How could he possibly be wary?

Truly, imperial power corrodes the human heart.

Luo Yangming sighed and walked away, flicking his sleeves.

Looking at Xie Yunzhou, he stood under the corridor for a while, hesitated, and then turned toward a certain courtyard.

That was the guest courtyard assigned to Shen Lingjiang and her servant. He hadn't visited once since returning yesterday.

When he arrived, he was blocked at the door by Ruyi.

Xie Yunzhou: "You dare block me?"

Ruyi was trembling, but she still blocked the doorway, stretching out her arms, refusing to budge.

She pouted, looking as if she were about to cry: "M-my Princess is ill, she... she cannot see anyone!"

Xie Yunzhou: "Ill again?"

Ruyi nodded vigorously.

Xie Yunzhou took another step forward: "I will go in and see. If it is serious, I will call a doctor for her, lest she die in my manor."

Ruyi’s eyes widened, and she immediately blocked him again, saying anxiously: "No, no, no! It is not serious! The Princess just needs to rest!"

Xie Yunzhou narrowed his eyes and muttered to himself: "What is she up to?"

With that, he lifted the person in front of him and tossed her aside, then burst through the door.

He entered and locked the door behind him, leaving Ruyi spinning in circles outside.

"Princess! Princess! Princess, I have failed you... I couldn't stop him..."

The courtyard was of moderate size. Xie Yunzhou bypassed the main hall and the small parlor, heading straight for the bedroom.

Wanting to see what Shen Lingjiang was up to, he didn't knock and pushed the door open directly.

Shen Lingjiang was sitting on the bed in thin, loose undergarments. She held a small round box the size of her palm in her left hand, and her right hand had pulled her pant legs up high.

The moment Xie Yunzhou entered, he saw a pair of thin, fair legs spread out on the bed, and Shen Lingjiang was lowering her head to apply medicine to her inner thighs.

Hearing the commotion, Shen Lingjiang was startled and scrambled to pull the quilt over herself.

She was usually composed; this was the first time Xie Yunzhou had seen her in such a flustered state.

Xie Yunzhou: "...What are you doing?"

Shen Lingjiang took a breath, her face expressionless. After a long while, she said: "Prince! When will you learn to knock before entering?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

Xie Yunzhou felt a rare sense of guilt. He rubbed his nose and gave a light cough: "Cough... You had someone blocking the door, so I thought you were up to some mischief."

Shen Lingjiang sighed: "Prince, I am currently in the Regent's manor, right under your nose. What could I possibly do? Secretly contact my home country?"

chapters.title: Auspicious for Travel
chapters.content:
Xie Yunzhou coughed twice more, said nothing, but walked over at a measured pace, snatched the small round box from Shen Lingjiang’s hand, opened it, and sniffed.

He frowned tightly: "Chafed from riding yesterday?"

Shen Lingjiang nodded.

Xie Yunzhou added: "This medicine is too inferior. It won't heal in ten days or half a month."

Shen Lingjiang nodded and asked: "So, does the Prince have a better solution?"

Xie Yunzhou didn't speak; he just tossed the medicine box in his hand and turned to walk out. About the time it takes to burn a stick of incense, he returned.

He handed over a black porcelain box the size of a palm and said indifferently: "Use this."

Shen Lingjiang opened it, sniffed it carefully, and raised an eyebrow at Xie Yunzhou: "Isn't this a bit of an overkill?"

Xie Yunzhou turned his head away and said: "Just use it. If you really let it drag on for ten days or half a month, you'll ruin my plans."

Shen Lingjiang nodded slowly, studying the ointment while asking: "Does the Prince have other matters?"

Xie Yunzhou: "That old brat Xie Yunqi is feigning illness to stay in Yandu. We must find a way to drive that dog back to Baiyong."

Prince Xin, Xie Yunqi, held the fief of Baiyong in Dazhou.

This man was ambitious and was the biological son of the late Emperor. Staying in the capital and growing closer to court officials was truly inappropriate.

Shen Lingjiang nodded in understanding. She clutched the quilt, silent for a moment, then suddenly smiled: "Is the Prince waiting to watch me apply the medicine?"

Xie Yunzhou: "..."

If he left now, it would look like he was afraid.

Xie Yunzhou turned and sat on a stool by the table. He looked toward Shen Lingjiang, saying nothing, just staring straight at her.

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Shen Lingjiang was so angry she laughed. After a pause, she lowered her head, pulled back the quilt, pulled up her pant legs, and continued applying the medicine.

She was thin, and fortunately, her pants were loose enough to be easily pulled up to her thighs without needing to remove them, which would have been truly improper.

Xie Yunzhou watched without blinking. Not only did he watch, but he also poured himself a cup of tea, nibbling on tea snacks while sipping tea and watching.

Shen Lingjiang’s skin was fair; her face was white, and her body seemed even whiter.

Her two legs were glowing with a pale luster, but they were too thin, scrawny and pitiful to look at.

The insides of her thighs were bruised and red, with some areas even chafed to the point of bleeding, which looked quite alarming.

Truly delicate.

Xie Yunzhou thought to himself while drinking tea.

Shen Lingjiang felt the gaze like needles on her back. She hurriedly finished applying the medicine, pulled down her pant legs, smoothed her clothes, and got off the bed.

The injury on her legs was by no means light, but she walked two steps without showing any abnormality, completely hiding the fact that her inner thighs were bruised and swollen.

Shen Lingjiang walked up to Xie Yunzhou and stared at him: "Prince, are you satisfied?"

Xie Yunzhou took a slow sip of tea, then nodded slowly: "It will do."

The next morning, after Xie Yunzhou returned from court, he changed into casual clothes and sought out Shen Lingjiang again.

He stared at her and asked: "Can you walk?"

Shen Lingjiang raised an eyebrow: "Is the Prince in such a hurry to deal with Prince Xin today?"

Xie Yunzhou nodded: "That old scoundrel has been feigning illness for a month, locked in his manor. I don't know if it's real or fake. Since a brother is ill, it is only natural for a younger brother to visit."

Shen Lingjiang understood his meaning: he wanted to see if Xie Yunqi was truly ill or just pretending.

Shen Lingjiang privately believed it was real.

After all, faking an illness was too easy to expose. If the Emperor sent an imperial physician to diagnose him and found nothing wrong, it would be considered deceiving the Emperor.

Shen Lingjiang nodded slightly and smiled at Xie Yunzhou: "The medicine the Prince gave me is excellent. It has already scabbed over this morning. It doesn't hurt or itch, so it won't hinder travel."

She paused, then added: "May I change my clothes?"

The implication was for him to wait outside.

Xie Yunzhou glanced at her, pouted, and walked out, muttering to himself as he went: "As if I'm happy to look anyway."

Shen Lingjiang heard him and smiled as she watched him leave.

She turned back and changed into a moon-white round-collared robe, with bamboo patterns embroidered in silver thread on the collar and sleeves. She tied her hair neatly with a ribbon and grabbed a black fox-fur cloak from the wooden rack before heading out.

Xie Yunzhou was waiting at the door. He turned his head when he heard the door open and was stunned for a moment.

Shen Lingjiang had delicate features, red lips, and white teeth; she looked exceptionally good in light colors.

Xie Yunzhou stared blankly for a while before looking away: "You look decent enough, but why pair this outfit with a mere strip of cloth?"

Shen Lingjiang raised her eyebrows slightly, instinctively touching the white ribbon tied behind her head, and smiled: "Prince, I am truly poor. I have no hairpins, so I have to make do."

Shen Lingjiang hadn't brought much luggage when she was sent as a hostage to another country. This was likely the most presentable outfit in her wardrobe.

Xie Yunzhou said nothing more, turned his head, and walked forward. After clearing the corridor, he spoke again: "If you can help me settle this matter, I will provide all your future attire."

Shen Lingjiang smiled faintly: "In that case, I dare not be anything but diligent."

The two walked out of the manor side by side, encountering Ruyi sweeping the courtyard on the way.

Ruyi pouted, wanting to follow, but was shooed away by Shen Lingjiang. She returned to the courtyard, pouting unhappily and venting her frustration on the broom.

Walking down the street, the markets of Yandu were very spacious, wide enough for a four-horse carriage to pass, with plenty of room for stalls on either side.

The streets were bustling. Even under the shadow of the imperial city, it was full of life, with snack stalls and toy vendors that dazzled the eyes.

As soon as they left the manor, they saw many people pushing and shoving as they ran forward, all in a great hurry.

Shen Lingjiang asked instinctively: "What is happening?"

Xie Yunzhou didn't know and didn't answer.

However, a young man selling chestnut cakes by the roadside laughed and said: "You two don't know? The Minister of Rites is marrying off his daughter! They say the wedding procession is like a long dragon; the front has reached the bridge gate, and the last of the dowry hasn't even left the manor yet! The procession is at East Street now, and they seem to be tossing out wedding money. Many people have gone to pick it up!"

So that was it.

Shen Lingjiang nodded in understanding, then lowered her eyes to look at the chestnut cakes on the stall.

Square-shaped chestnut cakes, made without any fancy molds, each piece was a milky yellow, emitting a faint, sweet fragrance.

Xie Yunzhou didn't notice her gaze and was about to walk on when Shen Lingjiang tugged on his sleeve.

"Do me the favor of buying me a piece of chestnut cake."

Shen Lingjiang tugged on Xie Yunzhou’s sleeve, looked up, and smiled at him, a smile full of genuine affection.

Well, genuine affection for the chestnut cake.

Xie Yunzhou frowned and glared at her: "Are you a child? Still craving sweets."

Shen Lingjiang continued to smile: "Sir, please be kind."

Out in public, surrounded by commoners, Shen Lingjiang deliberately omitted the title "Prince" and, after a moment's thought, chose the address "Sir."

But for some reason, this word pricked Xie Yunzhou’s ears. He immediately put on an indescribable expression, looking both disgusted and embarrassed.

But in the end, he turned his head away and said irritably: "Fine, fine, fine! Pack one for her!"

chapters.title: Hypochondria
chapters.content:
The man was quite talkative. Not expecting that a single remark would lead to a sale, he immediately took out a fresh piece of oil paper, picked out six chestnut cakes, and handed them to Shen Lingjiang with both hands. "My chestnut cakes are the best in town! They’re mixed with dried osmanthus and honey, sweet but not cloying, leaving a lingering fragrance in your mouth! Do try them; I guarantee you’ll come back for more!"

Shen Lingjiang’s eyes crinkled with a smile. She took the cakes, tasted one, and nodded in praise, "Thank you, they really are delicious!"

With that, she cradled the cakes and walked ahead.

Xie Yunzhou rolled his eyes, fished a small piece of silver from his pocket, slapped it onto the stall, and followed after her.

The man clutched the silver and shouted, "My lord, I can't provide change for such a small piece of silver!"

Xie Yunzhou ignored him and strode away.

"Would you like to share? They really are quite good." Seeing him catch up, Shen Lingjiang held out the cakes toward him, smiling.

Her smile was elegant, and her voice was as clear as the tinkling of jade pendants. Standing amidst the crowd, she looked like a piece of fine jade among common stones, truly a celestial being.

Xie Yunzhou was momentarily dazed and dazzled. He immediately looked away and scolded in a low voice, "What are you smiling at? You’re bundled up like a bear."

Having said that, he strode forward, walking so fast that Shen Lingjiang had to jog to keep up.

Shen Lingjiang stopped chasing. She stopped smiling, frowned as she looked down at the ink-colored cloak draped over her shoulders, glared at Xie Yunzhou’s back, and then took a fierce bite of her chestnut cake, muttering, "So difficult to please."

Afterward, she followed at a leisurely pace, eating her pastry slowly while curiously observing the stalls on both sides, stopping to take a closer look whenever she saw something interesting.

Xie Yunzhou stopped at the street corner, waiting impatiently. When Shen Lingjiang finally approached, he turned and glared at her. "If you go any slower, you might as well go collect Xie Yunqi’s corpse once he dies of his illness."

After the reprimand, he grabbed Shen Lingjiang by the wrist and pulled her along at a brisk pace.

Being dragged by the wrist, the movement was so sudden and rapid that a piece of the chestnut cake in her hand fell off. She cried out in shock, "Xie Yunzhou, I dropped my chestnut cake!"

She had called him by his own name.

It was as if his palm had been scorched by fire; Xie Yunzhou immediately let go. He turned back to glare at Shen Lingjiang, his ears turning a deep crimson as he barked, "Insolent!"

Shen Lingjiang: "..."

Shen Lingjiang studied Xie Yunzhou, suddenly feeling that he resembled a startled, bristling wild cat, fierce on the outside but timid on the inside, lacking his usual domineering and aloof demeanor.

Xie Yunzhou rubbed his nose, coughed twice, and turned his head to walk forward, urging her with ill-concealed impatience, "Walk faster."

Shen Lingjiang shook her head with a smile and followed.

The two arrived before the Prince Xin’s Mansion. The gate was wide and imposing, with stone beasts taller than a man guarding either side, and the coiled dragons on the eaves looked incredibly lifelike.

Guards stood on both sides of the gate. One of them recognized Xie Yunzhou, his eyes widening in shock, especially when he saw him stepping onto the stone stairs.

"Your Highness!"

The two guards bowed to Xie Yunzhou. Xie Yunzhou said expressionlessly, "I heard my Imperial Brother is ill, so I have come to visit."

One of the guards looked troubled and hesitated, "This... our Prince is seriously ill and is declining all visitors."

Xie Yunzhou raised an eyebrow, his expression mocking. "Are you blocking me?"

The guard’s face turned pale. He stood there, caught in a dilemma, and dared not speak again.

Shen Lingjiang tugged at Xie Yunzhou and whispered, "These men are just following orders from above. What good does it do to make things difficult for them?"
